scout.name: Scout
scout.description: The Scout is one of two starter towers obtained upon joining the game for the first time, with the other being the Sniper.

Description: The Scout is one of two starter towers obtained upon joining the game for the first time, with the other being the Sniper.

The Scout is very cheap in comparison to other towers, meaning it can be placed right from the start of the game. However, the Scout has low DPS, even at higher levels, meaning it is not effective later on during the game. In PVP mode, it has far higher DPS than in regular modes, though it is still lower than most other options.
The Scout is considered an early-game tower due to its low cost and low overall damage.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Scout is mainly used as an early-game tower due to its cheap price and great cost efficiency compared to other towers. After the Fallen Shield debut in Fallen mode, the Scout becomes weak against the enemies that spawn, mainly due to its minimal DPS.
After the Fallen Shield debut in Fallen mode, the Scout becomes weak against the enemies that spawn, mainly due to its minimal DPS.

Early on, placing down multiple Level 2 Scouts can be effective due to their cheap hidden detection, decent damage and acceptable firerate. Later on, upgrading them to Level 3 or 4 is advised, as they are more cost efficient than previous levels.
Later on, upgrading them to Level 3 or 4 is advised, as they are more cost efficient than previous levels.

The Scout has cheap hidden detection. Accordingly, the Scout can be used to defend against weaker Hidden enemies, like the Hidden and Molten Demon, while you can work on getting more expensive towers and upgrades. Later on during the game, towers that deal more DPS, such as the Minigunner, are more efficient at dealing with stronger Hidden enemies like Hidden Bosses.
Later on during the game, towers that deal more DPS, such as the Minigunner, are more efficient at dealing with stronger Hidden enemies like Hidden Bosses.

The Scout can be used as a cheap way to distract enemies, like Patient Zero, from using their abilities on superior towers, like the Turret. This is only advised if you have brought the Scout to deal with the early waves. It is not advised to bring the Scout for the sole purpose of feigning abilities. Additionally, if you have other towers that will contribute more to overall DPS, it is advised to maximize the placement limit for these towers before preparing feigning Scouts.

The DJ Booth is useful to increase the Scout's somewhat short range. Due to the cheap placement cost of the Scout, it may be cost efficient to place multiple Scouts around the DJ Booth to use in conjunction with its Drop the Beat ability, on the green track, to generate cash.

Trivia: The Scout's name, appearance and function is loosely based on the Tower Battles' Scout.
When the game was in Alpha, and for a while after BETA release, the Scout's upgrade stats were not displayed on its upgrade description. It was simply referred to as " sans gun ".

The Scout has the second lowest placement cost in the game, only $25 behind the Paintballer. However, the Golden Snowballer is technically the cheapest placement cost in the game, being $67, but it is only available to developers. Additionally, its Level 1 upgrade cost is the second cheapest upgrade in the game, just $25 behind the Paintballer 's Level 1 upgrade cost.

The SCT from the legacy Hidden Wave, the Scout from Pizza Party and the Null Scout from the Null & Void event are based on this tower.
The Scout used to appear alongside the Pyromancer, Commander, Sniper and Minigunner on the "Triumph" screen before the Community Maps Update.
The Scout and the Sniper are the only towers which can be unlocked without any requirements or currency.
The Scout currently appears in the loading screen image alongside the Commander, Engineer, Pyromancer and the DJ Booth.

sniper.name: Sniper
sniper.description: The Sniper is one of the two starter towers obtained upon joining the game for the first time, along with the Scout. It is a long-ranged cliff tower with a slow firerate, possessing high damage per shot.

Description: The Sniper is one of the two starter towers obtained upon joining the game for the first time, along with the Scout. It is a long-ranged cliff tower with a slow firerate, possessing high damage per shot.

Its utility comes from its very long range, allowing the Sniper to target enemies from far away. It deals high damage at a rather slow firerate. Slower enemies are vulnerable to the Sniper for long periods of time due to the Sniper's range, but faster enemies may be able to bypass it. Because the Sniper is a cliff tower, it can detect Flying enemies. The Sniper can also detect hidden enemies at Level 2+ and damage lead enemies at Level 3+. It is immune to all stuns by default.

The Sniper is considered a solid early to mid-game tower, being able to take down many enemy types due to its triple detections, making it useful for Hardcore Mode and other harder gamemodes. Towards late game, the Sniper becomes inefficient against stronger enemies like the Slow Boss and the Fallen Giant due to its insufficient damage output, or fast enemies like the Bolt and the Yeti due to their speed, so it is recommended to get a stronger tower by then.
The Sniper has no placement limit.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Sniper is effective early on during the game due to its cheap cost and long range. Its earlier levels allow it to kill most enemies in one shot for a cheap price. It can also be useful against Hidden enemies, as upgrading it to Level 2 is quite cheap.
Its earlier levels allow it to kill most enemies in one shot for a cheap price.
It can also be useful against Hidden enemies, as upgrading it to Level 2 is quite cheap.
The Sniper should not be relied on too much due to its slow firerate and overall low DPS. The slow firerate can result in you being easily overwhelmed later on in the game by hordes.

The Sniper has lower DPS than other starter towers, but to compensate, it has a relatively long range, so it can keep shooting enemies for a while. You can pair this with the Commander or the Medic so that it will shoot faster.
You can pair this with the Commander or the Medic so that it will shoot faster.
Later on in the game, to maximize damage, you should change the Sniper's targeting to Strongest, or replace them with stronger towers like Ranger.
The DJ Booth can easily expand the range of the Sniper to cover most, if not all, of the map.

The Sniper can be used as a cheap way to deal with Flying enemies that appear early on during the game. It can also damage Lead enemies at Level 3+, making it rather useful against flying and lead combinations like Lead Balloon, although there are better alternatives, like the Ace Pilot or Military Base.

It can also damage Lead enemies at Level 3+, making it rather useful against flying and lead combinations like Lead Balloon, although there are better alternatives, like the Ace Pilot or Military Base.

The Sniper is one of the few towers that can damage all enemies, no matter their immunities, when upgraded to Level 3+. Despite it being able to damage all enemies, it is generally not worth using the Sniper late on during the game due to its low DPS and slow firerate.
Despite it being able to damage all enemies, it is generally not worth using the Sniper late on during the game due to its low DPS and slow firerate.

The Sniper has no placement limit, requiring many placements to be effective, therefore other cliff towers should not be brought due to the limited cliff space available in most maps occupied by the snipers. Towards late-game, the Snipers can be sold to make space for other cliff towers, but this is not recommended unless absolutely necessary since it is rather time consuming and results in a general loss in cash and total dps.

Trivia: When the game was in Alpha, the Sniper's upgrade stats were not displayed on its upgrade description. It was simply referred to as "sans long gun".

Weirdly, the Sniper costs 100 Coins to unlock, according to the store, despite being given for free. This is because prior to the MEGA Update, the Sniper used to cost 100 Coins to purchase from the store.

The Sniper is also the only cliff tower to have no placement limit.
The Sniper is loosely based on the Sniper from Tower Battles.
The Sniper used to appear alongside the Pyromancer, Scout, Commander and Minigunner on the "Triumph" screen before the Community Maps Update.
Formerly, the Sniper used to have the longest range in the entire game not counting any admin-exclusive towers. After the Overhaul Update, this record is given to the Ranger.

paintballer.description: The Paintballer is a starter splash damage tower that can be bought in the store for 100 Coins, but it could also be obtained by a now expired code.

Description: The Paintballer is a starter splash damage tower that can be bought in the store for 100 Coins, but it could also be obtained by a now expired code.

It boasts a faster firerate than other splash towers in exchange for lower damage. Additionally, unlike most other splash towers, its explosion can only damage five enemies with each explosion. This is reduced to four enemies in PVP. Its damage also does not decrease the further the enemy is from the center of the explosion. This means that every enemy hit will always receive the same damage. The Paintballer falls short of other towers in most parts of the game, especially DPS, as its highest DPS is much lower than those of other towers, such as the Shotgunner. This means that it is not that useful later on during the game. It gains hidden detection at Level 1, though unlike most other splash towers, it cannot damage lead enemies.
The Paintballer is mostly regarded as an early game tower due to its extremely cheap placement cost and upgrade prices, but low DPS.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Paintballer's extremely low placement cost allows you to spam loads of them, makes it very useful in the early-game. Its cheap upgrade costs and splash damage can deal with weaker enemies like the Abnormal or Heavy. Even a couple of Level 0 Paintballers can hold themselves very well for the first few waves. Later on, its DPS becomes ineffective against higher health enemies such as the Normal Boss or Elite Abnormal as it is meant to be a splash damage tower. It can however be useful in dealing with summons from summoner enemies like the Necromancer (Modern Enemy) 's Skeletons.

The Paintballer gains Hidden Detection at Level 1 for an extremely low price, making it a nuisance against hiddens relatively early on. However, it cannot fare against hidden enemies with higher health like the Hidden Boss due to its low DPS. You should use towers with high DPS like the Minigunner to counter this obstacle, since they are more efficient.

Unlike other splash damage towers, the Paintballer does not have lead detection, so you will need to use other towers to deal with Lead enemies.

The Paintballer can be used to mislead enemies with stunning abilities such as the Warden and the Executioner, preventing them from stunning important towers like the Turret This is also useful if you have a group of high DPS towers that would most likely be vulnerable to stuns, hindering their DPS capabilities. Though, this tactic is not required for towers that cannot be stunned at all like the Accelerator. Keep in mind that certain enemies with stomp abilities will still be able to stun everything within their radius, neglecting this strategy.

demoman.name: Demoman
demoman.description: The Demoman is a starter splash damage tower that can be bought in the store for 200 Coins. While targeting a specific enemy, it will also affect those around the target, dealing splash damage.

Description: The Demoman is a starter splash damage tower that can be bought in the store for 200 Coins. While targeting a specific enemy, it will also affect those around the target, dealing splash damage.

At Levels 0-2, the Demoman takes one second to aim at an enemy before throwing its explosive grenades. This only affects the damage for the first throw, as it means the Demoman has to wait a second before throwing it. While it is aiming, it will focus on one enemy until it throws its explosive grenade, after which it can target a different one. If the targeted enemy dies, the Demoman will continue targeting it, though its grenade will not land where it died, it will throw it further away, which is generally the area where the enemy would have travelled to if it did not die. The Demoman will also continue to aim at that enemy even if it leaves its range, allowing it to attack outside of its range. After the first throw, while the Demoman still aims, this does not affect its firerate. The explosion caused by the Demoman does not have damage drop-off. The Demoman can also damage Lead enemies.

The Demoman is great for large hordes of non-boss enemies, except for those immune to splash damage. It is relatively weak against major bosses, though it can be useful in tackling the enemies that spawn from some major bosses. The Demoman is considered an early game to mid-game tower, though in late game it can be quite useful for swarm-clearing when multiple are placed down.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Demoman can outshine the Sniper and Soldier as a cheap tower, as its versatility is exceptional.

The main weakness of the Demoman is its slow firerate and projectile. Faster enemies, such as the Bolt, can easily get out of the range of the Demoman. At later Levels, the Demoman has faster projectile and much faster firerate, making it easier to deal with them. You can also use a Commander or DJ Booth to remedy this as they boost firerate and range respectively. Additionally, these enemies may get out of range of the explosion as it takes time for the projectile to leave the Demoman and hit the path.

At Level 0-2, the Demoman has an aim time. While it is aiming, it will focus on one enemy until it throws its grenade. Additionally, it will never stop aiming at that specific enemy. Because of this, it can actually attack that enemy even if it gets out of its range. This also means that it will not stop aiming at it even if it dies, which in some cases may make the grenades land in an area where there are no enemies.

The Demoman can be used to kill Lead enemies.

The Demoman's firerate is lower than the Rocketeer and Mortar, and the Demoman does not have a placement limit. Therefore, it may be more beneficial to use the Demoman over these towers in certain situations. Though to compensate, the Demoman overall has lower DPS, so having no placement limit is a great feature.
Trivia: The Demoman was inspired by Team Fortress 2's RED Demoman. The first and second versions of the Level 3, 4 and 5 Default skin were a direct reference to this as they both wore a black vest with a red shirt underneath. The Level 2 and 3 upgrades are direct references to unlockable weapons for the Demoman. The Level 2 upgrade name is based on the Ullapool Caber, which is similarly based on a Stielhandgranate. The Level 3 upgrade name is based on the Loch-n-Load. The Level 4 upgrade name is based on one of Demoman's item sets, which the set coincidentally contains both weapons above and the Scotch Bonnet, which the Level 4 Demoman 's helmet takes inspiration of. The Fortress skin is directly based on the RED Demoman.

boomerang.name: Boomerang
boomerang.description: The Boomerang is a starter tower bought for 300 Coins. It attacks enemies by throwing a boomerang at them.

Description: The Boomerang is a starter tower bought for 300 Coins. It attacks enemies by throwing a boomerang at them.

The Boomerang will lock onto an enemy within its range and aim for 1 second before throwing out a boomerang. This boomerang will travel in an arc and pierces through multiple enemies until it either runs out of enemies to hit or reaches the maximum number of enemies it can hit, where it returns back to the Boomerang. Regardless of how many enemies the Boomerang hit visually, it will always only damage as many enemies as what its max hits is set to. Although setting the targeting is possible and visually, the Boomerang will target enemies based on it, once thrown it will instantly snap back and throw it at the first enemy. This boomerang takes time to travel to an enemy. It will not throw its boomerang again until it has returned to it, meaning its actual firerate is capped based on how long it takes for the boomerang to return.

At Level 3, it will gain a second boomerang, effectively doubling its damage. This will also not function the same as the first one, as it will target the last enemy the first boomerang will hit. For example, if there are six enemies in a line, the Boomerang will throw the first boomerang at the first enemy in the line and the second boomerang at the fifth enemy. They will begin returning to it once the first boomerang hits the fifth enemy in the line and the second boomerang hits the first enemy in the line.
The Boomerang is primarily an early to mid-game AOE tower which from Level 0 can be used to damage Flying enemies and from Level 3+ Lead enemies. It has a placement limit of 12.
Strategy: This tower is best placed in areas where it can cover the most of the path. Unlike the Executioner, it cannot hit an infinite amount of enemies, meaning positioning it specifically to make it hit as many enemies as possible is not necessary.
Unlike the Executioner, it cannot hit an infinite amount of enemies, meaning positioning it specifically to make it hit as many enemies as possible is not necessary.

This tower can be used against Lead and Flying enemies, but it will struggle against single high-health ones such as the Frost Mage or the Elite Lead. It can however perform well against groups of weaker enemies such as the Balloon. Additionally, while the Boomerang cannot target hidden enemies, it can hit them if the boomerang hits it while travelling to another enemy.

Trivia: The store description of the Boomerang is a reference to the Avatar: The Last Airbender franchise. This part of the description was originally used by the Executioner, though it was moved to this tower once it was released.

The Level 4 upgrade name is a reference to The Lord of the Rings.

slime_trooper.name: Slime Trooper
slime_trooper.description: The Slime Trooper is a starter support tower which fires globs of slime at enemies, slowing them down. It costs 300 Coins to purchase.

Description: The Slime Trooper is a starter support tower which fires globs of slime at enemies, slowing them down. It costs 300 Coins to purchase.

The Slime Trooper will fire a slime projectile at enemies at a decently slow firerate. When hit, they will receive the Slowed attribute, which slows them down and has slime drop from them, slowing them down by 15% at Level 0 and increasing at higher levels, reaching 22.5% at Level 4. Boss enemies are immune to any kind of slowdown applied by Slime Trooper. At Level 4, it will be able to hit multiple enemies at once as its slime projectiles now explode on impact and dealing Splash Damage, though as it does not deal explosion damage some effects from that like Defense bypass, damage drop off or default lead detection are not present.

The Slime Trooper's ability to slow down enemies is very similar to Toxic Gunner, though they are both different effects and the latter has more potent slowdown and additional effects on top of slow. Slime Trooper is able to detect Hidden and Flying enemies, making it useful across various gamemodes. As Slime Trooper cannot damage Lead enemies, it will require other towers to attack the them, such as Sniper or Shotgunner.

The Slime Trooper is considered an early-game tower. It does great as starting defense, but towards late game, its damage is insufficient to deal with stronger enemies, therefore taking on a support role towards late game. The Slime Trooper is a support tower, and its main purpose is to slow down enemies, so it cannot defend against enemies by itself without the help of other towers, so it is best paired with high damage towers like Ranger or Turret.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Slime Trooper is a decent way to stall enemies, giving high damage towers like Ranger and Rocketeer more time to damage these enemies. As its slowdown effect is unique, it can be used alongside other towers like the Freezer, Tesla or Toxic Gunner without issue, allowing the effects to stack. Using these together with Slime Trooper can cause enemies to crawl at incredibly slow speeds, allowing more time for other towers to attack the enemies. However, this is not a reliable strategy unless a lot of high damage towers are brought. Boss enemies will not receive the Slowed attribute, making them immune to the slowdown. Firework Technician is also a good tower to pair with Slime Trooper as doing so grants Slime Trooper the ability to hit Lead enemies. The Medic can also be used to give it lead detection. Thanks to it being able to hit more enemies at Level 4, it can also generate multiple fireworks at once.

The Slime Trooper's targeting can be set to Random at Level 4 to maximize the splash damage and slowdown effect across a large group of enemies. The Slime Trooper has a slow firerate, so this may not be very effective against swift enemies like Molten Mech or Yeti. This can be somewhat solved by pairing it up with cooldown decreasing towers like Commander or Medic.

The Slime Trooper possesses a rather small range, and thus careful placements is required to maximize this tower's effectiveness. At later levels, its range becomes much larger, thus being more forgiving in terms of placements. Despite not having a placement limit, it is best to only put a few well-placed Slime Troopers, mostly at choke points or near the front of the map to apply the effect on as many enemies as possible.

It is generally recommended not to focus on Slime Trooper solely for DPS, mainly due to its rather slow firerate, projectile travel time and middling damage output. It is better used as starting defense or stalling.

At Level 4, the Slime Trooper's Splash Damage has a small explosion radius, but has no limit to how many enemies can be hit, so Slime Trooper excels against dense hordes of slow-moving enemies rather than spread out groups of fast-moving enemies. An example of this is Fallen mode's Wave 35, where the huge crowds of enemies tightly squeezed together are perfect for the Slime Trooper to maximize its damage output and slowdown effect, although other towers are needed to help as the Slime Trooper cannot deal with such late-game enemy hordes alone.

soldier.name: Soldier
soldier.description: The Soldier is a starter ground tower that fires in bursts. It can be bought for 350 Coins in the store.

Description: The Soldier is a starter ground tower that fires in bursts. It can be bought for 350 Coins in the store.

The Soldier fires in bursts, with a short delay between each burst. It is a fairly cheap tower, making it recommended for use in earlier waves. It gains hidden detection at Level 2 and flying detection at Level 4 (Level 0 for PVP), so it is an effective counter against Hidden and Flying enemies.
The Soldier is considered an early to mid-game tower. Later on during the game, its effectiveness dwindles against high health enemies, being outclassed by other towers with higher DPS.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Soldier is an effective early-game tower at Level 2, having high DPS for a cheap price. By mid-game, you should have multiple Level 3–4 Soldiers, as they can effectively kill enemies that appear there, such as the Dark Necromancer or Slow Boss. However, it loses value as the waves progress due to its DPS being too low to deal with high health enemies that appear later on during the game. It should not be relied on late-game if you have better towers and can be replaced by towers like the Minigunner or Ranger.

freezer.description: The Freezer is a ground tower that fires an ice beam and applies chill and slow down enemies, freezing at later levels. It can be bought in the store for 650 Coins.

Description: The Freezer is a ground tower that fires an ice beam and applies chill and slow down enemies, freezing at later levels. It can be bought in the store for 650 Coins.

The Freezer targets a single enemy and fires a Frost Ray, chilling it and slowing it down. The chillness slowness effect stacks with each hit multiple times. This effect also deals damage over time, chipping away the health of enemies affected by it. Starting from Level 2, it can freeze enemies. When the chillness slowness effect is higher than the max slowdown, the enemy will be frozen, which generally—when targeting a single enemy, takes four or five shots. Larger enemies will be frozen for a shorter amount of time than average sized enemies. Enemies with Freeze Immunity also cannot be frozen, slowed down or have their defense dropped by the Freezer.

At Level 3+, the Freezer begins firing in bursts and gains the ability to drop defense by 10% every tick. It can only decrease an enemy's defense by 33%. For example, if an enemy has 50% defense, it will be decreased by 16%. And at Level 4, the Freezer gains the ability to throw a Frost Grenade which freezes enemies within an explosion radius.

The Freezer does well as an all-rounder support tower. Due to its generally low price and decent DPS, it can be a solid choice for early-game defense to mid-game with very good cost efficiency. Towards late game, the Freezer is useful for stalling, defense melting and dealing additional DPS through its damage over time, though its DPS alone is negligible in later waves.
The Freezer has lead detection from Level 0 and hidden detection from level 2 along with no placement limit.
Ability: Throws a frost grenade that freezes up to five enemies for 2 seconds in an explosion radius of 6.
Throws a frost grenade that freezes up to five enemies for 6 seconds in an explosion radius of 6.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Freezer is an excellent choice to deal with early waves, especially when multiple are placed down, due to its cost efficiency and low price. Other towers should be used against higher health enemies like the Fallen Giant. Later on, it does not have enough DPS to handle other enemies, due to their much higher health, but can still be used for stall.

The Freezer can be used to deal with lead and hidden enemies early on, which can be very useful in Hardcore Mode. The Freezer plays a very similar role in early-game defense to Golden Scout, making Freezer a viable alternative to it.

The Freezer can be very effective at slowing down enemies, especially at Level 3+, as its burst count allows it to freeze an enemy in a single burst. It can be very effective at slowing down fast average-sized enemies, like the Fallen Rusher or Bolt. It is much less effective against bigger enemies like the Fallen Giant, as freeze time is reduced on larger enemies. It also cannot freeze or slowdown freeze immune enemies. While it cannot freeze Bosses as they are immune to freeze by default, they are not immune to the chillness slowdown effect unless they have the Freeze Immunity. However, Bosses are slowed down by much less than regular enemies.

The Freezer's defense dropping ability can be useful for decreasing an enemy's defense, allowing your towers to deal more damage to it. However, do note that as the defense dropping happens when an enemy is frozen or slowed down. Because of this, freeze immune enemies cannot have their defense dropped. The defense drop can stack with other towers, such as the Pyromancer, Electroshocker, Toxic Gunner or Jester, allowing you to remove all of an enemy's defense. Do note that only a burn defense dropping tower and a poison defense dropping tower, like the Pyromancer or Toxic Gunner are required to do this. The Freezer can still be used to speed up the process. However, the Freezer's defense drop does not stack with other freeze defense dropping sources, such as the Frost Blaster 's and Cryomancer 's defense drop.

While it does freeze enemies for a longer amount of time, it is not recommended to use it on singular enemies as it has a hefty 15 second cooldown. This can be somewhat mitigated by having multiple Level 4 Freezers. This ability should not be used on enemies with Freeze Immunity, as it will do nothing on them, wasting the ability.

This froze all enemies within a 10 stud radius for 6 seconds (except major bosses and those immune to the Ice Drop). It used to cost $250 and had a 75 second cooldown. This ability was unusable against enemies under a roof since the drop would never collide with them. This did not apply to Crystal Cave as that roof was non-collidable. The Freezer's Ice Drop was able to freeze the Gold Titan and Molten Boss prior to the 15th of August 2019.

Prior to the MEGA Update, the Freezer fired in bursts, similar to the Soldier, except that it targeted different enemies with every shot within a burst. If there was only one enemy in range of the Freezer, then it would target that enemy only once. However, if an enemy had Basic Freeze Immunity, then the Freezer could target those enemy multiple times. This burst functionality would later be re-added in the Krampus' Revenge Update, though it would target an enemy based on its targeting.

Prior to the Overhaul Update, the Freezer fired an explosive ice projectile which could freeze multiple enemies. After the 24th of December 2019, the Freezer was the only explosive tower to have direct damage. This meant that it could deal damage to a targeted enemy that had explosive immunity (like the Golden) but could not deal damage to other enemies with explosive immunity if they were not the intended target. This meant that the total damage was effectively doubled for the targeted enemy, if they were caught in the projectile explosion.

This tower may be loosely based on the Ice Monkey from Bloons Tower Defense as well as the Cryo-Gunner from Tower Battles.
The original Level 1 upgrade name is a reference to R2DA's Frost Knuckles.

Prior to the 5th of May 2023, the IcyTea skin decreased the Freezer's placement footprint. It was the only skin that could decrease the tower's placement footprint. It was also one of the only skins in the game to change a tower in any other way than its appearance at the time, with the other being XR500 Turret.

When the third act of the Lunar Overture Event released, the Freezer, alongside all other freezing towers, were able to permanently stop enemies from moving, making them ridiculously strong. This, however, was fixed few hours later.

assassin.name: Assassin
assassin.description: The Assassin is an intermediate melee ground tower that can be purchased from the store for 800 Coins.

Description: The Assassin is an intermediate melee ground tower that can be purchased from the store for 800 Coins.

The Assassin will slash at enemies within range with its knife, dealing high single-target damage. At Level 2+, it gains the Whirlwind Slash, turning its every third hit into a whirlwind that pierces through every enemy caught in it. The whirlwind replaces the main attack, dealing the main attack's damage in its own whirlwind range. At Level 4, it gains an additional ability, Fan of Knives, where it will throw out three knives which travel beyond the tower's range in a fan shape at enemies every time a meter of 500 total damage is hit, being able to pierce through three enemies per knife.

Both the main attack and Whirlwind Slash can be used to increase the damage threshold, but not the Fan of Knives. If the damage dealt exceeds the threshold, any excess damage will be carried over to the next counter. For example, if the Assassin deals 60 damage and has a threshold of 460, it will start throwing knives after dealing 520 damage. The additional 20 damage will carry over to the next throw, meaning the counter seen on the tower will start at 20/500.
The Assassin has hidden and lead detection from Level 2. It has no placement limit.
Strategy: The Assassin can be an effective early-game tower, due to its cheap cost, decent AoE and DPS. The Assassin can hit lead and hidden enemies quite early on, making it excellent for gamemodes where such enemy types appear quite early, like the Hardcore mode. At the beginning, it is recommended to place down two Level 0 Assassins, which should be upgraded to Level 2 once the cash is available. Later on, it is recommended to fully upgrade Assassins, as lower levels will struggle to handle higher health enemies like the Molten Golem or Fallen Giant. The Assassin can be used to quickly clear earlier waves and essentially speedrun early game, especially with its Whirlwind Slash which allows it to attack multiple enemies at once.

The Assassin can be used to quickly clear earlier waves and essentially speedrun early game, especially with its Whirlwind Slash which allows it to attack multiple enemies at once.

While it can become ineffective during late-game, It can shred or decrease hordes of lower-health enemies like Hazmat or Breaker4, allowing other towers to target the stronger enemies on the lane. The Assassin is especially useful in taking out weaker hordes of lead enemies as many other towers cannot attack this enemy type, allowing them to focus on the enemies they can damage.

Due to the Assassin's low range, it is quite important to maximize how much path it can cover. Poor placement will lead to it performing poorly. Ideal spots for it are small bends, like the multiple u-turns on U-Turn or the u-turn at the beginning of Simplicity. Other decent options are spots which enemies cross over multiple times, such as the center of Crossroads or one of two loops of Northern Lights.

By late-game, the Assassin will be unable to fight off the far stronger enemies. It is recommended to invest in far better towers by then. Assassin can still be used to clear crowds, especially when many are placed down.

The Assassin benefits greatly from the Firerate Buff and Damage Buff. The Firerate Buff makes it attack faster, reaching its three hit and 500 damage thresholds quicker and increasing its DPS. The Damage Buff not only boosts the damage from the main attack, but also the damage of the whirlwind and the knife throw, boosting the DPS of all of its three attacks. The Range Buff is not that effective on the Assassin, as it only boosts its main attack range. The Whirlwind Slash and Fan of Knives abilities will not have their range boosted by it.

The Assassin synergises well with the Firework Technician as it has AOE attacks that can launch a high amount of fireworks from hitting multiple enemies at once. Do note that the Assassin only starts performing AOE attacks from Level 2 onward with its Whirlwind Slash. This means that using the Firework Technician to boost a Level 0-2 Assassin is not as effective since those levels only use basic, single-target attacks.

The Assassin can indirectly hit Flying enemies with its Whirlwind Slash and Fan Of Knives if another detectable enemy is within attacking range. This means that Assassin is technically able to damage all three enemy types, though it is not recommended to rely on this for Flying enemies.

Trivia: The Assassin is the second left-handed tower in the game, with the first being the Harvester. All other towers are either right handed or use both of their hands from Level 0.

In the official trailer for the Assassin before its release, it was misspelled as Assasin due to an oversight.

The Assassin's Level 4 upgrade name is a reference to a member of the balancing team named Tom Da Ninja. The acronym for " Death Arms " is DA, so the upgrade name Death Arms Ninja also spells out DA Ninja, as in Tom Da Ninja.

militant.description: The Militant, formerly known as John, is an intermediate tower that costs 800 Coins to buy from the store, but can also be obtained by purchasing the Starter Bundle. It could also be obtained by a now expired code.

Description: The Militant, formerly known as John, is an intermediate tower that costs 800 Coins to buy from the store, but can also be obtained by purchasing the Starter Bundle. It could also be obtained by a now expired code.

The Militant begins with low damage but it is supported by a fast firerate. It has long range, allowing it to cover large amounts of the track. Through upgrades its DPS, firerate, range increase greatly, but these upgrades are costly.
The Militant is considered an early to mid-game tower.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Militant's high DPS and low cost make it very viable to use early on during the game. It can also be very useful mid-game and in some weaker modes, late-game. Early on, you can place multiple Level 1 Militants, due to their high DPS, high range, flying detection and hidden detection. Later on during the game, they should be upgraded to Level 3 or 4. Later on during the game, the Commander can be very useful at increasing its DPS, making it quite useful late-game.
Early on, you can place multiple Level 1 Militants, due to their high DPS, high range, flying detection and hidden detection. Later on during the game, they should be upgraded to Level 3 or 4.

Later on during the game, the Commander can be very useful at increasing its DPS, making it quite useful late-game.
The Militant can be quite effective against hidden enemies like the Hidden Boss due to its cheap Hidden detection and decent DPS.

Because the Militant gains flying detection at Level 1, it can be used in Hardcore to kill early-game Balloons or, if enough are placed down, deal with Flying enemies that appear in mid to late-game waves of Fallen and Pizza Party modes. You will need multiple Level 3-4 Militants to deal with the late-game Fallen and Pizza Party enemies due to their high health.

Trivia: When John was first added to the game, its upgrade stats were not displayed on its upgrade description. It was simply referred to as "swager21". It was the only tower that did not include the word "sans" in its upgrade description at the time of its release.
It was the only tower that did not include the word "sans" in its upgrade description at the time of its release.
This tower used to be redeemable with the now expired code: J0HNRBX.

The Militant (when it was originally called John) had an ability called Gorilla Sounds which increased the damage of most towers within its range by 30%. This lasted 10 seconds and had a 30 second cooldown. During Hardcore Testing BETA, this ability was renamed to Enraging Shout. This ability could not increase the damage of the following towers: Any projectile-based towers: the Mortar, Rocketeer, Demoman, Freezer (splash damage only; its direct, non-explosive, damage can be increased), Paintballer and Holiday Archer. The Ace Pilot bombs, Commando missiles or Pursuit missiles, as they all count as projectiles. The Shredder when its Knife Throw ability was activated, as the knives it threw counted as a projectile. The Pyromancer 's burn damage or the Swarmer 's bee damage. The Pyromancer 's normal damage could still be increased. The Enforcer. All units.

The now removed Enraging Shout ability would play various sound effects, with some skins having their own specific sound effects. The regular Enraging Shout sound was voiced by YouTuber JOHN ROBLOX. There were four lines: " Oh you think you're hard, you think you're hard ya dumb old zombies, shred em, shred em, shred em, shred! " " Yeah! Yeah! Yeah! " with a scream at the end. Sounds resembling that of a gorilla, specifically one going " oo-oo-oo " repeatedly. " Yeah, get em, get em, get em, yeah, yeah, get em! " The Pumpkin skin for Militant had two sound effects, both of which are laughs. The Ace Pilot skin for Militant had one sound effect that was only used during Hardcore Testing, prior to that it did not play anything. The one line was: " kakugo surun yo " In English, it translates to "Ya better be prepared!". This is a reference to JOHN ROBLOX's video, zerotwo but in roblox, although the actual sound effect comes from the anime Macross Delta.

shotgunner.name: Shotgunner
shotgunner.description: The Shotgunner, formerly known as the Enforcer, is an intermediate ground tower that wields a powerful pump shotgun to attack enemies with. It costs 850 Coins to buy from the store.

Description: The Shotgunner, formerly known as the Enforcer, is an intermediate ground tower that wields a powerful pump shotgun to attack enemies with. It costs 850 Coins to buy from the store.

The Shotgunner shoots multiple bullets at once through Scatter Shot. Damage is split among 8 bullets per firerate (so the base damage is 2x8), and these bullets are spread within a small cone and can pierce through enemies. The same enemy can be hit with multiple bullets, increasing the damage inflicted. On all levels, three enemies can be damaged by the same bullet. The first two enemies will be dealt full damage, while the last will only be dealt 50% of the damage. The closer an enemy is to the Shotgunner, the more likely they are to be damaged by the bullets.

The Shotgunner is considered a mid to late-game, as its medium cost can be utilized in the mid-game, while its later upgrades and mediocre range, but high DPS can suffice in the late game. It is excellent against huge swarms of enemies as it allows Shotgunner to maximise its high DPS.
The Shotgunner has a placement limit of nine per player. This is removed in PVP mode.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Shotgunner is best placed in a straight line, as enemies traveling away from the Shotgunner will be affected by all the bullets. It is also recommended to set the Shotgunner's targeting to Farthest so that it hits as many enemies as possible.
It is also recommended to set the Shotgunner's targeting to Farthest so that it hits as many enemies as possible.

Multiple Level 0–2 Shotgunners are very cost-efficient and effective at killing enemies, even fast ones like the Speedy or Quick, although it is quite expensive. Towards late-game, multiple Level 3 and 4 Shotgunners can be used to wipe out hordes of enemies, such as the Fallen Giant or Molten Titan.
Towards late-game, multiple Level 3 and 4 Shotgunners can be used to wipe out hordes of enemies, such as the Fallen Giant or Molten Titan.

Be aware that the Shotgunner has a quite mediocre range. DJ Booth or Ranger can be used to increase the range of Shotgunner, but the range increase is minimal at best. However, the DJ Booth can still be useful to reduce the price of the Shotgunner's upgrades or to boost its damage. The Tesla complements the Shotgunner quite well as the Electroshocker can restrict enemy movement significantly, so the Shotgunner can hit more targets with each shot. The Freezer can help to freeze enemies, but it cannot freeze multiple enemies without its Frost Grenade ability. Meanwhile, the Sledger and Frost Blaster can freeze multiple enemies at once.

The Shotgunner has a smaller placement footprint than most towers, making it take up far less space.
The Shotgunner fires multiple bullets at once, making it quite effective against Tank enemies.

While the Shotgunner does have high DPS for its cost, its overall damage output is mitigated due to its small range. This makes Shotgunner better used as a frontline defense to maximize damage output. Shotgunner is most effective on maps with small loops like Simplicity and Midnight Issue.

The Shotgunner's bullets can only pierce through a limited number of enemies, with the first two enemies being dealt full damage, and the last enemy being dealt only half of the damage. On all levels, it can pierce through two enemies, so each bullet can hit three enemies. This makes Shotgunner a good choice against crowds of high-health enemies where Splash Damage towers normally struggle.

Shotgunner is a very effective tower for killing Flying enemies, as it gets flying detection at Level 2+ and has high dps. Before Level 2+, Shotgunner can still accidentally hit flying enemies within range of the enemy it is targeting.

Trivia: The Shotgunner (when it was called the Enforcer) was inspired by the Enforcer from the Risk of Rain series.

Before the Overhaul Update, the Shotgunner (known as the Enforcer back then) had the appearance of a police officer. It also had an ability that spawned a SWAT Van with 600 health and a 45 second cooldown. This ability was voiced by YouTuber JOHN ROBLOX. There were three lines: " Strike force moving out. hunter.description: The Hunter is an intermediate tower that can be purchased from the store for 1,000 Coins. It could have also been obtained from a now expired code.

Description: The Hunter is an intermediate tower that can be purchased from the store for 1,000 Coins. It could have also been obtained from a now expired code.

The Hunter has a decently long range and deals a high amount of damage, however has a rather slow firerate. Uniquely, it requires time to aim before it can start attacking. It can attack Flying enemies at Level 0, and gains hidden detection at Level 3, In PVP mode, the hidden detection is unlocked at Level 1 instead. Therefore, the Hunter is a fairly good mid-late game DPS tower, being a good and simpler Ranger alternative for newer players.

The Hunter deals high damage at later levels, making it a consistently good tower across all modes, even Frost and Hardcore modes. The Hunter excels at mid-late game DPS, especially good against slow, tanky enemies because of the slow reload and high damage bullet. When concentrated on one spot, multiple Hunters can take down bosses with ease and aid other DPS anchors in taking down later bosses.
The Hunter has a placement limit of ten per player.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Hunter is a decent choice for mid to late-game due to its high DPS. As it has flying detection from Level 0, it can be an effective counter against Flying enemies like the Fallen Angel or Crying Angel. The Hunter can also be used against Hidden enemies, though due to it only getting hidden detection at Level 3 it is quite an expensive choice for this.
As it has flying detection from Level 0, it can be an effective counter against Flying enemies like the Fallen Angel or Crying Angel.
The Hunter can also be used against Hidden enemies, though due to it only getting hidden detection at Level 3 it is quite an expensive choice for this.
You might want to use the Commander to decrease the Hunter's slow firerate.

It is generally advised to concentrate multiple Hunters on one spot, preferably at loops and bends. This makes it much easier for multiple hunters to receive buffs from other support towers such as DJ Booth or Ace Pilot.

The Hunter is an excellent DPS tower, but it is still advised to bring at least one other DPS tower, especially in much tougher gamemodes such as Fallen, where tanky enemies appear often and overwhelm Hunters easily.
Trivia: The original name for the Hunter was going to be called Clout God and it had a different design. The name and design were changed as some people felt it was too similar to the Tweeter from Tower Battles. The first version of the Blue skin for the Hunter looks similar to the original design.

Description: The Pyromancer is an intermediate tower that costs 1,250 Coins to buy from the store. It is capable of dealing burn damage to enemies, damaging them over time even when not directly targeted. At higher levels, it can also melt defense by up to 50% of the listed value. For example, an enemy with 50% defense will have its defense decreased to 25%.

If an enemy is set alight, the flames will be applied to the enemy until the burn time runs out. There are two types of damage the Pyromancer can apply. The first is Normal Damage which is applied every 0.258 when the enemy is colliding with the Pyromancer's flame. This flame can initially only hit one enemy, though it upgrades it increases to five. This can pierce through multiple enemies. The second is Burn Damage which is applied for every second an enemy is set alight. Both damage types can damage Lead enemies. The Pyromancer can also detect Hidden enemies at Level 1+. The Pyromancer will attack any enemy, even if the enemy is on fire, as long as it can detect it, though it will prioritize enemies that are not on fire.

The Pyromancer is best combined with other towers since it deals little damage by itself but can deal area of effect. Some enemies are immune to burn, like the Molten. This does not mean the Pyromancer cannot attack them; it only means that it cannot light them on fire.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Pyromancer is considered an all-round tower, due to it being useful at every point of the match. It can be used to easily deal with weak enemy hordes like the Normal, Heavy or Quick and at higher Levels, it can even take out high health enemies like the Normal Boss and Elite Abnormal.
It can be used to easily deal with weak enemy hordes like the Normal, Heavy or Quick and at higher Levels, it can even take out high health enemies like the Normal Boss and Elite Abnormal.

The Pyromancer will set every enemy in its range on fire. In what order the Pyromancer will choose its target is based on its targeting. If there is only one detectable enemy in the Pyromancer's range, then it will always target that enemy. This also occurs if all current enemies in the Pyromancer's range is set on fire.

The Pyromancer can also be used to melt an enemy's Defense by half. The Pyromancer can be used alongside the Freezer / Frost Blaster, the Electroshocker and the Toxic Gunner / Jester to further melt the enemy's Defense, though it cannot be used alongside its golden variant, the Golden Pyromancer or other burn defense melting sources. As such, with these towers, an enemy's Defense can be removed entirely. Do note that only the Toxic Gunner or Jester is required to remove defense entirely, though other defense melting towers can be used to speed up the process. This can be useful since it can harshly decrease high Defense enemies like the Vindicator, Reaver, or Slow King.

Due to the Pyromancer's low range, the DJ Booth is recommended to increase this tower's range.
The Pyromancer is best placed near the beginning of the path. This lets it kill weaker enemies and decrease the defense of enemies before they reach your other towers.
The Pyromancer will not be able to set enemies on fire when placed on high grounds, like those on The Heights.

Since the Pyromancer's burn damage does not stack if you have multiple Pyromancers, you should generally only place down one Pyromancer instead of multiple. The Pyromancer's burn damage also does not stack with burn damage dealt by other towers, like the Archer 's flame arrows. You can also spread out multiple Pyromancer's along the path; this will make it so that enemies remain set alight continuously as they walk towards the exit.

Trivia: When the game was in Alpha, and for a while after BETA release, the Pyromancer's upgrade stats were not displayed on its upgrade description. It was simply referred to as " sans flamey gun ".

Prior to the Overhaul Update, there was a bug where any Range Buff applied to the Pyromancer (including Platinum and Golden skins) did not affect enemies in their extra range, only affecting them in their initial range.
The Pyromancer was inspired by the Pyro from Team Fortress 2. The Pyromancer was originally based on the Flamethrower from Tower Battles.

Prior to the Overhaul Update, this tower used to slow down enemies. After the Overhaul Update, the Pyromancer sped up enemies that were on fire, though this has been removed.

In the Frost Invasion Event, the Pyromancer dealt twice as much damage to enemies that spawned there.
The Pyromancer used to appear alongside the Scout, Commander, Sniper and Minigunner on the "Triumph" screen before the Community Maps Update.
The Pyromancer has one of the oldest firing sounds in the game, having kept it since 2020.
Despite having the "-mancer" suffix, the Pyromancer is not a mage.
The Pyromancer in the game has been shown and said to be a great cook multiple times.

tooltips: A close range tower that sprays fire, melts defense, and burns enemies to deal damage over time.
Capable of detecting hidden and lead enemies.

The Pyromancer is an intermediate tower that costs 1,250 Coins to buy from the store. It is capable of dealing burn damage to enemies, damaging them over time even when not directly targeted. At higher levels, it can also melt defense by up to 50% of the listed value. For example, an enemy with 50% defense will have its defense decreased to 25%.

ace_pilot.name: Ace Pilot
ace_pilot.description: The Ace Pilot is an intermediate tower that can be bought for 1,500 Coins. Unlike other ground towers, the attacking unit of the Ace Pilot, the plane, is an air unit.

Description: The Ace Pilot is an intermediate tower that can be bought for 1,500 Coins. Unlike other ground towers, the attacking unit of the Ace Pilot, the plane, is an air unit.

The Ace Pilot will circle around the runway. At Level 2+, this can be changed to a figure eight. With its Toggle Reverse ability, it is possible to reverse its flight path. The Ace Pilot is armed with a pair of machine guns on each wing at the base and will shoot any enemy within its patrol radius. At Levels 2–5, the aircraft will periodically drop a bomb directly where the targeted enemy was last, exploding and damaging any enemies caught in the explosion. The explosion is separated into two spheres. Enemies in the inner sphere will be dealt 100% of the stated damage, while damage in the outer sphere decreases linearly by distance from the edge of the inner sphere to the edge of the outer sphere. Since its bombs deal splash damage, they ignore defense, dealing full damage to the enemies with defense. These bombs can also damage Lead enemies. Due to it being an air-based tower, it is immune to stuns, and because it is not a humanoid tower, it is also immune to debuffs from enemies added before v1.9.0. Additionally, because it is an air-based tower, it can detect Flying enemies.

At Level 4, the Ace Pilot will also grant nearby towers hidden detection with its Hidden Assist, giving towers without hidden detection, like the Ranger, the ability to detect Hidden enemies. Its machine guns are then replaced by a single autocannon, granting it higher damage and firerate. The Ace Pilot boasts a high DPS, but its limiting range and inconsistent circling cripple its full potential. Therefore, in most situations, it does not operate at the highest DPS most of the time.
The Ace Pilot has a placement limit of eight per player.
Ability: Flies the opposite direction.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: Place this tower where it can be used to its full potential. This primarily involves placing it at turns. Placing it on a straight path is not recommended, as it will not shoot as often. As the Ace Pilot flies clockwise, placing it so it covers a counterclockwise path turn will mean it has a greater chance of attacking an enemy. The first roundabout on Wrecked Battlefield is a good example of this. You can also place it on a clockwise path and use the Toggle Reverse ability to make it fly counterclockwise, having the same effect.

Try not to focus solely on Ace Pilots. This is because faster enemies may walk right past the Ace Pilot without being damaged. If you want reliable defense, then a Minigunner or Cowboy could be a more reliable option.

The Commander cannot decrease the firerate of the bombs. However, it can decrease the firerate of the guns.

Unlike the Pursuit, the Ace Pilot does not stop to hover over an area whenever an enemy enters its range. This means that the Ace Pilot is unlikely to be attacking all the time, reducing the effectiveness of the tower.

In Hardcore mode, the Ace Pilot can be used as an effective way to deal with flying, lead and enemies with defense that appear early on during the game, such as the Lead, Hefty and Balloon.

The bombs that the Ace Pilot drops are a good way to clear out hordes of weaker enemies, like the Abnormal or Slow, while also dealing additional damage to higher health enemies, like the Abnormal Boss. The Ace Pilot's bombs completely ignore defense, dealing full damage to enemies with defense. Because of this, it can be useful against hordes of enemies with defense that appear early on during the game, like Heavies, Abnormal Bosses or Hefties. While the bomb is aimed directly at the target, it may miss the enemy as it takes a little while for the bomb to land. At Level 5, the missile has a faster projectile speed, so is less likely to miss the enemy's intended target.

medic.name: Medic
medic.description: The Medic is an intermediate support tower that provides various buffs to other towers and replenishes base health after it has been lost. It can be unlocked from the store for 2,000 Coins.

Description: The Medic is an intermediate support tower that provides various buffs to other towers and replenishes base health after it has been lost. It can be unlocked from the store for 2,000 Coins.

The Medic heals base health by a specified amount each wave with Take your Vitamins. The amount of health healed increases with the level of the Medic and the amount of Medics placed down. It also has the ability to overheal, increasing base health to value higher than its maximum. If there are multiple Medics, the health regeneration and overheal stacks with each Medic. Similarly, these effects stack with other sources of such effects, like Skills.

The Medic holds a medi gun, which it can use to apply a shield to towers. Whenever shielded, the tower will have a shield modifier on them. This shield provides a passive 15% Firerate Buff and an immunity to stuns. It does not grant an immunity to debuffs or freeze. If the tower is stunned, its shield will be broken instead, reappearing shortly after. At Level 0, it can only shield one tower, but this is increased up to five at Level 5. It cannot shield other Medics or any tower currently shielded by another Medic. There is a 0.5 second cooldown before another tower can be selected or deselected.

At Level 3, it gets the Ubercharge ability. This provides all towers shielded by the Medic with a Damage Buff, Stun Immunity and Freeze Immunity for a brief period of time. While it may look like this is tied to the shield, this is not actually the case. The Damage Buff will remain on the tower, even if its shield is gone. Unassigning a tower with Medic will however remove the buffs from it. While this ability is active, the Medic itself gains the Freeze Immunity.
The Medic has a placement limit of 4.
Ability: Assigned towers gain a Damage Buff, Stun and Freeze Immunity.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Medic has the ability to permanently grant a Firerate Buff and temporarily grant a Damage Buff to towers, making it very useful as a support tower. However, unlike other towers like the Commander, DJ Booth or even the Mercenary Base, it is not able to apply it to every tower in range, it can only apply it to a few of them. Because of this, players may need to either place down multiple of them to cover most or all of their towers, or only target the most important of their towers. Due to its limited tower selection, towers with naturally low placement limits like the Turret or Gatling Gun are a great pick when using the Medic, as their low placement limits mean few Medics are needed to boost them all. The Medic can give towers a shield, which stops them from being stunned once. This does not stop either debuffs or being frozen. These towers are still affected by these effects, but they will not lose their shield from them. When its shield is broken, the targeted tower not only loses its immunity to stuns, but also the Firerate Buff provided by the Medic. It does not however, lose any of its Ubercharge buffs. farm.name: Farm
farm.description: The Farm is an intermediate cash-generating tower that can be purchased from the store for 2,000 Coins.

Description: The Farm is an intermediate cash-generating tower that can be purchased from the store for 2,000 Coins.
The Farm generates cash for the player at the beginning of each wave, instantly giving the player a cash bonus. It does not do anything during the wave itself, and is solely a source of bonus income.

The Farm cannot damage by normal means. The only way to deal damage is by placing the Farm in the range of a Harvester, which will make the Farm create thorns while the Harvester 's Thorns ability is being used. Thorns generated by a Farm have their damage, duration and range statistics halved, though their power (except the range) increases with Levels, becoming same strength as the Harvester at Level 5. Tick and slowdown are seemingly unaffected by this and are the same as the Harvester.

It can also be strategically used to make more money for the respective player, allowing them to buy more expensive towers and upgrades sooner. The Farm, if used appropriately, can be extremely beneficial in obtaining expensive towers like the Turret, Ranger and Accelerator earlier than usual. The Farm also has a slightly larger placement footprint than other towers, though it is smaller than the Turret.
The Farm has a placement limit of ten per player. This is decreased to eight in PVP mode.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Farm is very useful to have in your loadout, as its ability to generate cash makes it very useful throughout the entire game. This is even more important when using expensive towers like the Accelerator, Engineer and Ranger. The only time you should not bring the Farm is when there are too few waves to make it worthwhile. This includes most events. Some events outright prevent Farms from generating cash or even being placed down, so it is useless to bring the Farm for them.

Keep in mind that the Farm does not generate money for teammates.

When using the Farm, ensure you have a balance of defense and farming. Too little of either can be dangerous. When playing with others, it is usually recommended to either focus wholly on Farms or defense. The other players can assist in the areas you are not working on. If you are defending in the early game, you should switch to Farms once the players who have farmed in the early game place down stronger towers that can sustain the following waves, and vice versa. You should state in chat what role you intend to play before making any move and observe if the other players are farming or defending. Be ready to drop your farming if the situation calls for it. Sometimes, the player defending may not be able to cope and needs assistance from other players. Depending on the stage of the game which this happens, you may need to use an early game tower to help. It is always a good idea to bring along some early defense, even if you are planning to farm the majority of the early game, just to be safe. When playing alone, the balance can be hard to maintain. Cheap, cost-effective early game towers should be used to defend. It may be more effective to use the Cowboy or Golden Cowboy instead of the Farm, as they cover both economy and defense at the same time. Do note that both can be used in conjunction.

When using the Farm, there is usually a choice between sticking to Level 3 or Level 5 Farms, though there is no right or wrong choice. If you do decide to upgrade to Level 5 Farms, upgrade them from Level 3 to Level 4 first and then upgrade them to Level 5. In Molten, Fallen and Frost modes, Level 5 Farms are generally more beneficial due to the larger number of waves and rather low cash gained from defeating enemies. In Easy, Intermediate, Polluted Wasteland II and Badlands II mode, the low number of waves makes Level 5 Farms usually not worthwhile. When playing in Pizza Party, Hardcore or Voidcore mode, Level 5 Farms are still a good option, but Level 3 Farms are sometimes sufficient, as you get enough money from defeating enemies.

On the final wave of any mode, all Farms not affected by Harvester should be sold, as they do not generate any cash, do not grow thorns and take up the tower limit.

Do not place Farms near the path in important spots, especially without Harvester, as they take up space and are potential optimal spots for offensive towers. If you have the Harvester, you may consider spreading out the Farms so that most of the path is covered by thorns, or clumping them up in order to do the most damage possible.

Although the DJ Booth cannot discount the Farm, Farms still count as a tower for DJ Booth Green track ability making it sometimes situational to place farms near DJ Booth early for more cash generation.
When farming, try to minimize unspent cash at the end of each wave while aiming for Level 2 and 3 Farms. Afterwards, get the Level 4 and then Level 5 Farms.

Consider how you place Farms in game for space and organization. Map placement can play a huge factor in Farm placement, as some maps may not have suitable room for Farms to be placed on, with the room having to be taken by other towers. You may want to factor this when doing solo or party strategies. You may want to place Farms in rows, such as four Farms placed extremely close to four other Farms to not waste space. It is not recommended to place Farms in areas you will have a hard time seeing or getting to if possible, such as behind the building in U-Turn.

The Farm was based on the Tower Battles version of the Farm.
The Level 2 upgrade Wheat was based on BelowNatural's wheatfields in the map Ducky's Bootcamp from R2DA.

Some towers do not have range, like the Military Base or Elf Camp, which could be considered having shortest range than the Farm.

electroshocker.name: Electroshocker
electroshocker.description: The Electroshocker is an intermediate tower that has the capability to deal damage through chain reactions. At later levels, it also becomes a support tower as it gains the ability to stun enemies and reduce Defense. It can be purchased in the store for 2,500 Coins. It can also damage Lead enemies from Level 0 and detect Hidden enemies from Level 2 onward.

Description: The Electroshocker is an intermediate tower that has the capability to deal damage through chain reactions. At later levels, it also becomes a support tower as it gains the ability to stun enemies and reduce Defense. It can be purchased in the store for 2,500 Coins. It can also damage Lead enemies from Level 0 and detect Hidden enemies from Level 2 onward.

The Electroshocker shoots a lightning-chain projectile from its Electro Gun that arcs toward and damages (where applicable) a set number of enemies, targeting the closest enemy to the original target. The Electroshocker can also stun enemies for 0.1 seconds at Level 0 which increase as with upgrades up to 0.25 seconds at Level 5. This completely stops the enemy. For enemies with Stun Immunity, the enemy is not stunned but rather slowed down by 40%. Bosses are not slowed down as much as regular enemies, since the slowdown is 20% on them.

From Level 5, it can melt 20% Defense with every hit, though it can only remove up to 20% of the defense. For example, if an enemy has 50% defense, the defense can be decreased by up to 10%, down to 40%.

The Electroshocker is considered an all-rounder tower, as its cheap cost allows it to be used for early-game dps, especially against Lead enemies, while its stunning capabilities, Defense reduction, chain damage and decent DPS, especially from Level 4+, make it extremely effective in the mid to late game.
The Electroshocker has a placement limit of seven per player.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Electroshocker can be used to clear out hordes of weaker enemies, though it will do worse against enemies with higher health, such as the Fallen Squire.

Use the Electroshocker in areas that enemies pass multiple times or at corners, as it gives the Electroshocker more opportunities to slow down and damage enemies. Intersections such as in the map Crossroads are also viable options.
Intersections such as in the map Crossroads are also viable options.
The Electroshocker can be very useful against fast enemies, such as the Fallen Rusher, while also dealing a decent amount of damage against them, especially when they come in hordes.

While the maximum range is stated as 17, due to the chain range, this can be further extended. Chain range works by shocking an enemy within another enemy's range, so long as they are within the chain range of that enemy. For example, an enemy outside the range of the Electroshocker may still be shocked if they are within the chain range of another enemy that was shocked. This only applies if the Electroshocker has not reached its maximum number of hits. This can allow the Electroshocker to indirectly hit undetectable enemies, like Flying enemies indirectly, such as the Balloon. Paired with its ability to hit Lead enemies, it can deal with Lead Balloon pretty well, only if other detectable enemies are in range. You can use the DJ Booth to increase the range of the Electroshocker. However, the chain range is not increased.

Since the Electroshocker can stun any enemy without Stun Immunity, it can be useful at any point in the game. Unlike most other slowing towers, its stun is not affected by size, making it quite good against larger enemies, like the Fallen Tank, or even major bosses, such as the Fallen King. For enemies with the Stun Immunity, there is no stun effect; rather, the enemy is slowed down by up to 40%. For Boss enemies, that effect is significantly weaker on them, though they are still slowed down by 20%.

The Electroshocker pairs well with towers that take time before they start attacking, such as the Minigunner and Accelerator. The Electroshocker also pairs well with towers with a slow firerate, like the Ranger and Mortar, as it gives them more time to attack enemies with their slow firerate.

The Electroshocker has lead detection, allowing it to deal with lead enemies, like the Lead. In later Levels a cluster of Electroshockers can deal with tankier late-game lead enemies like Deep Freeze.
You can use the Commander to decrease the firerate of the Electroshocker, which increases the number of times that it can stun enemies within its range.
Trivia: The vest that the Level 3+ Electroshocker wears is the Faraday Vest from R2DA, which in turn is named after the scientist Michael Faraday, who studied electricity. The creator of this vest is BelowNatural, the creator of Tower Defense Simulator.
The creator of this vest is BelowNatural, the creator of Tower Defense Simulator.
This tower may be very loosely based on the Plasma Trooper and/or the Stunner from Tower Battles.
The Tesla Tower, originally used by the first versions of the Electroshocker was a nod to the Wardenclyffe Tower in Shoreham, Long Island, New York, created by Nikola Tesla.

The first Level 4 upgrade name, "MOAR POWER" could have been a reference to Bloons Tower Defense 6 as there is an upgrade for the Boomerang Monkey called "M.O.A.R. Glaives". However, "M.O.A.R." actually stands for Multiple Object Advanced Ricochet in Bloons Tower Defense 6. It could also be a spoof on "more power".

The Level 5 upgrade name, "Zeus Cannon" is a reference to an upgraded Thundergun from the Call of Duty franchise, specifically the Zombies mode.

rocketeer.description: The Rocketeer, formerly known as the Rocketer, is an intermediate ground tower that attacks enemies with a rocket launcher. It is purchasable in the store for 2,500 Coins.

Description: The Rocketeer, formerly known as the Rocketer, is an intermediate ground tower that attacks enemies with a rocket launcher. It is purchasable in the store for 2,500 Coins.

The Rocketeer is a splash damage tower that deals very high damage to enemies within an explosion radius. It however, has a rather slow firerate. It has no damage drop-off, meaning it will always deal the same amount of damage to an enemy regardless of its distance from the explosion. Additionally, similarly to other splash damage towers, it is also able to damage Lead enemies and bypass defense. It has decent range, and can detect Hidden enemies at later levels. These aforementioned attributes allow it to be very effective against hordes of enemies.

At Level 4, it gains a quad missile launcher, which allows it to fire four missiles at once, targeting up to four different enemies at a time in its spread angle. This upgrade comes with the cost of reduced missile accuracy. If there are less than four enemies in the spread angle, the missiles will target an enemy already targeted by other missiles.
The Rocketeer is mostly considered a mid-to late-game tower due to its relatively high cost, as well as its ability to take down hordes of strong enemies with its high damage.
The Rocketeer has a placement limit of eight per player.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Rocketeer should not be used as an early game tower because of its high cost. If you wish to have splash damage during the early game, towers such as the Mortar or Electroshocker are cheaper choices.

While the Rocketeer does have better DPS from its main projectile, the Mortar can often deal higher DPS due to its clusters when facing off against large hordes, which have a far greater reach than Rocketeer's missiles, even if they are unlikely to all deal full damage. In contrast, the Rocketeer can be far more ideal against single enemies in comparison to the Mortar due to it having much higher DPS, especially since it does not have damage dropoff.
In contrast, the Rocketeer can be far more ideal against single enemies in comparison to the Mortar due to it having much higher DPS, especially since it does not have damage dropoff.

Due to its high DPS and hidden detection, the Rocketeer can reliably take down high health Hidden enemies such as the Shadow Boss. An explosion may also indirectly damage a Hidden enemy on Levels 0-1 if there are other detectable enemies nearby.
An explosion may also indirectly damage a Hidden enemy on Levels 0-1 if there are other detectable enemies nearby.

The Rocketeer can be very useful when paired with the Firework Technician, as the fireworks generated by the tower can assist in Rocketeer's area of effect potential. This is especially true at Level 4, where it will begin to fire four missiles at once, with each one having a decent chance to generate fireworks, resulting in higher overall odds for the Rocketeer to generate fireworks.

This is especially true at Level 4, where it will begin to fire four missiles at once, with each one having a decent chance to generate fireworks, resulting in higher overall odds for the Rocketeer to generate fireworks.

Due to its high splash DPS bypassing defense and with great area coverage from its large range, the Rocketeer can also be very helpful against high health targets and bosses such as the Slow King, Fallen Guardian or even the Fallen King, which can gain up to 60% defense.
Trivia: Prior to the MEGA Update, this was called the Rocketer. Rocketeer is the more universally-recognized correct spelling and, as such, was changed.
Rocketeer is the more universally-recognized correct spelling and, as such, was changed.

Originally, the Rocketeer gained a Howitzer artillery cannon at the final Level instead of a quad missile launcher. The quad missile launcher was the originally planned weapon that the Rocketeer would use at the final Level, though this never happened until January of 2025.

The v1.51.0 rework of Rocketeer could knock back enemies similarly to towers like the Hallow Punk, though this did not make it into the actual game.
The Rocketeer was loosely based on the Tuber from Tower Battles.

tooltips: A mid-game AOE tower with a slow fire-rate and solid damage. At max level it locks onto multiple enemies to fire a barrage of missiles.
Capable of targeting hidden, and lead enemies.
The Rocketeer, formerly known as the Rocketer, is an intermediate ground tower that attacks enemies with a rocket launcher. It is purchasable in the store for 2,500 Coins.
