It places down various traps on the ground, which when they come in contact with an enemy, the traps damage it in various ways or apply debuffs to them. All traps can damage Hidden enemies, damage Lead enemies and bypass defense. When there are no enemies in range, the Trapper will lay its traps randomly, but if there is an enemy within range the Trapper will target it by laying its traps directly at the enemy. It takes it 0.5 seconds to throw a trap, with the thrown traps having a velocity of 15. The only exception is when it is set to Random. Although a random enemy will still be highlighted when the Trapper is selected, the Trapper will lay its traps randomly and not at the highlighted enemy. There is a 10 second cooldown before a trap can be changed again.

Description: The Trapper is an intermediate tower that can be bought for 3,000 Coins. It places down various traps on the ground, which when they come in contact with an enemy, the traps damage it in various ways or apply debuffs to them. All traps can damage Hidden enemies, damage Lead enemies and bypass defense. When there are no enemies in range, the Trapper will lay its traps randomly, but if there is an enemy within range the Trapper will target it by laying its traps directly at the enemy. It takes it 0.5 seconds to throw a trap, with the thrown traps having a velocity of 15. The only exception is when it is set to Random. Although a random enemy will still be highlighted when the Trapper is selected, the Trapper will lay its traps randomly and not at the highlighted enemy. There is a 10 second cooldown before a trap can be changed again.

There are three types of traps that the Trapper can place down. The first is the spike trap, which is available from Level 0. Spike traps have a set amount of health, which when decreased to zero will make them disappear. This trap can hit as many enemies as long as it still has health. This trap can also deal more damage than its health, as the damage it deals is separate from its health. For example, if a spike trap has 1 health out of 60 left, an enemy that steps on it will receive the full 25 damage, if its health is at least 25. Spike traps get smaller as their health gets lower.
The second type is the landmine, which is unlocked at Level 2. When an enemy steps on it, it will quickly explode, dealing splash damage to all enemies caught in its explosion and applying burn.

The third and last trap is the bear trap, which is unlocked at Level 4. This trap, unlike the two previous traps, only deals damage to a single enemy. However, it deals higher damage than the other two traps and additionally stuns the enemy it hits for 3 seconds.
Each trap has a lifespan before disappearing. This lifespan will reset once it is used, however, as all of them except spike trap disappear on a single hit, this has little use for most of the traps.

The Trapper is considered an all-rounder tower as its cheap cost allows it to be used in the early game, while later on its upgraded traps deal immense damage to crowds and have great supporting utility.
The Trapper has a placement limit of seven per player.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: As it takes a long time for the Trapper to place down its traps, it is generally recommended to place the tower in the back, where it has more time to pile up traps. The Commander can also be used to decrease the Trapper's firerate, allowing it to place down more traps quicker.
The Commander can also be used to decrease the Trapper's firerate, allowing it to place down more traps quicker.

The Trapper's spikes can be very useful early on at dealing with both hordes of weaker enemies such as the Abnormal, though due to their low damage they are not effective against higher health enemies like the Normal Boss until later upgrades or when upgraded. It is generally best to place down multiple Level 1 or 2 Trappers early on because of their cost efficiency.
It is generally best to place down multiple Level 1 or 2 Trappers early on because of their cost efficiency.
Landmines can be quite useful at clearing out hordes of high health enemies, because of their high damage, them setting enemies on fire and their ability to ignore defense.

Bear traps only deal damage to a single enemy, meaning that it should generally only be used for high health enemies. It is best to set the Trapper's targeting to Strongest, as it means that the bear traps are less likely hit enemies with lower health. Additionally, the bear traps stun enemies for three seconds, making them quite effective at stalling enemies. If an enemy has Stun Immunity or is a Boss enemy, it will not be stunned but only slowed down instead.
It is best to set the Trapper's targeting to Strongest, as it means that the bear traps are less likely hit enemies with lower health.

Additionally, the bear traps stun enemies for three seconds, making them quite effective at stalling enemies. If an enemy has Stun Immunity or is a Boss enemy, it will not be stunned but only slowed down instead.
If an enemy has Stun Immunity or is a Boss enemy, it will not be stunned but only slowed down instead.
When the Trapper is set to Random, it will not target a random enemy — it will instead drop its traps in random spots.
The Trapper's spike and bear trap damage is unaffected by Damage Buffs, so pairing these traps with Damage Buffing towers like the DJ Booth or Mercenary Base is useless.
The Trapper is very useful on maps with longer paths, as it gives the tower more time to accumulate traps before enemies get to them.

While the Trapper itself does not have lead detection, its traps will still damage Lead enemies, making it effective against these types of enemies. However, the Trapper is unable to directly throw traps at Flying enemies due to its aforementioned lack of flying detection. While the traps can hit hidden and lead enemies, they cannot hit Flying enemies, as they will fly over it. As the spike and bear traps deal damage like unit collision, they cannot hit Ghost enemies. However, the landmine is not affected by this.

The Trapper's spike and bear traps are very useful against enemies with the tank attribute, as they deal damage to them at a quick speed.
Trivia: The Trapper is loosely based on the Spike Factory from the Bloons Tower Defense series.

Prior to the 11th of June 2025, the Level 3 Trapper with spike traps selected had the highest firerate of any tower in the game, that being 7.5 without the Firerate Bug. The current tower with the highest firerate is the Level 4 Ranger.

tooltips: A [sic] early game defensive tower that lays down traps. At later levels the tower can select from multiple traps to focus on AOE or stuns.
Traps trigger on all enemies except for flying.

The Trapper is an intermediate tower that can be bought for 3,000 Coins. It places down various traps on the ground, which when they come in contact with an enemy, the traps damage it in various ways or apply debuffs to them. All traps can damage Hidden enemies, damage Lead enemies and bypass defense. When there are no enemies in range, the Trapper will lay its traps randomly, but if there is an enemy within range the Trapper will target it by laying its traps directly at the enemy. It takes it 0.5 seconds to throw a trap, with the thrown traps having a velocity of 15. The only exception is when it is set to Random. Although a random enemy will still be highlighted when the Trapper is selected, the Trapper will lay its traps randomly and not at the highlighted enemy. There is a 10 second cooldown before a trap can be changed again.

pulse_trooper.name: Pulse Trooper
pulse_trooper.description: The Pulse Trooper is an intermediate tower that fires pulses at enemies in its range. It can be purchased in the store for 3,250 Coins. It can also damage Lead enemies from Level 2 onward.

Description: The Pulse Trooper is an intermediate tower that fires pulses at enemies in its range. It can be purchased in the store for 3,250 Coins. It can also damage Lead enemies from Level 2 onward.

The Pulse Trooper will fire a piercing pulse in a 360° arc around the tower. This pulse will expand as it goes through the tower's range, disappearing once it reaches the end of its range. These pulses will damage any enemy they hit once. At Level 4, it also unlocks the Sweeper ability. This will stop the Pulse Trooper from attacking normally and instead will replace it with a map wide dual laser. These two lasers will move through the entire map for a few seconds, damaging each enemy twice. Both attacks are capable of indirectly hitting Hidden and Flying enemies.
The Pulse Trooper has a placement limit of seven per player.
Ability: Stops all normal attacks and unleashes two map-wide lasers on the map. These take a specific laser duration to move around the map, with each laser dealing damage once to any enemy it hits, effectively resulting in an enemy being damaged twice by this ability.
Strategy: Although its single-target damage is rather poor, the Pulse Trooper excels at clearing out crowds thanks to its pulses damaging every enemy in its range. Due to this, spots which cover a lot of the path but also are in close proximity due to the Pulse Trooper having low range are best suited for it. Examples of such path layouts include loops or U-turns. Range boosting towers like the DJ Booth can be very beneficial for these towers thanks to this, as it will extend how far the pulses can reach, effectively boosting its potential DPS.

This is best used on high enemy count waves due to its map-wide range.

military_base.name: Military Base
military_base.description: The Military Base is an intermediate tower that spawns various military-themed vehicles, which can be bought in the store for 4,000 Coins. Levels 0-3 will spawn Humvees of varying strength, Level 4 will spawn a Tank and Level 5 will spawn a Railgun Tank.

Description: The Military Base is an intermediate tower that spawns various military-themed vehicles, which can be bought in the store for 4,000 Coins. Levels 0-3 will spawn Humvees of varying strength, Level 4 will spawn a Tank and Level 5 will spawn a Railgun Tank.

Periodically, the Military Base will spawn a unit at the end of the path. The unit will head towards the start of the path until it gets destroyed, damaging enemies along the way. If it reaches the entrance, the unit will disappear. When there are enemies in a unit's range, it will slow down so that it has more time to attack enemies.

For the first two upgrades, the main purpose of this tower is to spawn units with its Military Caravan that deal direct collision damage to enemies (Humvee and Humvee 2). After Level 3, the unit itself (Humvee 3) can deal damage through ranged weapons, and after Level 4, units spawned by the Military Base can deal ranged splash damage (Tank and Railgun Tank). The explosion is separated into two spheres. Enemies in the inner sphere will be dealt 100% of the stated damage, while the damage in the outer sphere is decreased linearly. Its splash damage deals full damage to enemies with defense. Military Base spawns can damage lead enemies through collision or splash, but not with their mounted guns. Both the tower and units are immune to debuffs, units being fully and while technically the tower can receive some debuffs, none of them can actually impact any of its stats. These units cannot be stunned, but they can be damaged by certain enemy abilities.

At Level 4, the Military Base gains the Airstrike ability which drops six bombs in a cluster around on a specified path location when used. The bombs cause explosions that damage any enemies within the blast radius. Like all explosions, the explosion is separated into two spheres. Enemies in the inner sphere will be dealt 100% of the stated damage, while the damage in the outer sphere is decreased linearly. Its splash damage also deals full damage to enemies regardless of if they have defense or not. At Level 5, the bombs gain more damage and have a larger blast radius.

The Military Base is considered an all-round tower. Its cheap placement cost and early upgrade are affordable in the early game, and its base units, such as the Humvee and Humvee 2 can deal with lower health enemies. Later on, its later expensive upgrades, but more advanced units like the Tank and Railgun Tank can deal with higher health enemies that appear onwards in the mid to late game. Be aware that there is a limit of five Military Bases per player.
Ability: Drops bombs on a selected path location, damaging any enemies within the bombs' explosion radius. A red marker will appear on the location of the path selected, and bombs will drop when the marker is clicked.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: Upgrading a Military Base to Level 1 reduces the spawnrate by 10 seconds, allowing the unit to spawn in 35 seconds instead of 45. Selling a Military Base will destroy the unit. In PVP, the spawnrate is even shorter for both Level 0 and Levels 1-5 by 5 seconds, making it spawn far faster there.

It should not be used against single high health enemies, like the Fallen Tank, due to its long cooldown.

The Military Base was made unusable between the 21st of July 2021 and 22 July 2021, because if multiple units spawned very close to each other it would lag out the game, giving players an unfair advantage. This glitch no longer works. You could still equip the Military Base in your loadout, despite it being unusable. However, placing it would make the following message appear: " Military Base placement has been temporarily disabled. This unit is faulty, allowing players to gain an unfair advantage. "

The Level 5 Military Base used to be the most expensive upgrade in the game for quite a long time. When the Duck Hunt Update released, it added the Engineer tower, which had a more expensive upgrade cost. Later with updates, more towers would get upgrades that were more expensive than the Military Base's Level 5 upgrade, such as the Turret or Accelerator.

The aircraft responsible for orchestrating the airstrike is a Northrop Grumman B-2 'Spirit' stealth bomber.

The arrow on the Airstrike's marker is the tangent line of the plane's flight of where it drops the bombs. It is based on the line passing through the coordinates of the player's camera and the selected path. If multiple Airstrikes are selected at once, the planes fly on equiangular flight paths relative to each other.

crook_boss.name: Crook Boss
crook_boss.description: The Crook Boss is an intermediate tower that sends out goons to fight alongside it. The tower is unlocked upon reaching Level 30, but it can alternatively be purchased as a gamepass for 168 Robux. The Crook Boss can be claimed using the pop up message that appears when joining the lobby.

Description: The Crook Boss is an intermediate tower that sends out goons to fight alongside it. The tower is unlocked upon reaching Level 30, but it can alternatively be purchased as a gamepass for 168 Robux. The Crook Boss can be claimed using the pop up message that appears when joining the lobby.

Initially, the Crook Boss has medium damage, an average firerate and low range. However, with later upgrades, the firerate decreases and its damage increases significantly. The range also increases but is still quite short compared to other towers, such as the Turret. The Crook Boss has the ability to spawn the Pistol Goon from Level 0, which with later levels gets double spawns. Additional, at Level 3, it spawns Tommy Goon 1, which gets replaced by Tommy Goon 2 at Level 4. These units all have lifespans, meaning they are on the map only for a few minutes. Every time it summons a unit, it stops attacking for a second and a half. Both Tommy Goon 1 and Tommy Goon 2 have hidden detection and the Pistol Goon has flying detection.

The Crook Boss is a mid to late-game tower due to its expensive cost and good DPS. It can also be used a great sub-dps tower in the late-game due to its high DPS at Level 4. However its capabilities in the late game are limited because of its moderate placement limit.
There is a limit of five Crook Bosses for each player. Additionally, it has a limit of ten Pistol Goons per tower and a limit of three Tommy Goon 1s and Tommy Goon 2s per tower.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: You can only place a maximum of five Crook Bosses. If you have other towers without placement limits (such as the Minigunner and the Swarmer) then it is best to use them after you have got five Crook Bosses.
If you have other towers without placement limits (such as the Minigunner and the Swarmer) then it is best to use them after you have got five Crook Bosses.

The Crook Boss is well worth its cost mid to late-game, and it does a decent job at dealing damage, especially when the goons are included. In some regards, the Crook Boss is better than the Minigunner, but it does have a placement limit.
In some regards, the Crook Boss is better than the Minigunner, but it does have a placement limit.
Do not rely entirely on the goons as their low health makes them vulnerable to enemy collision and abilities that deal damage.

If you are on a map where units can consistently target enemies from further away, such as Crossroads or Honey Valley, the units that spawn from the Crook Boss may prove quite useful in providing extra damage, especially against slower enemies. You may also use towers, such as the Electroshocker, Toxic Gunner or Freezer, to slow down enemies, giving the units more time to shoot at enemies. Do note, however, that there is a limit on how many of them can be spawned from a single Crook Boss. Additionally, they all have lifespans, making them last on the map for only a few minutes.
You may also use towers, such as the Electroshocker, Toxic Gunner or Freezer, to slow down enemies, giving the units more time to shoot at enemies.
Do note, however, that there is a limit on how many of them can be spawned from a single Crook Boss. Additionally, they all have lifespans, making them last on the map for only a few minutes.

Though the Game Master skin does not directly buff the Crook Boss, the piggy banks it spawns lights up a large portion of the map. This can be useful in dark maps like Pizza Party, where low visibility can be a nuisance or detriment to the player.
Trivia: Originally, the Crook Boss spawned the Crook at Level 4 and the Mafia at Level 5. However, in the Frost Invasion Update, this was changed so that is spawned the Body Guard, Body Guards 1 and Body Guards 2. Prior to the 13th of May 2022, the Golden skin spawned the Golden Crook at Level 2-3 and the Golden Mafia at Level 4. However, when golden perks were added, it spawned the Body Guard, Body Guards 1 and Body Guards 2 like all other skins, unless the golden perk was active.

Prior to the 13th of May 2022, the Golden skin spawned the Golden Crook at Level 2-3 and the Golden Mafia at Level 4. However, when golden perks were added, it spawned the Body Guard, Body Guards 1 and Body Guards 2 like all other skins, unless the golden perk was active.
The Crook Boss was the first tower released that could be unlocked at a certain level, and also the first tower that could be bought with {Robux} Robux.
The Crook Boss was originally a reference to the Mafia City meme.
Prior to the MEGA Update, the Level 1 upgrade description would mention that the Crook Boss gains a " gamer hat ", though it was not a statistical change.

Prior to the Frost Invasion Update, the Crook Boss only had a unit limit in Hardcore Testing BETA, which was set to two. In the Frost Invasion Update, it was later re-added as the limit was never added in the Overhaul Update, though it was decreased from two to one. This limit would later change in updates.
In the Frost Invasion Update, it was later re-added as the limit was never added in the Overhaul Update, though it was decreased from two to one. This limit would later change in updates.
The Crook Boss' Level 4 upgrade name, The Godfather, may be a reference to the famous mafia movie and novel of the same name.
Alien Focus skin of the Crook Boss is the second most expensive items purchasable in the game with coins, at 1,346,914,768 Coins.

commander.name: Commander
commander.description: The Commander is an advanced support tower that decreases the firerate of towers within its range, increasing their damage output. It can be purchased in the store for 4,000 Coins.

Description: The Commander is an advanced support tower that decreases the firerate of towers within its range, increasing their damage output. It can be purchased in the store for 4,000 Coins.

The Commander provides a 10% firerate boost to towers in its range, making them attack enemies faster. This buff can be boosted further at Level 2+ through the Call to Arms ability, which increases it by 10% for ten seconds. Both buffs get higher with levels, with the passive buff getting increased to 20% and the Call to Arms ability buff getting increased to 20%. It also has a second ability, Support Caravan, which costs $2,000 to use. This will summon two Gunner APCs and one Missile APC on the map. When any ability used, it will enter fury mode, allowing it to attack any enemy in its range for ten seconds. The attack time from using an ability stacks if multiple are used at once or when an ability is used while it is attacking. When an ability is used while fury mode is active, the timer for it will stop until the ability animation is finished.

The Commander is the primary narrator in most matches. Text dialogue appears beside the image or the model with an idle animation of the Commander, corresponding to the appearance of certain waves. This dialogue appears regardless of whether a Commander tower is present on the map, and the image or model of the Commander next to the dialogue will display different emotions.
The Commander has a placement limit of six per player.
Abilities: Boosts all towers' firerate in its range by a variable amount for 10 seconds. Additionally, the Commander will be able to attack enemies with its own weapon for 10 seconds.
Summons two Gunner APCs and one Missile APC. Additionally, the Commander will be able to attack enemies with its own weapon for 10 seconds.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: Firerate boost is calculated as Original Firerate ÷ (1+Firerate Boost) where Original Firerate is the base firerate of the tower, Firerate Boost is the boost supplied by the Commander in decimal form (for example, 10% is 0.1). For example, a Level 4 Commander (20%) will decrease the firerate of a tower firing from 1 second to 0.833 seconds. While in the game it may look like the firerate is rounded down to the second decimal, this is only visual. The firerate is longer than that and is not rounded up. The Commander can boost the pump time of the Enforcer, meaning it is fully effective on it if units are not included. The Commander cannot decrease the cooldown of burst towers. The Commander also cannot boost the Executioner due to the axe not returning in time to take advantage.

When placing a Commander, try to place it near as many towers as possible, as this will allow for a high number of towers to be boosted. This is also true in reverse; it is recommended that you place your towers close to a Commander (if there is one) for the Firerate Buff. This also includes cliff-based towers. The Ace Pilot and Pursuit can also be boosted, though their towers (runway and helipad, respectively) must be within range of the Commander.

Slow firing towers, such as the Rocketeer or Ranger, will benefit massively from the Firerate Buff that the Commander supplies.

Placing three Level 2+ Commanders and activating their Call to Arms ability one at a time every 10 seconds is one of the most effective ways to utilize the Commander, as Call to Arms will be permanently active if this is done correctly, providing the 20% buff permanently. You can also place two Level 2+ Commanders and constantly sell and replace one to renew its Call to Arms ability to save a placement for another tower, or four if you want to be safer with keeping the Call to Arms ability active at all times while not having to worry about selling and replacing Commanders, as having three Commanders require you to be quite precise to keep the 20% buff at all times, and you may get distracted from using its ability while upgrading other towers. There are a few ways to tell when to use another ability, which include waiting until the Firerate Buff icon and visuals disappears, waiting until the ability timer gets reduced by 10 (which without Skills, is it reaching 20) or waiting until the attack timer reaches 2.

You can increase the range in which the Commander can affect towers and the Call to Arms range by using the DJ Booth. The DJ Booth can also be useful at reducing the usage cost of the Support Caravan ability.
The DJ Booth can also be useful at reducing the usage cost of the Support Caravan ability.

It is best to use the Commander's Call to Arms ability on a boss with high health (such as a major boss, like the Fallen King). Be aware that some bosses have blocking abilities, meaning that a wrongly timed Call to Arms ability will be useless. Additionally, you cannot activate the Call to Arms ability if the Commander is stunned. To overcome this, the Medic can be used to protect the Commander from stuns, though this is generally not recommended as the shield also provides boosts best used on other towers. Alternatively, you can sell and replace the Commander. Do note that this will remove the passive Firerate Buff for a short while if there are no other Commanders placed down.

Be aware that you cannot stack the Call to Arms ability. If a Call to Arms ability is still active for towers, then activating another Call to Arms will not grant any additional buff. However, it resets the duration of the ability. However, the Call to Arms ability can stack with boosts from other towers, like the Gladiator 's Warrior's Call.

The Commander cannot boost the firerate of the Ace Pilot 's bombs, Pursuit 's missiles, Commando 's missiles or any units like the Railgun Tank from the Military Base or the Tommy Goon 2 from the Crook Boss, even if their associated tower is in the range of a Commander.
If the Call to Arms ability is active, and a new tower is placed in the range of the Commander, that tower will not be boosted by the ability until it is activated again.

While the Commander has flying, lead and hidden detection, it can only attack enemies with these attributes periodically with its two abilities. Given how costly it is to get its abilities and that they both have lengthy cooldowns, relying solely on the Commander to fight against enemies with these attributes is unwise. Other towers like the Ace Pilot, Electroshocker and Militant are more effective and reliable against them, with the Commander buffing them.

When Call of Arms is used, the fireate buff is applied instantly, however, the displayed timer only appears once the animation is done, which is roughly 2 seconds. Therefore, to be more optimized with chaining the buff, wait until the timer hits 2, then activate the next ability.
Trivia: When the game was in Alpha, the Commander's upgrade stats were not displayed on its upgrade description. It was simply referred to as "sans support sans support".
The Commander is heavily inspired by the Tower Battles tower of the same name.

Before the Overhaul Update, the spawnrate of the Military Base could be boosted by a Commander (so that the spawn time between units is reduced), but it was through an unconventional method. The stated buff was subtracted from the spawnrate (an example is a 25% buff on a Level 5 Military Base; the spawnrate would decrease from 45 to 44.75). As 44.75 seconds rounded up to 45 seconds, there was no noticeable decrease in spawn time. However, this did not apply to the spawnrates of units from the Crook Boss. Interestingly, the Call to Arms reduced the spawnrate of units from the Military Base further, but even this buff could not produce a noticeable decrease in spawnrate.

There were multiple other voice lines that were recorded by JOHN ROBLOX, however they were never added to the game. tooltips: A support tower that provides a passive attack speed buff to nearby towers. Can also use its active skills to provide a temporary massive buff to nearby towers.

The Commander is an advanced support tower that decreases the firerate of towers within its range, increasing their damage output. It can be purchased in the store for 4,000 Coins.

upgrades.name: Call to Arms
description: Boosts all towers' firerate in its range by a variable amount for 10 seconds. Additionally, the Commander will be able to attack enemies with its own weapon for 10 seconds.

upgrades.name: Support Caravan
description: Summons two Gunner APCs and one Missile APC. Additionally, the Commander will be able to attack enemies with its own weapon for 10 seconds.

warden.name: Warden
warden.description: The Warden is an advanced ground tower with short range that can be purchased from the store for 4,000 Coins after triumphing Pizza Party. Alternatively, it is obtainable through a gamepass for 337 Robux without having to triumph the map.

Description: The Warden is an advanced ground tower with short range that can be purchased from the store for 4,000 Coins after triumphing Pizza Party. Alternatively, it is obtainable through a gamepass for 337 Robux without having to triumph the map.

The Warden attacks enemies with its baton. The Warden does not deal damage when it fires, it instead deals damage when its weapon contacts the enemy. It also cannot change which enemy it is targeting while swinging it. Because of this, the Warden may sometimes miss the target, or hit an entirely different enemy. Every third swing is a crit, dealing more damage and stuns an enemy for a few seconds. From Level 3, the Warden stuns enemies with every hit. The stun time depends on how big the enemy is; the bigger the enemy is, the shorter the stun time is. Additionally, if an enemy has the Stun Immunity, it is only slowed down by 40% instead of being completely stopped. It can only damage one enemy with each swing.

At Level 4, it gains a riot shield, which it uses to block stuns. The stun block has a 6 second cooldown and the parry itself lasts 1 second. After succesfully blocking a stun, the Warden will grant itself a temporary 100% Damage Buff and Stun Immunity for 6 seconds. When dealing crit damage, the Damage Buff will boost the crit damage by as much as regular damage. For example, for 80 damage and a crit multiplier of 3, an 100% Damage Buff boosts the Warden 's damage from 80 to 160, increasing it by 80. Because of this, the crit damage, which is 240, will also get increased by 80 to 320.
The Warden has a placement limit of 12 per player.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: A few Wardens can be pretty effective in the mid-game. By late-game, its Level 4 can also be useful due to its parry effectively granting it permanent Stun Immunity through the parry itself and the actual immunity the parry gives.
By late-game, its Level 4 can also be useful due to its parry effectively granting it permanent Stun Immunity through the parry itself and the actual immunity the parry gives.
Due to Warden's short range, it should be placed at bends or turns on the map to make the most use of its range. The DJ Booth can be useful at increasing its range.
The DJ Booth can be useful at increasing its range.

The Warden will often struggle against large hordes of enemies, as it can only damage one enemy at a time. Therefore, placing multiple Wardens or using support towers like the Commander is recommended.
As the Warden's Level 3 and 4 upgrades are quite expensive, the Farm or the DJ Booth can be used to afford them quicker.
The Warden has lead detection at Level 2, making it fairly useful against Frost Invaders and Elite Leads.

The Warden can parry stuns at Level 4, as it unlocks Riot Shield, making it useful against enemies that can stun multiple towers, such as major bosses. It also very effective against major bosses, if they stun while in range of your Wardens, due to the 100% Damage Buff. On a lot of waves, no enemies that stun spawn or only enemies that debuff towers appear, making its parry get triggered less. This can be corrected to some degree by activating Exploding Enemies in match, which will make every enemy stun towers on their death, making the parry trigger more often.
It also very effective against major bosses, if they stun while in range of your Wardens, due to the 100% Damage Buff.

Multiple Level 4 Wardens can quite effectively slow down enemies. This is very useful for towers with long firerates, cooldowns or spawnrates, as it gives them more time to attack an enemy. Larger enemies, like the Slow Boss will be stunned for a shorter period of time. Enemies with Stun Immunity, like the Molten Titan will only be slowed down rather than stunned. The Warden's stun is very weak against major bosses, as they all have a significantly reduced stun time. Additionally, they are only slowed down instead of stunned.

The Warden has a small placement footprint, meaning that it can squeeze in beside other towers quite easily.
Trivia: The Warden, Cowboy and Saboteur are the only towers that requires both a badge and coins to unlock.

The Warden's Level 4 upgrade name, Class Foxtrot Defense Level, is a reference to the Halloween 2022 Trailer, where the Warden opens a door with its equipment inside. This door has a note which says that it should only be opened in class foxtrot defense level. The term "foxtrot" may also derive from the titular final boss, Wox the Fox.
The term "foxtrot" may also derive from the titular final boss, Wox the Fox.

The Warden's Level 1 upgrade name, Night Shift, is most likely a reference to Five Nights at Freddy's. The tower as a whole seems to be very loosely based on the Night Guard from Five Nights at Freddy's 2, although he does not wield a baton.
The tower as a whole seems to be very loosely based on the Night Guard from Five Nights at Freddy's 2, although he does not wield a baton.
Oddly, the second version of Warden's inventory description was the same as the Gladiator 's.
The Warden's Warden Job Interviews is a parody of a Five Nights at Freddy's Movie meme. A video of the TikTok can be found here.
A video of the TikTok can be found here.
The Level 2 upgrade cost is a reference to the The Bite of '87 from Five Nights at Freddy's, which in the franchise happened in 1987.

The Warden was originally made to act as a permanent stand-in for the Sledger as part of a bigger plan to make new permanent towers based on existing event towers. The Warden was the only tower ever finished from this plan, with the rest of the towers having little progress done on them. The only other known tower was a sawblade launcher tower that would've had a similar function to the Executioner.

cowboy.description: The Cowboy is an advanced ground tower which generates income every few shots. It can be purchased from the store for 4,000 Coins only after triumphing Badlands II. Due to a bug, the tower does not need to be purchased, instead appearing in the Gift Box. Alternatively, its gamepass can be purchased for 340 Robux.

Description: The Cowboy is an advanced ground tower which generates income every few shots. It can be purchased from the store for 4,000 Coins only after triumphing Badlands II. Due to a bug, the tower does not need to be purchased, instead appearing in the Gift Box. Alternatively, its gamepass can be purchased for 340 Robux.

While initially having a fast firerate, it deals only moderate damage, and has middling range compared to towers such as the Accelerator. On later levels, the Cowboy gains much higher damage, bigger range and a faster firerate. The Cowboy can also generate cash every sixth shot at Level 0 and Level 5. The number of shots needed for the Cowboy to generate cash can be seen above its tower icon in the upgrade box or when you hover your cursor over it. After firing the sixth shot, it will spin its gun for a few seconds. The Spin Time is decreased at higher levels. This ability is extremely useful as a secondary source of economy and can even replace the Farm in certain conditions.
The Cowboy is considered an all-round tower. Its DPS makes it decent to defend early and mid-game, while its ability to generate cash can make it useful for the entire match.
The Cowboy has a placement limit of twelve per player. This is decreased to ten in PVP mode.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: While the Cowboy is decent early on during the game, it should be replaced with higher DPS towers later on, like the Accelerator. It can be kept for its extra cash generation. It can also serve as extra DPS to complement your main DPS tower, depending on your loadout.
It can be kept for its extra cash generation. It can also serve as extra DPS to complement your main DPS tower, depending on your loadout.

Early on during the game, you may want to place down multiple Level 0 Cowboys because of their cheap price, decent DPS and effective cash generation, then slowly upgrade them one by one. However, do note that you may let some high health or Hidden enemies get past, like the Fallen Squire or Fallen Soul. Therefore, it may be worth upgrading some Cowboys to Level 3 for its greater DPS and hidden detection.

The Cowboy can generate a set amount of money every sixth shot, starting at Level 0. However, this does not give as much cash compared to the Farm early on. If you intend to replace Farm with the Cowboy, be aware of this. If you want to use this tower for cash generation early on, multiple Level 2 Cowboys can be quite effective. Later on, Level 4 or 5 Cowboys can be used for additional cash, due to their way lower firerate, higher income and lower spin time. The amount of cash earned can be increased even further with Commander 's Firerate Buff. The DJ Booth can reduce the Cowboy's upgrade costs, increase its range, and improve its damage, further contributing to its cash generation capabilites. Though, it is best to keep the DJ Booth set to the purple or green track as the red track increases its damage by 20%, lowering the amount of times it can shoot. However, for shorter or more difficult gamemodes like Polluted Wasteland II, this tactic is usually not needed

Enemies summoned by other enemies or sent by players do not count for cash shot. However, any enemy that the game does not consider a summoned enemy can still be generated cash from. This includes actually summoned enemies game does not consider summoned, like the Slime from the Slime, or enemies converted in a way that makes them look like a summoned enemy, such as Corpses. Additionally, you can increase the money earned by the Cowboy by placing it near the start of the path, ensuring that no other towers can damage enemies before the Cowboy. While the Cowboy cannot damage lead enemies, like the Lead, shots towards these enemies will contribute to the Cowboy's cash shot.

Trivia: The Cowboy could have been unlocked from the Badlands map. However, this map was removed in the Wanted Dead Update and replaced with Badlands II. The Cowboy could have also been unlocked by triumphing End of the Line. However, this map was removed in the MEGA Update.

The Cowboy has had many ways to generate money throughout the updates. Between the MEGA Update and Smaller = Bigger Update, the Cowboy was unable to generate cash. Before the MEGA Update, the Cowboy could generate cash with its Gold Rush ability at Level 5, which had a 4% chance to drop a money bag worth between $100 and $350 every time it damaged an enemy. Between the Smaller = Bigger Update and Overhaul Update, the Cowboy had a 12% chance (1% chance at Level 5) to generate between $60 and $750 cash, with the max amount increasing with each wave. This made the Cowboy generate an absurd amount of money for early and mid-game waves, making it a direct replacement to the Farm for many players at the time. Between the Overhaul Update and Wanted Dead Update, the Cowboy could generate at minimum of between $10 and $60 cash every fifth shot at Level 2, with the max amount increasing by $1 with each wave. After the Wanted Dead Update, the Cowboy can generate a set amount of cash every sixth shot.

The chance for the Cowboy to generate cash with each shot was also decreased to compensate for the faster firerate. dj_booth.name: DJ Booth
dj_booth.description: The DJ Booth is an advanced tower that is primarily a support tower with some economic and offensive capabilities through its Drop the Beat ability unlocked at Level 3. It can be bought from the store for 5,000 Coins.

Description: The DJ Booth is an advanced tower that is primarily a support tower with some economic and offensive capabilities through its Drop the Beat ability unlocked at Level 3. It can be bought from the store for 5,000 Coins.
The DJ Booth provides boosts to towers in range through different tracks, which also changes the behavior of its Drop the Beat ability.

The Purple track is unlocked on Level 0 and is active by default. It grants a 12.5% Range Buff to towers, which with Levels increases to up to 25%. When the Drop the Beat ability is used, it will create three (four at Level 5) pulses which knockback and slow down enemies. These can hit any enemy, regardless of immunities. The knockback is the regular knockback, meaning any immunity that prevents enemies from being knocked back, such as Stun Immunity, will prevent the enemy from being knocked back. How far back the enemy is knocked back depends on its size. Bigger enemies will get pushed back a smaller distance than an average-sized enemy. However, only boss enemies are immune to the slowdown. The slowdown effectiveness is based on the number of towers in the DJ Booth's range, starting from 10% and increasing by 1% to up to 25%. At Level 5, base slowdown is increased to 10% and max slowness is increased to 35%. It applies a 10% Range Buff at Level 5 if the Purple track is not selected.

The Green track is unlocked on Level 0. It grants a 5% Discount Buff to towers, which with Levels increases to 15%. When the Drop the Beat ability is used, it will generate cash. There is a base amount of cash given, which is $250, which is increased by $35 for every tower in range of the DJ Booth, up to a total of $600. All three statistics are able increase to up to $750 base cash, $75 increase per tower and $2,250. It applies a 5% Discount Buff at Level 5 if the Green track is not selected.

The Red track is unlocked at Level 2. It grants a 10% Damage Buff to towers, which with Levels increases to 20%. When the Drop the Beat ability is used, it will create three (four at Level 5) pulses that deal 25 damage to enemies. It can damage hidden, lead and flying enemies. This damage increases to 50 at Level 5. The pulses also drops the defense of enemies. The base defense drop is 2%, which increases by 0.25% for every tower in the DJ Booth's range up to 10%. The pulses only drops defense once, as it cannot drop more defense than what its defense drop is. For example, if the Level 5 DJ Booth has 40 towers in its range, it will only drop 15% defense from a Fallen Hazmat, making it have 45% defense. It applies a 7.5% Damage Buff at Level 5 if the Red track is not selected.
There is a limit of one DJ Booth per player.
Ability: Performs an ability based on the track.
•Purple: Creates pulses that knockback enemies and apply slowness to enemies, with slowness increasing for each tower in its range.
•Green: Generates Cash when used, with the amount increasing for each tower in its range.
•Red: Creates pulses that damage and reduce defense of enemies, with each tower in its range boosting how much defense is reduced.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The DJ Booth's buffs are calculated as Range Buff: Original Range × (1 + [[Range Buff]]) Discount Buff: Original Price × (1 − Discount Buff) Damage Buff: Original Damage × (1 + [[Damage Buff]]) where Range and Discount Buffs are the buffs supplied by the DJ Booth in decimal form (for example, 10% is 0.1). Additionally, damage is rounded down. For example, a Level 5 DJ Booth set on the Green Track (15% Discount Buff, 10% Range Buff, 7.5% Damage Buff) will decrease the cost of a Level 4 Ranger from $25,000 to $21,250, increase its range from 70 to 77, and increase its damage from 875 to 940. However, the Range Buff cannot increase the range of the following towers: The Shotgunner, as its bullets do not extend into the gained range. The DJ Booth. The DJ Booth also cannot decrease the upgrade prices of another DJ Booth. The circling range of the Ace Pilot. The radius in which towers gain hidden detection from the Ace Pilot also cannot be increased. These towers' attack ranges will still be increased. The chain range of the Electroshocker and Tesla. The attack range can still be increased. The deadzone ranges of towers like the Biologist and Engineer. The sentry building range of the Engineer. The explosion radius from Splash Damage towers cannot be increased. The Discount Buff cannot decrease a tower's placement cost. It also does not affect the Farm. The DJ Booth can drop defense of enemies, though the way it is done in is unique. Instead of reducing it by 25% of the enemy's defense, it is a flat reduction based on the number of towers in its range, with the highest being 18%. For example, an enemy with 50% defense and the DJ Booth has 20 towers in its range, it will have its defense reduced to 32%. This means that in comparison to other defense dropping towers, like the Pyromancer, it is more effective on enemies with low defense, such as the Molten Golem, while the Pyromancer is more effective on enemies with higher defense, like the Reaver.

The Purple track knocks back and slows down enemies when the Drop the Beat ability is used, making it useful at stalling hordes or singular enemies. Its knockback cannot affect any enemy immune to it, such as stun immune enemies. Additionally, bigger enemies will get pushed back a smaller distance. The only enemies immune to its slowdown are bosses. This makes it a great choice for slowing down enemies. If you have enough money, you can keep selling and replacing the DJ Booth and use its purple track ability to constantly slow down enemies.

The DJ Booth can be extremely useful in increasing the Commander and Mercenary Base 's range so that more towers receive the buffs from these towers. It can also be useful at reducing their ability costs.

The DJ Booth can increase the Medic 's range, allowing it to shield towers that are further away.
While the DJ Booth's range cannot be buffed by another DJ Booth, the Ranger 's Range Buff is able to buff the DJ Booth's range.

If you want to sell your towers, do be aware that towers within the range of the DJ Booth get less cash back in comparison to those outside the range of the DJ Booth. If you would like to relocate your towers, it is not recommended to sell your DJ Booth as well because sell prices are permanently affected if a tower is upgraded with a Level 3 or higher DJ Booth nearby.

Due to the fact that the DJ Booth can only give the buffs from one track before Level 5 (and even then, it does not give as much passively for other tracks), it may be a good idea to change the tracks regularly to cope with the kinds of threats that may be faced. If the wave is fairly easy, then it is recommended to use the Green track most of the time, with the discounts allowing you and other players to save money and build up defenses easier. If there are multiple tough enemies, using the Red track is recommended to increase other towers' damage, deal extra damage via the Drop the Beat ability, and for the enemies defenses to be reduced via the ability. If there are multiple fast enemies that can easily escape the range of your towers, using the Purple track's ability is great at pushing them back and slow them down. The increased range for affected towers will also ensure they can hit more enemies in their range.

On 29th of December 2021, the Ghost skin briefly used an edited version of The Only Thing They Fear Is You from DOOM Eternal due to a bug. This track was likely used during the development and was added to the game by accident, as on leaks of the Ghost skin, the same track could be heard. The Masquerade plays the Halloween 2020 Event lobby theme, though without the intro. The DJ Booth has a gamepass that allows you to play your own custom music with it for 85 Robux.

tesla.name: Tesla
tesla.description: The Tesla is a mid-late game advanced tower which attacks enemies with chain lightning, temporarily immobilizing them. It can be bought for 6,000 Coins.

Description: The Tesla is a mid-late game advanced tower which attacks enemies with chain lightning, temporarily immobilizing them. It can be bought for 6,000 Coins.

The Tesla fires lightning at enemies in its range. This lightning will extend to as many enemies as its max hits will allow it to, hitting the closest enemy to the initial target in a range of 12 at Level 0. These enemies will be stunned when hit, which stops them from moving. Boss and Stun Immunity enemies will only get slowed down instead.

At Level 2+, it gains smite, an ability activated when its meter seen in the upgrade menu is filled up by hitting multiple enemies. This will unleash thunder on the targeted enemy, dealing explosion damage to it.

The Tesla is an excellent option for stalling over a pretty large area, as its electric shocks can hold large crowds in place and give other towers more time to attack them, on top of dealing decent damage itself.
The Tesla has a placement limit of two per player.
Strategy: The Tesla can be an effective mid to late-game AOE tower due to its chaining and smite. While its range is rather average, its lightning has a high chain range, allowing it to chain to enemies that are very far away, though it still needs an enemy to attack in its main range for that to happen. Its shock allows it to keep enemies in its and other tower's range for longer, allowing it to deal more damage to them.

The Tesla is essentially a larger version of the Electroshocker, with a much higher chain radius, strong stuns and a smite explosion. It does however, have worse chain max hits, no defense melting and it is far more expensive.

This thunder creates an explosion, meaning it bypasses Defense, making the Tesla more effective against such enemies. saboteur.name: Saboteur
saboteur.description: The Saboteur is a poison-based tower bought for 7,500 Coins after triumphing Polluted Wasteland II or bought for 449 Robux.

Description: The Saboteur is a poison-based tower bought for 7,500 Coins after triumphing Polluted Wasteland II or bought for 449 Robux.

It fires in a manner similar to the Shotgunner. With each shot, multiple bullets come out of its spread gun. These shots are spread out and not guaranteed to all hit the same enemy. Additionally, it has a max hits stats which is used in its Scattershot. With it, the damage dealt by a pellet is done as many times as what the max hits is. For example, at Level 4, the max hits is 3, meaning each pellet deals damage three times to the enemy it hits. The max hits being 3 does not however mean it will only hit three enemies, as each of the 6 pellets can, even if this happens rarely, all hit a different enemy
With each shot, the Saboteur applies poison, which deals damage over time while also slowing enemies down. Unlike the Toxic Gunner however, it cannot melt Defense.

Starting from Level 3, it gains the Aggressive Toxins ability. When used, a cursor will appear allowing the Saboteur to throw a grenade anywhere in its range. This will apply the Neuralyzed attribute to the enemy, making towers target them while also increasing how much damage they receive. Enemies with Neuralyzed take priority over enemies with Aggro. This ability costs $500 to use.
The Saboteur has a placement limit of 8.
Ability: Throws a grenade at the selected area, applying Neuralyzed to them. This forces them to be targeted by towers while also boosting how much damage they receive.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Saboteur's decent DPS, low starting cost and support capabilities allows it to be useful throughout the entire match.

The Saboteur poisons any enemy it hits with its main attack, dealing additional damage over time. This poison also slows down enemies, allowing for the Saboteur to be a support tower from Level 0. If needed for the purpose of applying poison to as many enemies as possible, using targeting options like Random can allow it to hit as many enemies as possible, slowing down multiple enemies at once.

At Level 1, the Saboteur unlocks Scattershot, which makes it hit enemies more times based on how many targets were hit. While this is in a lot of situations, nearly the same as simply doubling or tripling the damage, there are a few notable cases where the Scattershot will do better or worse than just doubled damage. It hitting enemies more times means it will trigger effects like the fireworks from the Firework Technician or the crit from the Precision Skill more often than it would with just increased damage. This is especially notable for the Firework Technician, as the Saboteur can trigger fireworks way more often than most towers, especially at Level 4 where it hits enemies 18 times. Due to it hitting enemies more times, it will be more effective on Tank enemies, as upgrading from Level 0 to 1 will make it go from dealing 1 damage three times to dealing 1 damage six times. If the damage was simply doubled, these Levels would behave nearly identically against them.

The Saboteur can throw a grenade that forces any enemy hit by it to be targeted by towers, while also boosting how much damage they receive. This can be used to preemptively or immediately redirect firepower to a specific enemy or group of enemies without having to switch tower targeting. Notable examples of this include using the ability on Fallen Jester type enemies to kill them as soon as possible and prevent them from buffing other enemies. This ability should be used carefully, as if used on the wrong enemy, it could lead to hordes of other enemies getting past your defenses and cause a loss. Neuralyzed takes priority over Aggro, meaning it can be used to stop towers from having to target them. Enemies affected by this ability also receive more damage from towers. As this is not a Damage Buff, it functions differently and has different effects on towers. Unit damage is actually boosted by Neuralyzed, meaning towers like the Engineer, Military Base or Mercenary Base can have their units receive a boost in damage. While their attack damage does get boosted, the collision damage does not. This means units like the Rifleman are greatly affected while ones like the Riot Guard receive little to no change in their DPS. Damage over time from debuffs like chillness, burn, poison, sting or blood is affected by Neuralyzed. Because of this, the Saboteur can be used to boost the DPS of the Swarmer. Do note however that it does not boost the damage from a single stack (for example, 3 damage getting increased to 4 for a total of 120 damage) but instead boosts the total damage from each stack (for example, 90 damage from 30 stacks getting increased to 104 damage). The Slasher also greatly benefits from this. For example, against a 500,000 health enemy with no Defense, it normally deals 13,481 collapse damage. However, with a 15% Neuralyzed damage boost, it deals 15,504 damage instead. As the Neuralyzed effect is on the enemy itself, consumables are actually affected by it. For example, the Nuke will deal 86,250 damage to an enemy with a 15% Neuralyzed damage boost instead of the usual 75,000.

Do note however that it does not boost the damage from a single stack (for example, 3 damage getting increased to 4 for a total of 120 damage) but instead boosts the total damage from each stack (for example, 90 damage from 30 stacks getting increased to 104 damage).

The Slasher also greatly benefits from this. For example, against a 500,000 health enemy with no Defense, it normally deals 13,481 collapse damage. However, with a 15% Neuralyzed damage boost, it deals 15,504 damage instead.

As the Neuralyzed effect is on the enemy itself, consumables are actually affected by it. For example, the Nuke will deal 86,250 damage to an enemy with a 15% Neuralyzed damage boost instead of the usual 75,000.
Trivia: While not publicly released until the 22nd of April 2026, the Saboteur actually made an appearance in-game long before that point as it was used in Matchmaking for the PVP mode. This is because when first made, the Saboteur was a PVP -oriented tower, having mechanics specifically made for it, like stealing the opponent's health or paralyzing the opponent's towers. This concept was never properly released however.

minigunner.description: The Minigunner is a fast-firing advanced tower that can be purchased from the store for 8,000 Coins.

Description: The Minigunner is a fast-firing advanced tower that can be purchased from the store for 8,000 Coins.

Before the Minigunner starts firing, it needs to rev-up its M61 Vulcan. This process takes 1.4 seconds (1.2 at Level 1-2, 1 at Level 3+), and once it is fully revved up, it begins to shoot. If there are no more enemies in its range, it will wait for around a second for an enemy to re-enter its range before revving down requiring it to fully rev-up again. If an enemy enters its range during the process of revving down, the Minigunner will finish the rev-up process faster than normal. It has high DPS and a relatively low cost compared to other high DPS towers, like the Accelerator or Engineer. Additionally, there is no limit on the number of Minigunners that can be placed down during a game.

This is considered an all-round tower because it is affordable relatively early on but can deal fairly high damage at higher levels as well. While in regular modes, it has no placement limit, in PVP mode only twelve Minigunners can be placed per player.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Minigunner should be one of the towers that is placed down the most if brought in. it is recommended to place them in a large group near the start of the path if possible, or placing them in an area that covers a lot of the path (for example, at corners). Be careful when placing multiple Minigunners on the map when in teams, as this can block many vital spaces for stronger towers such as the Accelerator or Engineer. The DJ Booth and Commander are also integral support towers to be used with the Minigunner, especially with a Range Buff, as Minigunner lacks range for a DPS tower. Unlike other high DPS towers such as the Ranger and Turret, the Minigunner does not have a placement limit. If you still have space to place down more towers, the Minigunner is a great choice to further fortify your defenses.

Midway through the game, several Level 3-4 Minigunners are a cost-efficient option for wiping out hordes of enemies. The first Minigunners should be placed down in the transition to the mid-game, right when early game towers begin to struggle. Such instances include the debut waves of the Slow Boss and Necromancer.

If you plan to save up for the Minigunner during the early stages of the game, you should have teammates with reliable early game towers, such as the Golden Soldier, Golden Scout or Crook Boss to defend until you have gathered enough money to place it. You may also want to consider using the Farm to assist in getting an early game Minigunner, or alternative options such as using a Supply Drop, which grants you $1,000 instantly, or the Cowboy tower for passive income.

In terms of raw DPS, the Engineer, Accelerator and Ranger are far more effective. However, they are far more expensive and suffer from several limitations, making the Minigunner a far more flexible choice for some scenarios.

This tower is not affected much by the defense from enemies like the Fallen Giant and Warden due to its low base damage at lower levels. In most cases, the Minigunner can still deal most of its damage to such enemies, or even its full damage. Do note that the Levels 3 and 4 deal 7 and 15 damage respectively, which are high enough for most enemies with defense to be able to have a noticeable effect on its damage output. Even still, defense dropping towers like the Pyromancer are recommended to increase the damage of Minigunners against certain enemies with very high defense.

The Minigunner can serve as a cheap and effective way to wipe out Hidden enemies, like the Soul and Possessed Armor.
Trivia: When the game was in Alpha, and for a while after BETA release, the Minigunner's upgrade stats were not displayed on its upgrade description. It was simply referred to as "sans big gun".

Before the 13th of October 2019, when the Minigunner was Level 2 or higher, its face changed from the Roblox default face to the Grr! face, despite the fact that the upgrade icon kept the Roblox default face.
The Minigunner was inspired by Tower Battles' Commando as well as Team Fortress 2's Heavy.

Prior to the 8th of August 2019, the Level 5 upgrade was a jetpack. Functionally, it performed the same way as any other ground tower. Regardless of being a flying tower upon reaching that level, the hitbox of the Minigunner did not change with the jetpack. It could still be stunned by rocks from Tanks or the shockwave from the Gravekeeper.

ranger.name: Ranger
ranger.description: The Ranger, formerly known as the Outlaw, is an advanced cliff tower with long range that can be purchased in the store for 12,000 Coins.

Description: The Ranger, formerly known as the Outlaw, is an advanced cliff tower with long range that can be purchased in the store for 12,000 Coins.

The Ranger deals high damage with very long range but has a slow firerate. As a cliff tower, it can detect Flying enemies, but cannot detect hidden enemies at any level. The Ranger can also damage lead enemies at Level 2+. Additionally, it is immune to all stuns by default. At Level 2, it gains the ability to give towers a 10% Range Buff within its inner radius at the start of every wave for 20 seconds. At Level 4, it also deals splash damage through its Explosive Impact.

The Ranger deals extremely high damage at higher levels, but is expensive to upgrade to these levels. Due to these reasons, it is considered a mid-to-late game tower and is most effective for harder gamemodes.
The Ranger has a placement limit of eight per player.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Ranger is a cliff tower. Its viability changes depending on the map's available cliffs and their locations. It is important to know a map's layout before using the Ranger. Some maps, like Abandoned City, have many cliff spots in good locations, while others, like Dead Ahead have very few of them.
It is important to know a map's layout before using the Ranger. Some maps, like Abandoned City, have many cliff spots in good locations, while others, like Dead Ahead have very few of them.

Being a cliff tower, the Ranger is immune to almost all stuns. It is recommended to deal with enemies like the Fallen Honor Guard and especially bosses like the Fallen King and Molten Warlord. The Ranger is only not immune to some stuns from event enemies, like the Jack-o-Bot. However, it is not immune to debuffs.
The Ranger is only not immune to some stuns from event enemies, like the Jack-o-Bot.
However, it is not immune to debuffs.

The Ranger is a very expensive tower to use. As such, the Ranger should not be used as an early game option, due to its high cost and weakness against hordes. It should be reserved for mid-to-late game. Economy towers like the Farm or Golden Cowboy are highly recommended to afford the Ranger's expensive upgrades. The DJ Booth provides upgrade discounts, effectively making it cheaper to upgrade the Ranger.
Economy towers like the Farm or Golden Cowboy are highly recommended to afford the Ranger's expensive upgrades.
The DJ Booth provides upgrade discounts, effectively making it cheaper to upgrade the Ranger.

The Ranger grants a range boost to nearby towers at higher levels, so it is recommended to place towers near the Ranger. The Range Buff stacks with the DJ Booth 's. Other expensive towers like the Turret may not be as viable as you may not have enough cash to use both towers in tandem, though this depends on the gamemode and how you use your Farms and/or Cowboys. When a support tower, like the DJ Booth or Commander, is affected by this Range Buff, the towers in the buffed range will keep their buff even when the Range Buff ends, making it quite close to a permanent buff, which is especially useful for the DJ Booth. If a support tower is upgraded after the Range Buff ends, towers in the buffed range will not receive the stronger buff until the Range Buff is applied to the support tower again. Selling a support tower will remove the buffs from towers in the buffed range, even if the Range Buff is not active. For the Commander, the Call to Arms ability only affects towers in the buffed range while the Range Buff is active. If it not active, the Firerate Buff will not be applied to them, only making the passive Firerate Buff active.

The Ranger's slow firerate makes it struggle against some fast enemies and especially hordes. Towers with a fast firerate or towers that can damage multiple enemies at once should be used. The Commander should also be used to help boost the Ranger's firerate. The Ranger's firerate is heavily increased at Level 4, making it arguably even worse against hordes or fast enemies. Be wary of this when upgrading Rangers. The added splash damage somewhat makes up for this against enemies such as Breakers.

The Ranger has splash damage at Level 4, making it somewhat useful against hordes of enemies.

The Ranger should be set to Strongest in most scenarios to ensure it does its maximum damage. Beware of other weaker, but faster enemies that may slip through. Keeping some Rangers on First, or using other towers, is highly recommended.
Beware of other weaker, but faster enemies that may slip through. Keeping some Rangers on First, or using other towers, is highly recommended.
The Ranger has flying detection and lead detection, making it useful against enemies such as the Lead Balloon.

The Ranger does not have hidden detection, meaning it is ineffective against enemies like the Shadow Boss and Soul Boss. While the splash damage from Level 4 Rangers can indirectly damage them, it is usually too weak to have a major effect on them, requiring multiple Rangers as well as detectable enemies nearby. A Level 4+ Ace Pilot can grant it permanent hidden detection, but it must be close to do so. The Medic can be used to give it hidden detection and a Damage Buff with its Ubercharge ability. The UAV can grant it hidden detection plus extra range, but only for 30 seconds and with a limit of 4 uses. The Firework Technician can grant it temporary hidden detection as well as a firework attack, dealing extra damage. The Spotlight Tech can reveal Hidden enemies for the Ranger to shoot at.

Be incredibly wary of enemies that can slow the Ranger's firerate, such as Patient Zero, as the firerate will be slowed drastically.
Trivia: The Outlaw's purple laser used to make a unique zapping sound when fired.
The Ranger currently has the highest total damage per shot in the game.
The Ranger was loosely based on the Railgunner from Tower Battles.
The Ranger currently has the longest range of any publicly available tower in the game.
The Ranger currently has the highest firerate of any tower in the game.
When the Ranger was added, the game thumbnail called it the Space Outlaw even though it was only called Outlaw in the game.

Originally, the Ranger was meant to give hidden detection at the beginning of the wave. However, this was changed to a Range Buff when the Lunar Overture Update rework released. It is unknown if the hidden detection was only given to the Ranger itself or given to towers in its range like the Ace Pilot.

pursuit.description: The Pursuit is an advanced tower that can be bought for 15,000 Coins after reaching Level 100 or bought via a gamepass for 1,500 Robux. The Pursuit patrols a specified area, attacking any enemy that enters it that it can also see in its own range. The area it patrols can be changed with its Patrol ability. It also has two upgrade paths.

Description: The Pursuit is an advanced tower that can be bought for 15,000 Coins after reaching Level 100 or bought via a gamepass for 1,500 Robux. The Pursuit patrols a specified area, attacking any enemy that enters it that it can also see in its own range. The area it patrols can be changed with its Patrol ability. It also has two upgrade paths.

Once an enemy enters its range, it fires upon the enemy that fits its targeting, hovering in the air while it fires at the targeted enemy. It only stops firing when all enemies are killed, or all enemies have left its attacking area. It then resumes patrolling its range. It has a limited amount of ammo which, when it runs out, makes it reload.

At Level 3, the Pursuit gains the ability to fire missiles at enemies, which deal splash damage. The explosion is separated into two spheres. Enemies in the inner sphere will be dealt 100% of the stated damage, while the damage in the outer sphere decreases linearly. Additionally, the Pursuit's missiles can damage Lead enemies. The Pursuit's can also detect Flying enemies because it is an air-based tower. If upgraded to the bottom Level 4, it also can detect Hidden enemies.
The Pursuit is considered to be a mid to late-game tower due to its high DPS and splash damage capabilities, as well as its high cost.
The Pursuit has a placement limit of six per player. This is decreased to five in PVP mode.
Ability: Changes the position of its patrol range to the one selected by the player.
Strategy: As the Pursuit is an air-based tower, it is immune to all stuns. This makes it useful against enemies that can stun towers, like Molten Executioners, Fallen Honor Guards, Unstable Ices and bosses. As it is also not a humanoid tower, it is also immune to any debuffs from enemies prior to Lunar Overture Event, that being enemies like the Nuclear Monster or Soul Stealer.
As it is also not a humanoid tower, it is also immune to any debuffs from enemies prior to Lunar Overture Event, that being enemies like the Nuclear Monster or Soul Stealer.

At Level 3, the Pursuit gains missiles. These can be quite powerful, as they allow it to deal damage to multiple enemies at once. If you want to use the Pursuit's missiles for their area of effect capabilities, the bottom path upgrade is recommended as it focuses on missiles. Due to being explosives, they can bypass the defense of enemies such as Frost Hunters or Fallen Shields, and many other enemies with defense. While the top path's missiles are somewhat inconsistent due to their explosion size, the bottom path's explosion radius is far larger, rendering potential misses extremely unlikely.

The better buffs to apply to the Pursuit depend on the upgrade path you want to use the most. If you are going to use the top upgrade path, Firerate Buffs from towers like the Commander are recommended, as its main DPS comes from its guns. If you are going to use the bottom upgrade path, Damage Buffs from towers like the DJ Booth or Mercenary Base are recommended. As its main DPS comes from its missiles, which are not affected by Firerate Buffs, Damage Buffs are better here, as they can affect both the guns and the missiles. Regardless, both are still beneficial and, preferably, both should be applied.

Regardless, both are still beneficial and, preferably, both should be applied.

The missiles of the Pursuit can damage Lead enemies and both its guns and missiles detect Flying enemies. This, combined with its high DPS, makes it very useful against these enemies later on during the game. However, the Pursuit cannot directly attack Hidden enemies unless it is upgraded to Level 4 of the bottom upgrade path. It can only damage them indirectly if they are caught in its missile explosions otherwise. Due to the price of this upgrade, and the price of the Pursuit as a whole, it is not advised to rely on this for hidden detection early on.

Due to the price of this upgrade, and the price of the Pursuit as a whole, it is not advised to rely on this for hidden detection early on.
Do keep in mind that the Pursuit has an ammo system, which means it will need to reload after it has depleted its ammo bar.

The Pursuit's Patrol ability is very useful, as it gives the Pursuit effectively full map range and allows it to keep up with enemies that may escape from its range. Do note that, compared to the Pursuit's range, the cooldown on this ability is less than favorable for the top path, so using Patrol carefully is advised. This ability is even more effective in maps with lots of loops like Polluted Wasteland II and Honey Valley as the Pursuit will not need to be constantly moved. The Pursuit's patrol range is slightly bigger than it looks, as it extends to any area that the Pursuit can reach with its attack range. When using the Patrol ability, keeping this in mind can increase the amount of enemies Pursuit can cover.

Trivia: The Pursuit was teased on the 15th of May 2020 by BelowNatural in this tweet.
The Pursuit seems to be based on the Heli Pilot from the Bloons Tower Defense series.
Before its rework on the 27th of November 2024, the placement sound was taken from the Airstrike gear from the Roblox catalog.
Weirdly, the gamepass for the Pursuit used to be called Helicopter instead of Pursuit before 15th of April 2023.

The Pursuit is the first tower to have two upgrade paths, with previous towers having only one upgrade path. However, the Hacker was the first tower to originally come with two upgrade paths, as the Pursuit was an older tower with only one upgrade path prior to its rework in v1.43.0.

The Pursuit is the second tower to change the position in other maps without being sold, with the first being Brawler. However, unlike Brawler which can free space for other towers after being moved, the Pursuit's originally placed helipads still have a fixed position and cannot free up space until it is sold.

tooltips: An expensive and high damage dealing tower that occasionally fires AOE rockets. Can be ordered to patrol specific areas of the map to provide universal coverage.
Capable of targeting flying and lead enemies.

The Pursuit is an advanced tower that can be bought for 15,000 Coins after reaching Level 100 or bought via a gamepass for 1,500 Robux. The Pursuit patrols a specified area, attacking any enemy that enters it that it can also see in its own range. The area it patrols can be changed with its Patrol ability. It also has two upgrade paths.
