gatling_gun.name: Gatling Gun
gatling_gun.description: The Gatling Gun is an advanced tower that is able to be placed on both ground and cliffs, which can be controlled by the player using its ability. It can be bought for 35,000 Coins when the player has reached Level 175 or bought for 1,364 Robux.

Description: The Gatling Gun is an advanced tower that is able to be placed on both ground and cliffs, which can be controlled by the player using its ability. It can be bought for 35,000 Coins when the player has reached Level 175 or bought for 1,364 Robux.

The Gatling Gun will fire at any enemy in its range based on its targeting, hitting only one enemy. However, unlike most other towers, its range is actually a circular sector, which gets a larger angle with upgrades. When an enemy gets out of its range, it will not follow it, even if it could technically reach it if it moved. The Gatling Gun also has a limited amount of ammo. Every shot loses one ammo; it will not reload until it runs out of ammo; after that, it will take a few seconds for it to reload.

Its FPS (f irst- p erson s hooter) ability allows the player to control the Gatling Gun, which changes how the tower is used drastically. Most noticeably, the tower itself will no longer automatically shoot at enemies, and will only do so when the player shoots. The player can also reload at any point while the tower itself only does so when it runs out of ammo. The player does not have to manually reload when the tower runs out of ammo, as that still happens automatically. When firing, the bullets now pierce through enemies. The first two enemies receive full damage, while the third receives halved damage. If the damage is not a whole number, it is rounded up. Additionally, the player is not affected by any range statistics; the player can fire anywhere on the map, even if the Gatling Gun could not do it on its own. However, unlike the non-controlled Gatling Gun, the player cannot shoot through some obstacles, such as cliffs. Additionally, the player itself is affected by spread and recoil.

The Gatling Gun itself has flying detection from Level 0 and hidden detection from Level 3. When controlled by the player, it has both of these detections. The Gatling Gun also cannot be stunned, regardless if it is being controlled or not. It also cannot have debuffs applied to it if the enemy that applies it was added before the v1.9.0 update.
Due to the Gatling Gun's high base cost, extremely expensive upgrades, and high DPS, it is considered a mid-late game tower due to the placement limit of one.
There is a limit of one Gatling Gun per player.
Ability: Upon use, player gains control of the tower. Tower now needs to be fired by the player, though it gains the ability to pierce through enemies, hidden detection (if not at Level 3), no longer affected by range and is now affected by spread, recoil and obstacles on the map. Using the ability while the player is in control will remove control from the player.
Strategy: The Gatling Gun is one of the most expensive towers to place down and upgrade, making it impractical for early-game. Other, cheaper towers or consumables are recommended for early-game. Using income sources like the Cowboy, DJ Booth, Supply Drop or Farm is heavily recommended to be able to afford the Gatling Gun and its upgrades.
Other, cheaper towers or consumables are recommended for early-game.
Using income sources like the Cowboy, DJ Booth, Supply Drop or Farm is heavily recommended to be able to afford the Gatling Gun and its upgrades.

The Gatling Gun has a high DPS, making it great against high health targets. When controlled using its FPS ability, it is even better, as it can pierce through enemies, making it great against hordes of high health enemies.
When controlled using its FPS ability, it is even better, as it can pierce through enemies, making it great against hordes of high health enemies.

While its range is quite high, being the second highest in the game at Level 5-6, its range is in the shape of a circular sector, meaning its effectiveness is significantly reduced. This can be fixed by controlling it through its FPS ability, as you can attack enemies from any point of the map. However, it means you only have control of the tower and cannot do anything else. You can still use abilities that do not require you to choose a spot, such as the Commander 's Call to Arms or the DJ Booth 's Drop the Beat. However, abilities that require you to choose a spot such as Brawler 's Reposition or the Military Base 's Airstrike are disabled for the player during FPS ability. Taking control of the Gatling Gun, turning to face a desired spot, then releasing control allows for the player to influence where the Gatling Gun is aimed at. The Gatling Gun should be positioned so that will face a straight path, allowing for it to shoot for as long as possible if not controlled by a player. This additionally makes it easier to hit multiple enemies at once while controlling the Gatling Gun.

While controlling the Gatling Gun after using the FPS ability, it is not affected by the selected targeting. This makes it great against Aggro enemies, as you can target the enemy that you want to be targeted instead of being forced to target the Aggro enemy. It is recommended to target problematic enemies such as summoners like the Fallen Summoner or enemies that can buff other enemies like the Fallen Jester. This is also why the Gatling Gun is a good choice on multiplayer matches as it can handle some difficult enemies with ease.

The Gatling Gun can be placed on both cliff and ground spots, meaning it can be placed anywhere on the map. Both spots have their own benefits while using its ability. If placed on the ground, it is much easier to make use of its piercing, as you will be firing in a straight line. If placed on a cliff, it is less likely that you will be obstructed by objects on the map due to you being above them. Do note, however, that not all objects actually prevent the Gatling Gun from shooting at enemies, though they can obstruct the view.

Do note that while the tower itself can fire through objects of the map, you cannot fire through all of them. Consider if the spot you are placing the Gatling Gun in is obstructed by anything in any impactful way while placing it down. Some elements on the map may be able to be fired through, but will still obstruct the player's vision. Skilled users of the Gatling Gun can fire at enemies behind said cover even when they are not able to be directly seen. What can or cannot be fired through is not always intuitive, so knowledge is required to make the most of this quirk.

While the tower normally only reloads when it runs out of ammo, it can be reloaded manually at any time while controlled. It is recommended to reload manually whenever no enemies are spawning, which is usually the period of time between current wave ending and new wave starting. Manual reloads can also be performed if enemies are currently being blocked by map elements. Do be aware that the Level 5–6 Gatling Gun have a very long reload time, longer than even the period of time between waves. You can start a manual reload, then release control of the Gatling Gun to focus on other enemies. This is useful for multitasking.

The Gatling Gun has flying detection from Level 0, hidden detection from Level 3 if not controlled by player and from Level 0 if controlled by a player, making it great against such enemies that appear in the mid and late-game.
The Gatling Gun has a larger placement footprint than other towers, so be aware of the space that it takes up. This should not matter too much, as each player can only have one placed down.

The Gatling Gun can be very useful in Jailed Towers, as when it gets jailed while a player is using its FPS ability, the player will still be able to attack enemies with it. However, trying to use the FPS ability after it got jailed will result in it not working. The gun will visually fire, but no damage will be dealt and no ammo will be lost. Other controls like reloading are also unusable.

In FPS mode, the Gatling Gun has recoil, which means it is possible for some bullets to offshoot and not hit an enemy, something more glaring from Level 4+. A simple way to avoid this is to fire in bursts which will avoid too much recoil.
Trivia: The Gatling Gun is the first tower that can be placed both on ground and cliff spots. Despite this, the description of the Gatling Gun suggests that it can only be placed on cliffs, calling it a 'cliff tower'. It is also the first ever tower that can be controlled by a player.

The Gatling Gun is the fourth most expensive public tower to place down, being beaten by the Juggernaut by $4,750, Turret by $2,500 and the Accelerator by $2,250.

The Gatling Gun currently has the second highest total price of any public tower at a total cost of $213,250, being beaten by the Juggernaut. The Gatling Gun also has the fourth highest upgrade cost, with its Level 6 upgrade costing $100,000. Moreover, the Gatling Gun has the second most expensive Level 1 upgrade cost of $3,000, being beaten by Tesla by $1,314.

turret.name: Turret
turret.description: The Turret is an advanced tower with long range and high damage. It cannot be purchased from the store, instead unlocked at Level 50 or via its gamepass, priced at 340 Robux. When the player reaches Level 50, the Turret can be claimed using the pop up message that appears when joining the lobby.

Description: The Turret is an advanced tower with long range and high damage. It cannot be purchased from the store, instead unlocked at Level 50 or via its gamepass, priced at 340 Robux. When the player reaches Level 50, the Turret can be claimed using the pop up message that appears when joining the lobby.

The Turret excels at single target damage, boasting a strong mix of high range, damage and firerate. However, it is also very expensive. It costs $7,750 to place it down, the second most expensive starting cost for any tower. It takes a cumulative total of $149,000 to reach the max level, making it the third most expensive tower to fully upgrade in the entire game. In PVP mode, it does have reduced placement and upgrade costs, but it is still one of the most expensive towers to fully upgrade there. As the Turret is not a humanoid tower, it is immune to debuffs which are applied by enemies added before the v1.9.0 update. Debuffs from enemies like the Boomer can still affect it. This however does not make it immune to stuns. Additionally, it has a larger placement footprint than most other towers. It can detect hidden enemies and has lead detection.
Because of its extremely high base cost and very expensive upgrade prices, as well as high DPS, the Turret is considered a mid-late game tower.
The Turret has a placement limit of three per player. This is increased to five in PVP mode.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Turret has one of the most expensive starting costs for a tower, so it is impractical for the early-game. For the early-game, using cheaper towers is recommended. Using the Farm or Cowboy will allow you to place a Turret earlier, though, usually this is not recommended as there are better options than this.
For the early-game, using cheaper towers is recommended.
Using the Farm or Cowboy will allow you to place a Turret earlier, though, usually this is not recommended as there are better options than this.
The Turret has hidden detection by default and lead detection at Level 1, making it useful against enemies with these properties that may appear in the mid and late-game, especially in Hardcore mode.
The Turret has a larger placement footprint than other towers, so be aware of the space that it takes up.
It is highly recommended to pair the Turret with the DJ Booth to decrease the price of its extremely expensive upgrades. It can also be helpful at increasing its already large range.
It can also be helpful at increasing its already large range.

The Turret is immune to debuffs applied by legacy enemies. This includes the Soul Stealer 's Fatigue Debuff or the Gunslinger 's Scared Debuff. However, this does not include the Boomer or Necrotic Skeleton 's debuffs as they do not apply an icon to the tower. The Soul Stealer also cannot spawn a Soul from it, as the Fatigue Debuff is never applied.
The Soul Stealer also cannot spawn a Soul from it, as the Fatigue Debuff is never applied.

While the Turret does have a very high DPS, one of the highest in the entire game, it also has one of the lowest placement limits. Due to this, towers without limits like the Minigunner, Golden Minigunner, Swarmer or Golden Soldier can, if enough are placed down, deal more DPS than it. This is far less of an issue the more players there are in the match, as with player count the placement limit per player gets decreased, making towers with no limits far less viable while low placement limit towers like the Turret are completely unaffected.

Trivia: Strangely, the Void Reaver can still spawn a Soul from the Turret, which is not a humanoid tower unless the XR500 skin is equipped. The Soul Stealer cannot spawn a soul from the Turret unless it is the XR500 Turret. The Soul Stealer and legacy Fallen Soul also can only increase the firerate of the XR500 Turret, but not any other skins.

mortar.name: Mortar
mortar.description: The Mortar is an advanced cliff tower with a long range capable of damaging enemies with its explosions. It can be unlocked by reaching Level 75 or purchased via a gamepass for 300 Robux. When the player reaches Level 75, the Mortar can be claimed by using the pop-up message that appears when joining the lobby.

Description: The Mortar is an advanced cliff tower with a long range capable of damaging enemies with its explosions. It can be unlocked by reaching Level 75 or purchased via a gamepass for 300 Robux. When the player reaches Level 75, the Mortar can be claimed by using the pop-up message that appears when joining the lobby.

The Mortar is a cliff tower that shoots rather slowly but deals high damage over a large explosion radius. It has a long range, but as the Mortar shoots at a target farther away, the shells take longer to reach their target. These shells will generally land behind the targeted enemy. The explosion it produces is separated into two spheres; enemies in the inner sphere will be dealt 100% of the stated damage, while the damage in the outer sphere decreases linearly. At Level 4, when the Mortar's shells explode, they will drop three cluster bombs, which will create additional explosions when they hit the ground. These will land around the main explosion, meaning they are very unlikely to all hit and deal full damage to the targeted enemy. By default, the Mortar can damage Lead, as well as target all non-hidden flying enemies. The Mortar is immune to all stuns by default.

The Mortar is considered an all-round tower due to its relatively cheap placement cost, expensive upgrade prices, and its ability to effectively handle groups of enemies throughout the game thanks to its high area damage and strong overall damage output.
The Mortar has a placement limit of four per player. This is increased to five in PVP mode.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Mortar is essentially a cliff-based Rocketeer. However, the Mortar deals less single target damage without its cluster bombs (which are very unlikely to all deal full damage to the enemy) while having a significantly larger explosion. This makes the Mortar a better option against hordes.

In most cases, the Mortar's shells will land behind an enemy. This can be useful for hordes of enemies, as the Mortar's shells will land closer to the middle of the hordes instead of landing at the front. This allows its explosions to hit more enemies. However, this makes the Mortar somewhat weaker against single targets. As explosions will land behind an enemy, the enemy will be further away from the center of the explosion, which can reduce the amount of damage it receives. This is usually negligible for slow enemies, but for much faster ones like the Fallen Rusher, the Mortar's DPS may be reduced drastically.

At Level 4, the Mortar's shells drop cluster bombs when they explode. These cluster bombs will also explode when they hit the ground. However, do note that these should not be relied on, as the cluster bombs are very inaccurate and create a smaller explosion than the shells. At least 1 or 2 Level 5 Mortars can be efficient with taking out hordes of Breaker4s due to it being able to kill it in a single hit and its cluster bombs killing the Breaker3s that spawn.

Compared to the Ranger and Sniper, the Mortar has a significantly smaller range, lacking in range when cliff spots are far enough from the path. The DJ Booth can aid with this by boosting its range.

The Commander can help remedy the Mortar's slow firerate.

This tower has surprisingly good DPS for a splash damage tower, so it will also be able to help with major bosses like the Fallen King. Additionally, it can easily take care of their summons with its explosions.

The Mortar cannot detect Hidden enemies. You will have to use other towers for an effective Hidden defense. In most gamemodes, Hidden enemies are usually close to other enemies, so the Mortar can indirectly hit them with its large explosion radius. Towers like the Ace Pilot or Firework Technician can give hidden detection but must be close to the Mortar in order to do so.

Towers like the Ace Pilot or Firework Technician can give hidden detection but must be close to the Mortar in order to do so.
Large clumped groups that appear from Breaker4 can be better targeted by setting Mortar to Random.
This tower completely ignores defense, dealing full damage to the enemy. Because of this, it can be useful against hordes of enemies with defense, like Hazards, Reaver or Fallen Giant.
In Hardcore mode, the Mortar can be used to kill hordes of Lead enemies.
The Mortar can be an effective tower in certain maps where you can stack the Mortar to maximize the cliff spaces and free up more space for other cliff towers like the Ranger.
Trivia: Outside of sales, the Mortar is a Level 75 tower with a gamepass cost of 300 Robux, lower in Robux compared to the Turret which is a Level 50 tower with a gamepass cost of 340 Robux.
The Mortar is loosely based on the Mortar from Tower Battles and the Mortar Monkey from the Bloons Tower Defense series.

When the Mortar was first released, it would have been affected by shockwaves created by bosses from their Stomp abilities. This would later be fixed the same day. This glitch would later return in the Overhaul Update, though it only applied to the Grave Digger 's Stomp. This was later fixed in the Entity System Update.

The Mortar formerly shared its Level 4 icon with the Ace Pilot 's Level 2 icon, but rotated.
The Mortar has a unique explosion at Level 5. It will create a nuclear explosion, instead of the usual explosion most other splash towers use.
Unlike the game, dropping a shell in real life will spontaneously fire the mortar. In the game, Mortar drops in a shell after firing and waits for an enemy to come close to fire again.
The Mortar's default skin in the lobby uses its Hardcore Testing BETA appearance with its face changed, instead of its current appearance.

mercenary_base.name: Mercenary Base
mercenary_base.description: The Mercenary Base is an advanced tower unlocked at Level 150. It can also be bought for 945 Robux. It can spawn various units on the path within its range, which can deal damage to enemies or support other units. These units have varying strengths, spawnrates and purposes.

Description: The Mercenary Base is an advanced tower unlocked at Level 150. It can also be bought for 945 Robux. It can spawn various units on the path within its range, which can deal damage to enemies or support other units. These units have varying strengths, spawnrates and purposes.
At Level 0, it spawns the Rifleman, which is a basic burst unit that attacks similar to the Soldier. It gains hidden and flying detections at Level 3+.

At Level 1, it gains the ability to spawn the Grenadier, which deals splash damage, which works like most other splash damage towers. The explosion is separated into two spheres; enemies in the inner sphere will be dealt 100% of the stated damage, while the damage in the outer sphere is decreased linearly. Additionally, its explosions bypass defense. At Level 6, the Grenadier gains defense, letting it take less damage from collisions and enemy abilities.

At Level 4, it spawns the Riot Guard, which has a very high amount of health and high defense but rather low melee damage — its main form of damage is collision damage. It can hit multiple enemies with its attack, though as it requires them to be very close to each other, this does not happen often. When walking, the Riot Guard will slowly build up speed until it is running. While in this state, colliding with an enemy will damage and knock back the enemy. Bigger enemies will be pushed back a smaller distance than average-sized enemies. After colliding with or when near an enemy, the Riot Guard will remain in place to soak up more damage.

At Level 5, it can spawn the Field Medic, which does no damage to enemies, but can support multiple humanoid units within its range, healing them and giving them a shield. Healing works similar to damage, as it heals units by 15 (20 at Level 6) every 0.2 seconds.

At Level 3, the Mercenary Base grants towers in its range a 10% Damage Buff, which gets increased to 12.5% at Level 5 and 15% at Level 6. This Damage Buff does not affect all sources of damage. Additionally, while the in-game stat box suggests it allows towers to deal decimal damage, damage is rounded down instead.

At Level 5, it also gains the Air-Drop ability for $2,500, which spawns in the units from each of the three queues on the tower itself. This ability completely ignores the regular unit spawnrates and instead has its own cooldown. The units can be air-dropped anywhere on the path, making the tower more flexible.

The Mercenary Base has a placement limit of three per player. In PVP mode only, there is also a limit of 10 Riflemen per tower, 7 Grenadiers per tower, 4 Riot Guards per tower and 3 Field Medics per tower. This limit, however, does not work for the Field Medic and only Field Medic. For other units, if the limit is reached, no units will spawn when the spawnrate ends.

The Mercenary Base is considered a hybrid offensive-support tower that can be used in many ways. The Rifleman and Grenadier units provide solid damage throughout the game, while the Damage Buff the tower grants from Level 3 and onwards helps it support other high-DPS towers in the late-game. Additionally, the Riot Guard can be used as backup, and the Field Medic can support all units to give them extra survivability.
Ability: Drops the Mercenary Base's units on a selected area on the path.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: When first placed down, the Mercenary Base will instantly spawn the Rifleman, which fares quite well against early game enemies. This can make it useful for early-game, though do note it is quite expensive at the placement cost of $2,750, which makes other towers much better while at a lower cost.
This can make it useful for early-game, though do note it is quite expensive at the placement cost of $2,750, which makes other towers much better while at a lower cost.

Unlike other spawning towers, the Mercenary Base must be placed by the path in order to spawn units without the use of the Air-Drop ability. It is recommended to place the tower down near the back but also near other towers, as it gives the units more time to attack enemies and allows the Mercenary Base to boost the damage of towers. This is especially important for Riot Guards, as when they speed up they can become quite fast, making them get to the entrance quite quickly if the Mercenary Base is placed close to it. Do note that the Mercenary Base has a large placement footprint, which can be especially an issue on maps with little ground space, such as Forgetten Docks or Construction Crazy.

The DJ Booth can be used to reduce the ability usage cost. You can quickly change the units in the queue specifically for the Air-Drop and then change them back to what they were before, making the Air-Drop send out the units you need while not affecting the unit queue.

Solo had a placement limit of 3, duo was set to 2, while trio and quad had a limit of 1. This was removed on the 23rd of October 2024, where its placement limit was changed to be always 3 for all player counts.

brawler.name: Brawler
brawler.description: The Brawler is a hardcore melee tower that attacks enemies with its mechanical fists. It can be purchased from the store for 1,250 Gems and has a level requirement of Level 50.

Description: The Brawler is a hardcore melee tower that attacks enemies with its mechanical fists. It can be purchased from the store for 1,250 Gems and has a level requirement of Level 50.

The Brawler attacks enemies with its mechanical fists, dealing damage. At Level 2, it gains the ability to combo its attacks, making it attack enemies in a burst of three continuous attacks, which ends in a cooldown. The burst does not restart if there are no more enemies in its range. For example, if it lands two hits on enemies and stops attacking, the next hit will be a final hit. The final hit from a combo will deal increased damage and knock back enemies. The enemy is not always pushed back the same distance, as this is determined by its size. Larger enemies will be pushed back less than an average-sized enemy. Knockback has a 3 second long cooldown before it can be applied again.

The Brawler also has a unique ability where it can change its current position into one which the player can select. However, this ability has a cooldown of thirty seconds. Upon landing, it will create a shockwave that deals a decent amount of damage to enemies and knocks them back. Uniquely, the Reposition ability can damage Flying enemies.
The Brawler is considered an all-round tower due to its cheap placement cost, good DPS, and ability to knockback enemies from Level 2+.
The Brawler has a placement limit of ten per player. This is decreased to six in PVP mode.
Ability: Leaps to the selected area on the map, changing its placement spot. Additionally, the Brawler will knockback to up to 20 enemies on its landing position with a knockback force of 25 within 7.5 reposition range at Level 3 (10 at Level 4), and will deal area damage in that range.

Leaps to the selected area on the map, changing its placement spot. Additionally, the Brawler will knockback to up to 20 enemies on its landing position with a knockback force of 25 within 10 reposition range, and will deal area damage in that range.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Brawler can be an efficient tower early on during the game. For hordes of weaker enemies, a few Level 0 Brawlers can quite efficiently clear out hordes of enemies. For singular, high health enemies, the Level 2 Brawler can be effective at killing them and slowing them down, giving your Brawlers and other towers more time to kill it.
For hordes of weaker enemies, a few Level 0 Brawlers can quite efficiently clear out hordes of enemies.
For singular, high health enemies, the Level 2 Brawler can be effective at killing them and slowing them down, giving your Brawlers and other towers more time to kill it.

The Brawler at Level 2+ knocks back on the third hit, making it useful at slowing down enemies. Enemies immune to stun are not affected, as Stun Immunity prevents them from being knocked back. Additionally, larger enemies will be pushed back less than average-sized enemies. At Level 4, it gains the Reposition ability, which allows it to knock back enemies in a large area, If there is only a single targetable enemy, the Brawler is capable of constantly knocking it back, preventing it from progressing further.

If there is only a single targetable enemy, the Brawler is capable of constantly knocking it back, preventing it from progressing further.
The Brawler has lead detection at Level 0, making it effective against lead enemies.
The Brawler cannot be stunned by any enemy, making it quite useful against enemies like the Warden or Fallen Guardian.
Due to the Brawler's Reposition ability, it is likely that it will often get out of range of buffing towers, making them much less effective.

The Brawler's Reposition ability, starting from Level 4, can easily take out hordes of weaker enemies. The ability can also hit Flying enemies, making Brawler quite effective for taking out hordes of Balloons and Balloon Kids faster. Also do note that this ability has a cooldown of 30 seconds, and Flying enemies will not be knocked back.

Also do note that this ability has a cooldown of 30 seconds, and Flying enemies will not be knocked back.
Due to its pretty high DPS, Stun Immunity and the Reposition ability, the Brawler can actually do well against major bosses like the Molten Warlord unlike most other low range towers.
The Brawler has a small placement footprint, allowing it to squeeze in beside other towers easily.
Unlike other melee towers, the Brawler is not hitbox reliant, which means it can fully utilize Range Buffs.
Trivia: The Brawler is the first tower that can change its position on the map without being sold, the second being Pursuit.
The Brawler is canonically Engineer 's brother.
The Brawler is the cheapest tower to unlock with {Gem} Gems.
The Brawler trains with the Assassin and Slasher, as revealed in Blind Faith.
The Brawler level 4 upgrade name; GALVAKNUCKLES, is a reference to the Galvaknuckles from the Call of Duty series.
The Level 5 upgrade name is a reference to Boreas' Fury from the Call of Duty series.
Update History: For previous cosmetic variations, see the gallery page.

The Brawler is a hardcore melee tower that attacks enemies with its mechanical fists. It can be purchased from the store for 1,250 Gems and has a level requirement of Level 50.

necromancer.name: Necromancer
necromancer.description: The Necromancer is a hardcore spawner tower that can be unlocked in the store for 2,250 Gems and has a level requirement of Level 50. It could have also been obtained through a gamepass for 1,500 Robux.

Description: The Necromancer is a hardcore spawner tower that can be unlocked in the store for 2,250 Gems and has a level requirement of Level 50. It could have also been obtained through a gamepass for 1,500 Robux.

The Necromancer fires magic bolts at enemies. At Level 4, these are replaced by beams fired from its book, which are not projectiles. This makes it now lock on enemies, meaning it will not change what enemy it is targeting until the current enemy moves out of range or is killed. These beams deal damage based on the number of enemies targeted. For example, if it only targets one enemy, it will deal 30 damage, 45 damage when targeting two enemies, and 90 damage when targeting three enemies. The Necromancer also has a soul meter of 105, which it fills up by damaging enemies. When the soul meter is full, the Necromancer will summon gravestones. The Necromancer can destroy these gravestones using its Raise the Dead ability. The Necromancer will summon gravestones until it reaches the limit at that level. At Level 3, the Necromancer can now upgrade gravestones. After dealing enough damage it will upgrade the gravestones, regardless of whether they are currently placed down or not. Upgraded gravestones summon stronger units. At Level 4, these gravestones can also deal damage when destroyed. This is done through an explosion which has damage fall off, though it can only hit up to three enemies per explosion.

The units spawned depend on the Level of the tower and the gravestone. At Level 0, Level 1 gravestones can only spawn Skeletons, at Level 1, Level 1 gravestones gain the ability to summon Sword Skeletons. At Level 2, Level 1 gravestones gain the ability to summon Giant Skeletons. At Level 3, gravestones can be upgraded to Level 2, where they spawn Skeletons, Skeleton Knights, Hallow Guards and Giant Skeletons. At Level 4, gravestones can be upgraded to Level 3, where they spawn Skeleton Knights, Hallow Guards and Executioner Skeletons. The units that spawn from gravestones are random, with each unit having a chance of being summoned, though once the gravestones are at their final Level and they are all placed down, the summoned units will always be the same, based on the limits set for them at a specific Necromancer level.
The Necromancer has a placement limit of three per player.
Ability: Destroys all its graves, summoning units based on the gravestone level.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: Placement is important for the Necromancer, because of the way it spawns gravestones. The Necromancer needs to be placed next to the path so that it can summon gravestones, so you might not be able to utilize the most of its range. It is best to bring the Necromancer on maps with long paths, as it can often cover the entire map while placed at the back. This allows the Necromancer to stack its units more easily and fill its Soul Meter more quickly, as it will be continuously attacking at all times with full map range. Maps like Honey Valley, Polluted Wasteland II, and more, allow the Necromancer to fully utilize the potential DPS of its units, and itself.

The Necromancer stops attacking while summoning gravestones, making it unable to attack for a while. This does not happen when the Necromancer upgrades gravestones. This makes it unable to defend by itself, as hordes of fast enemies like the Bolt or Fallen could get out of its range fairly easily. Thus, bringing in reliable towers like the Minigunner will help avoid this issue.

The Necromancer's Raise the Dead ability can be used to summon various skeletons, which get quite powerful at later levels. It is recommended to wait until gravestones are at their higher level so that it spawns its strongest units. The units that spawn have determined limits, meaning that once the maximum amount of gravestones are upgraded to their final level, the summoned units will be the same every single time. If the gravestones are not fully upgraded, the summons will still be random. At Level 4, the Level 3 gravestones explode when you activate the ability, which can make them useful as traps to take down groups of weaker enemies and chip the health down of stronger ones.

Units spawned by the Necromancer, especially at higher levels, have high health, making them useful against crowds of enemies. The Executioner Skeleton 's axe also deals piercing damage, rapidly dealing damage to any enemy caught by it, though its high firerate and the far distance that its axe travels make it quite inconsistent.

The Necromancer has flying detection at Level 0, which can make it fairly useful against flying enemies, and while it does not have hidden detection until Level 2, some of its units can detect Hidden enemies and all of them can deal damage to them, making it still useful against Hidden enemies before being upgraded to Level 2. At Level 4, it also gets lead detection, making it useable against Lead enemies. You should not solely rely on the Necromancer for these two traits alone, however; there are better and cheaper alternatives such as Ace Pilot, Militant, and Golden Crook Boss. That being said, the Necromancer's pierce and high damage makes it great against hordes of Hiddens and Balloons, only slightly compounded by its slow firerate. At Level 4, it can do quite well against groups of Hidden Bosses along with supplementary damage with its ability.

The Necromancer is quite expensive to upgrade. Because of this, towers like the Farm or Cowboy are recommended to afford them more easily. The DJ Booth can also be helpful at reducing its upgrade costs.
The DJ Booth can also be helpful at reducing its upgrade costs.
As its units provide it with a huge increase in DPS, having support towers that make upgrading gravestones faster is recommended with this tower.

The Necromancer can pair up well with the Mercenary Base, because its Field Medics can heal multiple skeletons. This is particularly useful for the Executioner Skeleton as its primary attack is ranged. Additionally, its Damage Buff can be useful at boosting the Necromancer's damage, increasing its DPS and making it build graves faster.

Try stacking Executioner Skeletons on the map. To do this, wait for the Necromancer to place down its gravestones, and check if most of them have reached their max level. Once most of the gravestones are at max level, use the Raise the Dead ability. Repeat this process continuously. Certain maps, like Honey Valley, are better for stacking, as the Executioner Skeletons can be both summoned far away from the entrance while also having enemies in range for most of the time, delaying them from reaching the entrance as much as possible. This allows the Necromancer to reach its full potential DPS by stacking the various units from its gravestones. The units can also deal a lot of damage by ramming into enemies, such as the Hallow Guard and Executioner Skeleton.

Trivia: A Necromancer tower was originally planned to be added for the Halloween 2020 Event, however, it was replaced with the Toxic Gunner to avoid potential drama due to the tower being similar to the Graveyard tower from Tower Battles.
The Necromancer was the first non-hardcore tower to be obtainable for {Gem} Gems.

Originally, the Necromancer was planned to be only available every Halloween, though during the Lunar Overture Event, it was on sale until 2nd of December 2023. However, due to a bug, it returned on 21st of December 2023 and was present in the store since. An update on the 15th of January 2025 made the Necromancer a hardcore tower, now officially making it permanent rather than a bug. Because of this, the Necromancer was considered an event tower and put in the Exclusive category.

The Necromancer's beam attack at Level 4 shares a visual resemblance to the Plasma Trooper 's attack from Tower Battles.
The original Necromancer Level 4 upgrade name is a reference to the Darkhold from the Marvel Comics.

The Necromancer was planned to be the final reward for the Lunar Overture Season Pass, but was later changed to only be obtainable via purchasing with gems on the shop, as BelowNatural stated it would have been " too easy " to obtain it from the Season Pass.
The Necromancer was originally meant to deal splash damage, but this was changed to pierce for unknown reasons.

accelerator.name: Accelerator
accelerator.description: The Accelerator is a hardcore tower that attacks in delayed bursts. It has a charge-up that happens before the burst and a cooldown that happens after the burst. During the burst, it can deal massive amounts of damage in a short period of time, but does no damage in between bursts. It can be purchased from the store for 2,500 Gems and has a level requirement of Level 50.

Description: The Accelerator is a hardcore tower that attacks in delayed bursts. It has a charge-up that happens before the burst and a cooldown that happens after the burst. During the burst, it can deal massive amounts of damage in a short period of time, but does no damage in between bursts. It can be purchased from the store for 2,500 Gems and has a level requirement of Level 50.

The Accelerator must charge-up its plasma gun before it can attack enemies. During its attack, it will fire in quick, high-damaging bursts, remaining focused on one enemy until it is killed, leaves the Accelerator's range, or the overcharge ends. The Accelerator will deal a set amount of damage before cooling down with its left hand, indicating that the plasma gun has overcharged. After this, there will be a cooldown lasting a couple of seconds, after which it charges up again. The amount of damage needed for the Accelerator to overcharge can be seen above its tower icon in the upgrade box or when you hover your cursor over it. Damage can still go above this threshold, though the Accelerator will stop attacking immediately once it does so. For example, if the Accelerator deals 8,999 damage out of 9,000 and has 10 damage, it will deal 9,009 damage total in that burst, assuming the enemy it attacks has at least 10 health. The Accelerator can also damage Lead enemies from Level 0 and detect Hidden enemies from Level 1.
The Accelerator is considered a mid to late-game tower because of its high damage capabilities, but extremely high cost.
The Accelerator has a placement limit of five per player. This is increased to eight in PVP mode.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: Multiple Level 2 Accelerators are a cost-efficient way to get through the mid-game, as their DPS is usually high enough to deal with most mid-game enemies. The Farm or other towers that generate income like the Golden Cowboy are strongly recommended, as the Accelerator's upgrades are very expensive, especially its later upgrades. To further decrease the cost of Accelerator's upgrades, the DJ Booth is a very great choice due to its discount buff.

The Farm or other towers that generate income like the Golden Cowboy are strongly recommended, as the Accelerator's upgrades are very expensive, especially its later upgrades. To further decrease the cost of Accelerator's upgrades, the DJ Booth is a very great choice due to its discount buff.

The Accelerator has a very long overcharge before having to recharge, therefore buffs from the Commander, DJ Booth, Medic or Mercenary Base are usually fully effective on it. The DJ Booth 's purple track can still be helpful in boosting its already massive range.
The DJ Booth 's purple track can still be helpful in boosting its already massive range.

The Accelerator's lock-on mechanic can be a disadvantage. For example, if the Accelerator locks onto a strong enemy like the Fallen Giant, it will stay locked on until the strong enemy is defeated, leaves its range or the Accelerator charges up again. This can result in the Accelerator leaking other enemies while it is distracted, therefore it is highly recommended to bring other towers to deal with such.
This can result in the Accelerator leaking other enemies while it is distracted, therefore it is highly recommended to bring other towers to deal with such.

The Accelerator's lengthy charge-up and cooldown times hinder it greatly, with enemies getting out of range before the Accelerator can defeat them in the worst cases. It is important to utilize other towers alongside the Accelerator to prevent any potential leaks. Due to this and other factors, such as its high cost, it is generally infeasible to use the Accelerator in the early game, with its sluggish charge-up at lower levels resulting in some fast enemies leaking.

Due to this and other factors, such as its high cost, it is generally infeasible to use the Accelerator in the early game, with its sluggish charge-up at lower levels resulting in some fast enemies leaking.
The Accelerator should be allowed to cover large amounts of the path to maximize its DPS. The DJ Booth and Ranger are especially great in this regard for boosting the Accelerator's range.
Slowing towers like the Electroshocker or Cryomancer can be used to support the Accelerator, slowing the enemy down and giving the Accelerator enough time to charge-up and attack them.
Trivia: The Accelerator is loosely based on the Sparky from Clash Royale. The Accelerator's plasma gun is loosely based on the Gluon Gun from Half-Life.
The Accelerator's plasma gun is loosely based on the Gluon Gun from Half-Life.

Prior to the 12th of March 2022, the Accelerator was the only tower that could receive cash from summoned enemies. After the update, the Accelerator is no longer able to receive cash from these enemies in most gamemodes.

The Accelerator used to have hidden detection at Level 0; however, as of the Unwavering Tides Update this is no longer the case. Currently, the Golden Pyromancer, Turret and Gladiator are the only towers with hidden detection at Level 0. Prior to the Overhaul Update, the only towers to have hidden detection at Level 0 were the Outlaw and Paintballer.

The Accelerator is a hardcore tower that attacks in delayed bursts. It has a charge-up that happens before the burst and a cooldown that happens after the burst. During the burst, it can deal massive amounts of damage in a short period of time, but does no damage in between bursts. It can be purchased from the store for 2,500 Gems and has a level requirement of Level 50.

engineer.description: The Engineer is a hardcore tower that attacks enemies with a rebar launcher and can build various sentries within its range to assist with defense. It can be purchased from the store for 4,500 Gems and has a level requirement of Level 50. The Engineer is also available through a gamepass for 1,267 Robux.

Description: The Engineer is a hardcore tower that attacks enemies with a rebar launcher and can build various sentries within its range to assist with defense. It can be purchased from the store for 4,500 Gems and has a level requirement of Level 50. The Engineer is also available through a gamepass for 1,267 Robux.

The Engineer has three range rings: the white ring is the attack range of the Engineer, the yellow ring is the placement range for sentries, and the red ring is the deadzone range in which the Engineer cannot fire nor build sentries. The Engineer collects scrap when damaging enemies, with the amount of scrap obtained per shot being equivalent to the damage dealt to an enemy. The scrap fills up its Scrap Meter, which can be seen above its tower icon in the upgrade box or when the player hovers over it. When its Scrap Meter is full, the Engineer will briefly stop attacking to build a sentry. Within upgrades, the Engineer will build stronger sentries, however, they will require more scrap to be built. If the Scrap Meter is filled up but the maximum number of sentries are placed, the Engineer will wait until a sentry is despawned or destroyed before building another sentry. There is a limit to how many sentries can be built.

Sentries built by the Engineer are considered units, though they cannot move and can only be placed on the ground in the yellow range ring. They do have health however, which drains over time or decreases when hit by an enemy ability that deals damage, limiting the amount of time they can stay alive. The amount left before a sentry despawns can be seen with the duration bar above a sentry.
The Engineer is considered an all-round tower due to its cheap placement cost, decent DPS on early levels and very expensive upgrades with extremely high DPS later on.
The Engineer has a placement limit of six per player. This is reduced to five in PVP mode.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Engineer is a powerful late-game tower, as its DPS combined with its maximum number of sentries is one of the highest in the entire game. Since its sentries have a shield that makes them immune to damage, it can also be powerful against major bosses like the Frost Spirit. Do note that the shield is only active when the Engineer is not stunned. It is possible to shield the Engineer with the Medic, which means that for its sentries to be destroyed there need to be three attacks that damage units and stun towers in a row.

The Engineer can be used as an early game tower due to its decent DPS and sentry DPS and its cheap cost. Since the Engineer has flying detection and lead detection, it can also be used as an early game tower in Hardcore mode. Placing multiple Level 2 Engineers is cost-effective due to its ability to place Rifle Sentries.

The sentries are not affected by any buffs or debuffs, but the Engineer is still affected by all of them. The explosion damage from the War Machine Sentry is affected by buffs, though this is a bug.

Due to how expensive the Engineer is, the DJ Booth is highly recommended, as it can greatly decrease the Engineer's cost. It can also be useful for increasing the Engineer's attack range. Neither the sentry building range nor the deadzone range will be affected.

The Engineer needs to fill its Scrap Meter before it can build a sentry, which it can fill up by dealing damage to enemies. Using the Commander, you can summon sentries faster since the damage is dealt faster. The Mercenary Base and DJ Booth can also increase its damage, which also affects its Scrap Meter, allowing it to summon sentries even faster. The Field Medic cannot heal or shield the Engineer's sentries, as they are not considered humanoids. It is recommended to set the Engineer's targeting to Strongest to fill its Scrap Meter faster due to the higher damage dealt and minimal damage wasted. Do note that when the Engineer is building a sentry, it is unable to attack for a short while, allowing enemies to pass through, especially hidden enemies. This is not an issue on later levels as the Engineer can have more than a single sentry. Having other towers alongside the Engineer can also help mitigate this issue.

The Engineer went through multiple changes before being released. Rather than using a rebar launcher, it wielded a pistol, which, with levels, would be replaced with various rifles. The Engineer had five sentries instead of four, which had different purposes. The first three sentries were single target sentries, which would only deal damage to one enemy. These sentries are still in the game, with them being the Sentry, Rifle Sentry and Minigun Sentry. The fourth sentry was the Missile Sentry, which was a quad missile launcher that would deal splash damage. The fifth and last sentry was the Support Beacon, which would reveal hidden enemies in its range. Due to there being multiple types of sentries, you would be able to pick what kind of sentries the Engineer would place.

tooltips: A well-rounded tower that takes time to ramp up and build its turrets but can create a strong defensive line with great coverage once its turrets are setup.
Capable of detecting hidden, lead, and flying enemies.

The Engineer is a hardcore tower that attacks enemies with a rebar launcher and can build various sentries within its range to assist with defense. It can be purchased from the store for 4,500 Gems and has a level requirement of Level 50. The Engineer is also available through a gamepass for 1,267 Robux.

hacker.name: Hacker
hacker.description: The Hacker is a hardcore tower that hacks enemies, applying various effects to them. It can be purchased from the store for 5,500 Gems or through a gamepass for 1,574 Robux.

Description: The Hacker is a hardcore tower that hacks enemies, applying various effects to them. It can be purchased from the store for 5,500 Gems or through a gamepass for 1,574 Robux.

It damages enemies using synapses fired from its equipment, which starts off with a smartphone, then some sort of wrist gadget and in the bottom path, a laptop. These beams target a single enemy, dealing single target damage. Any enemy attacked by the Hacker will have these effects applied to it:

First hack is Unit Conversion, unlocked at Level 0. When the enemy is killed, it will be converted into a hologram, with reduced health. This hologram will function similarly to a unit, dealing damage to an enemy upon collision. The converted enemy will ignore defense and Tank of the enemy it is colliding with. If the converted enemy has defense, this defense will boost the damage it deals to other enemies. Bloated does also boost the health of such enemies. Boss enemies are unable to be converted into holograms. Enemy health is calculated using their max health and the tower's EV. Health is calculated as: Max Health EV
Second hack is Wire Fraud. Enemies targeted by the Hacker will have their rewards on death or damage increased. This is a global boost, meaning everyone in the match receives the added income.
Third hack is Slowness. This applies a slowness effect to any enemy, as long as it is not a Boss enemy.

The Hacker also has an ability, Hologram Tower, which allows it to duplicate a tower. It can duplicate any tower on the map and place it down in any spot. This tower will last for a limited amount of time and disappear once the lifetime ends. The cloned tower will have the hologram modifier on it. The ability has a varying cost based on the total cost of the cloned tower. Hacker cannot clone other Hackers or itself. If a cloned tower has a placement limit, then there can only be as many clones of that tower from one player at a time as its placement limit. For example, the Gatling Gun can only have one clone from a player at a time due to the tower having a placement limit of one.
The Hacker has hidden detection from Level 2. It has a placement limit of two per player.
Ability: Clones a tower after the drone has selected via the ability. Cost varies based on the total cost of the tower and the Hacker's Level.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: Duplicate towers with low placement limits, such as the Juggernaut, Turret, Necromancer, DJ Booth or Gatling Gun for the most value. Do note however that the lifespan of cloned towers are very short. This makes the bottom path ideal for this, as it has the longest clone lifespans. Additionally, due to the cooldown being 60 seconds, it is possible to have more than 1 clone. This can be further improved by using the Skill Accelerator to reduce the cooldown to 52.5 seconds. The DJ Booth can help by reducing tower costs, making them effectively cheaper to clone.

The Hacker will convert any enemy it is targeting into a hologram, dealing collision damage to enemies. Top path is preferred for this, as its high DPS and stronger EV allows it to create stronger enemies. This is most useful in modes where a large number of high health enemies are present, most preferably Polluted Wasteland II. As enemies only need to be targeted by the Hacker to be converted, it is recommended to have towers with high DPS, such as the Accelerator, damage the enemies in order to convert them faster. These enemies will bypass defense and Tank. However, they cannot damage Flying or Ghost enemies. If an enemy has defense, that defense will boost how much damage they deal. Because of this, do be aware when using defense dropping towers with the Hacker. While they will make converting enemies faster, they will also reduce the damage dealt.

While majority of enemies will still perform their on death abilities, some of them will be partially or fully negated. For example, the Breaker4 will only summon one Breaker3 on death when converted instead of three. Some enemies can have their second phase cancelled by the Hacker. For example, the Abomination will be converted over before it changes into the Reanimated.

The Hacker can be used to slow down enemies, making it easier to kill them. Bottom path is best for this, as it has a far better slowness than top path. Only Boss enemies are immune to this slowdown. Additionally, its slowness can stack with other towers, which means, combined with the Toxic Gunner and Harvester 's thorns, they can slow down every non-boss enemy by up to 95%.

The Hacker can be used to boost cash gained from enemies, allowing for easier cash generation. Bottom path is best for this, as it boosts the cash gained far more than top path.

To utilize the Hacker's high potential for dealing with crowds, set each Hacker’s targeting to Strongest and Weakest, respectively.
Setting the Hacker to Weakest can ensure that the tower will target and kill enemies on low health.

When using Firework Technician, each Synapses has their own chance to proc fireworks, resulting in the Hacker being way more likely to generate one. This can be helpful for bottom path Hacker to make up for its lower DPS.

Trivia: The Hacker’s Level 4 upgrade name is a reference to the Intel Core i9 processor. The string of numbers "3260590327" is the Place ID of Tower Defense Simulator on Roblox.

The Hacker was first teased all the way back in 2020, but did not make an appearance until the 11th of June 2025 in v1.67.0.

Bottom path Hacker has the second worst cost efficiency in the entire game, beaten by Swarmer at $5,800. However, the Swarmer can reach higher cost efficiency with all its bee stacks applied than the Hacker with all of its synapses accounted for.

The Hacker is the only Hardcore tower at the time of Null & Void to not receive a null enemy variant.

operator.description: The Operator, internally referred to as EvolvedOperator, is the evolved version of the Scout, unlocked by reaching Level 20 on the Scout tower, either by getting the experience or by skipping the need to get it by paying 499 Robux. Once done, it can be bought for 4,500 Gems and 15,000 Coins. As it is an evolved tower, only some of its upgrades are unlocked at the start. Description: The Operator, internally referred to as EvolvedOperator, is the evolved version of the Scout, unlocked by reaching Level 20 on the Scout tower, either by getting the experience or by skipping the need to get it by paying 499 Robux. Once done, it can be bought for 4,500 Gems and 15,000 Coins. As it is an evolved tower, only some of its upgrades are unlocked at the start. All other have to be unlocked by reaching higher evolution levels on the tower.

The Operator fires in bursts, with a moderate delay between each one. Starting from Level 2, it gains a Coordination damage buff for each Operator that has Coordination unlocked placed to it in a small radius. At Level 5, it gains Shared Optics, which lets it attack enemies in the range of another Operator with Shared Optics that is in its range. If the Operator in its range has other Operators in their range, then it will be able to fire from these Operator ranges too.
The Operator has hidden detection from Level 1 and flying detection from Level 2. It has a placement limit of 16.
Strategy: The Operator is best used in the early to mid-game.

At Level 2, it gains Coordination, which makes it apply and receive a damage boost from other nearby Operators that have Coordination. The area in which it is applied is very small, meaning the tower has to be placed in a tight group for this to work well.
The area in which it is applied is very small, meaning the tower has to be placed in a tight group for this to work well.

At Level 5, it gains Shared Optics, which will make it target enemies in the range of other Operators with Shared Optics in its range. This slightly conflicts with its Coordination, as that requires Operators to be placed close to each other while Shared Optics benefits from them being spread out. One way to benefit from both is to have one main group of Operators where one of them can see an Operator that is at the edge of their range, extending all their ranges. Afterwards, another Operator can be put in the range of the one at the edge, extending it even further. This can be repeated until you hit the placement limit. Another method is to have a few groups of Operators placed together apart from each other, but close enough that one group has another group in its range.

Trivia: The Operator is one of the first three evolved towers revealed in 2020 prior to the release of the Overhaul Update, the other two being Juggernaut and Kingpin.
The Operator's Level 3 design and upgrade name may be a reference to Robocop.
The Operator's Level 6 upgrade name, 1000-THR E.M is a reference to the name of the 1000-THR Earthmover from ULTRAKILL The Level 6 mask design is also possibly based on it.

The Operator's Level 4 upgrade name, Threat Detection Sentinel, can be abbreviated to TDS, which happens to be the abbreviation for Tower Defense Simulator.

enforcer.description: The Enforcer, internally referred to as EvolvedEnforcer, is the evolved version of the Shotgunner, unlocked by reaching Level 20 on the Shotgunner tower, either by getting the experience or by skipping the need to get it by paying 499 Robux. Once done, it can be bought for 4,750 Gems and 15,000 Coins. As it is an evolved tower, only some of its upgrades are unlocked at the start. All other have to be unlocked by reaching higher evolution levels on the tower.

Description: The Enforcer, internally referred to as EvolvedEnforcer, is the evolved version of the Shotgunner, unlocked by reaching Level 20 on the Shotgunner tower, either by getting the experience or by skipping the need to get it by paying 499 Robux. Once done, it can be bought for 4,750 Gems and 15,000 Coins. As it is an evolved tower, only some of its upgrades are unlocked at the start. All other have to be unlocked by reaching higher evolution levels on the tower.

The Enforcer fires a shotgun, meaning it fires out multiple pellets at once. These pellets are spread out based on their spread and random spread values. They can pierce through enemies. These bullets can sometimes miss targets to an enemy. Once it finishes a shot, it will need to pump its shotgun. This generally takes as long as shooting itself and will affect its firerate. Pump time is affected by the Firerate Buff. Once upgraded to Level 2, it will gain a flashbang grenade which it will throw out after dealing a specific amount of damage. This grenade will also stun enemies in a radius for a short time. While throwing the grenade, the Enforcer will visually stop attacking enemies, though it will still actually deal damage. The flashbang cannot stun enemies with Stun Immunity or Boss.
At Level 5, the tower splits into two separate paths:

Top path turns it into an ammo-based tower. Once it has fired a certain number of times, it will have to reload. This replaces its pump time. Additionally, it gains the ability to reposition towers with Reposition Helicopter. This lets the player move any tower they own anywhere on the map. However, non-humanoid towers like the Ace Pilot, Farm, Pursuit and Gatling Gun, are blacklisted from performing the ability.

Bottom path retains its pump functionality but gains the SWAT Van ability. This summons in depending on the upgrade either the Swat Van or Swat Van Gunner unit on the path. Both of the units are supposed to explode upon death.
The Enforcer has lead detection from Level 0 and hidden detection from Level 2. It has a placement limit of 5.
Abilities: Moves one player owned tower from one spot on the map to another. Cannot relocate the Farm, Pursuit, Ace Pilot or Gatling Gun.
Summons in a Swat Van which collides with enemies and explodes upon death. With upgrades, replaces it with Swat Van Gunner which also fires at enemies. Number of units spawned depends on the upgrade.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Enforcer can hit multiple enemies with one bullet. As each can hit up to two enemies, this means its DPS can effectively be doubled. However, this does not mean that with each shot it can only hit two enemies, as each individual bullet can hit a different enemy, strongly increasing the number of enemies hit. This is especially noticeable on the top path, as this means that despite its max hits being reduced to 1, it can still hit multiple enemies, though way less reliably. Proper use of targeting options and good placement can allow the tower to pierce through enemies much more. This is less important when going for the top path as each bullet can only hit one enemy.

When upgraded to the top path, the Enforcer gains the Helicopter Reposition ability. This will let it move your towers anywhere on the map. This can be used as a cheaper alternative to selling and rebuying towers as doing so will in a lot of cases be way more expensive than $2,500, though by late game you will also often have excess amounts of cash making this at times insignificant. This is best used on low placement limit towers, like the Juggernaut or Accelerator, as they can be quickly relocated with only a few ability uses. High placement limit towers like the Minigunner or Swarmer will require far more ability uses making simply rebuying them more convenient. Description: The Kingpin, internally referred to as EvolvedKingpin, is the evolved version of the Crook Boss, unlocked by reaching Level 20 on the Crook Boss tower, either by getting the experience or by skipping the need to get it by paying 599 Robux. Once done, it can be bought for 5,500 Gems and 15,000 Coins. As it is an evolved tower, only some of its upgrades are unlocked at the start. All other have to be unlocked by reaching higher evolution levels on the tower.

The Kingpin itself is a single target tower with no major gimmicks in the beginning, even lacking the Crook Boss ' summon animation for each unit. It does however have up to three unit queues, all of which summon in can summon a different unit. There are four available options:
Lackey, a simple single target unit with with decent health and DPS. The unit has hidden detection. It is unlocked from Level 0.
Money Runner, the only unit that cannot be used offensively outside of collision damage that upon death generates a set amount of cash. It is unlocked from Level 0.
Bouncer is a high health melee unit that attacks enemies with a bat. The unit has both hidden and lead detections. It is unlocked from Level 4B.
Contractor is a high range unit that deals a lot of damage at a slow speed. It has all three detections. It is unlocked from Level 6B.

While the bottom path has two units unique to itself, the top path instead gains the Bounty ability which lets the Kingpin mark an enemy in its range. While doing so, it will stop attacking enemies for 2 seconds. This marked enemy will generate a specific percentage of the enemy's total cash reward once the enemy has been killed, though the reward cannot exceed a specific value. Both the reward percentage and the reward cap increase with upgrades.
The Kingpin is primarily a mid to late-game tower, with top path focusing on income while bottom path focuses on DPS. It has a placement limit of 4.
Ability: Places a hit order on an enemy in range, making Kingpin stop attacking enemies for 2 seconds. When that enemy is killed, a bonus reward is given which is a specific percentage of the enemy's total cash reward. The reward from this ability cannot go above a specific limit.
Strategy: The Kingpin is best used as a mid-to-late game tower.

At Level 3, the Kingpin gains two paths. The top path is focused on giving the player cash through its Bounty ability and upgrading the Money Runners it spawns. The top path can be used as a secondary income source which may help at affording certain expensive towers like the Juggernaut. It is advised to use the Bounty ability on enemies that have a high cash reward, which usually is enemies with high health. Notably it also gains lead detection earlier than its bottom path counterpart. The bottom path is more focused on DPS and spawning units, this path unlocks the Bouncer and the Contractor. This path focuses on increasing the efficiency in which the units deal damage, whether it be by increasing their DPS, or shortening their spawnrate. Setting the bottom path Kingpin to spawn either Lackeys or Contractors can be extremely effective on certain maps where they can stack up in a single spot and attack simultaneously.

juggernaut.description: The Juggernaut or EvolvedJuggernaut is the evolved version of the Minigunner, unlocked by reaching Level 20 on the Minigunner tower, either by getting the experience or by paying 599 Robux. Once done, it can be bought for 6,000 Gems and 15,000 Coins. As it is an evolved tower, only some of its upgrades are unlocked at the start. All others have to be unlocked by reaching higher evolution levels on the tower.

Description: The Juggernaut or EvolvedJuggernaut is the evolved version of the Minigunner, unlocked by reaching Level 20 on the Minigunner tower, either by getting the experience or by paying 599 Robux. Once done, it can be bought for 6,000 Gems and 15,000 Coins. As it is an evolved tower, only some of its upgrades are unlocked at the start. All others have to be unlocked by reaching higher evolution levels on the tower.

The Juggernaut starts out working very similarly to the Minigunner. When enemies enter its range, it will rev up its minigun and start firing at them. It will not differ mechanically until Level 4, where it gains two paths.
The top path is a more support-based path where it gains a secondary range in which it reduces stun, freeze and debuff durations. Any tower in that range will have orange shields around them.
The bottom path is more offensive-based as it gives the passive ability of dealing boosted damage to Boss enemies.
The Juggernaut has hidden detection from Level 2, flying detection from Level 4A and lead detection from Level 4B. It has a placement limit of 1.
Strategy: The Juggernaut is best utilized as a mid-to-late game tower.

The Juggernaut, due to having the highest placement and upgrade costs, is impractical for easier gamemodes with a lower number of waves such as Intermediate and Casual. Economy towers, such as the Farm, Cowboy and Kingpin (top path) can aid in the its extremely expensive upgrades. The DJ Booth 's Green Track can also significantly aid in its extremely expensive upgrades, with the DJ Booth itself being an economy tower itself through its Drop The Beat ability through its Green Track.

As it has a placement limit of one and an extremely large placement footprint, consider placing it where its range will cover most of the path.

At Level 3, the Juggernaut gains two paths: The top path is focused on reducing the stun or debuff times of towers caused by enemies' abilities, such as the Necrotic Skeleton 's Gooey Demise, or the Fallen King 's Sword Swing. This is particularly useful for reducing the downtime of towers by reducing the stun and debuff durations of them. This is best utilized if the tower is already surrounded by other towers. Note that this is not as effective if it is not surrounded by enough towers, usually behind or in front of where most of the towers are placed. This path also gains flying detection, being useful for dealing with high health flying enemies like the Fallen Seraph, Balloon Kid, Voodoo Doll and Fallen Angel. Despite the fact that this path is only slightly cheaper than bottom path for flying detection, costing a total of around $72,000, this should not be much of a concern, as it is possible to get a Level 4A+ Juggernaut before Wave 22 in Fallen mode and before Wave 28 in Pizza Party. The bottom path is focused on dealing extra DPS to enemies with the Boss attribute via a damage multiplier. Note that the damage multiplier does not apply to enemies without the Boss attribute, but this still deals more DPS to enemies in general compared to the top path. This is best utilized for aiding in the defeat of Boss enemies, such as the Fallen Honor Guard and Executioner, as well as final boss enemies such as the Fallen King, Frost Spirit, and Wox the Fox. Although this path gains Lead detection, it is impractical for gamemodes that introduce enemies that have the Lead attribute early on, such as Pizza Party, costing a total of $77,000 just to get the detection.

The Juggernaut tower is the most expensive tower in the game's history, regardless of whether the player uses the top or bottom path, costing a total of $532,000 to completely max out the tower if on the bottom path, or $400,200 otherwise, followed by the Gatling Gun. The Juggernaut or EvolvedJuggernaut is the evolved version of the Minigunner, unlocked by reaching Level 20 on the Minigunner tower, either by getting the experience or by paying 599 Robux. Once done, it can be bought for 6,000 Gems and 15,000 Coins. As it is an evolved tower, only some of its upgrades are unlocked at the start. All others have to be unlocked by reaching higher evolution levels on the tower.

golden_minigunner.name: Golden Minigunner
golden_minigunner.description: The Golden Minigunner is a golden perk for the Minigunner, obtained from the Golden Crate for 50,000 Coins if you own the Minigunner. It can also be bought in the Daily Store for 75,000 Coins.

Description: The Golden Minigunner is a golden perk for the Minigunner, obtained from the Golden Crate for 50,000 Coins if you own the Minigunner. It can also be bought in the Daily Store for 75,000 Coins.

Before the Golden Minigunner starts firing, it needs to rev up its minigun. If there are no enemies in its range while revved-up, it will wait for around a second for an enemy to enter its range. If no enemy enters its range in that time, it begins to deactivate the gun and will need to rev the gun up again when an enemy enters its range. It fires bullets at enemies at a fast firerate. The Golden Minigunner has high DPS and a relatively cheap cost compared to other high DPS towers, like the Accelerator or Engineer.

The Golden Minigunner has more damage and costs more than its normal counterpart, the Minigunner, making it a direct upgrade in many ways. It is mostly considered a mid-game to late-game tower, although it can be used in early game if you have enough base health and focus solely on using the Farm for some time.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: It is highly recommend to get 2 Level 3 Golden Minigunners as both of them could deal 260 total DPS while being more cost efficient compared to a single Level 4.

The Golden Minigunner should be one of the towers that are placed down the most. If possible, place them in a large group near the front of the track, or place them in an area that covers a lot of path (for example, inside corners). Having a Commander or DJ Booth nearby helps a lot.
Having a Commander or DJ Booth nearby helps a lot.
Midway through the game, several Level 1-2 Golden Minigunners are effective in wiping out hordes of enemies for an effective price.

While this is a cost-effective way to triumph maps, this is not the best tower in terms of DPS. In terms of DPS and range, the Engineer, Ranger and Accelerator are far more effective. However, they are more expensive and have their own limitations, like placement limits. While it does have a quite higher DPS than the normal Minigunner, it also costs more to upgrade.

In terms of DPS and range, the Engineer, Ranger and Accelerator are far more effective. However, they are more expensive and have their own limitations, like placement limits. While it does have a quite higher DPS than the normal Minigunner, it also costs more to upgrade.
While it does have a quite higher DPS than the normal Minigunner, it also costs more to upgrade.

This tower is not affected much by the defense from enemies like the Giant Boss and Warden due to its low damage at lower levels. In most cases, the Golden Minigunner can still deal most of its damage to such enemies, or even its full damage. Do note that the Level 3 has 13 damage and Level 4 has 20 damage, which is high enough for most enemies to be able to decrease its damage. Even still, defense dropping towers like the Pyromancer are recommended to increase the damage of Golden Minigunners against certain enemies with very high defense.
Do note that the Level 3 has 13 damage and Level 4 has 20 damage, which is high enough for most enemies to be able to decrease its damage.
Even still, defense dropping towers like the Pyromancer are recommended to increase the damage of Golden Minigunners against certain enemies with very high defense.
The Golden Minigunner can be effective at killing high health hidden enemies that appear in mid game or late game, such as the Possessed Armor or Soul.
While the Golden Minigunner does not have incredibly low range, it is still lower than most other DPS towers, such as the Ranger, Engineer, Accelerator or Turret.

If you are planning to use the Golden Minigunner for early game, you need to have a high amount of base health and farm correctly to afford it. However, this is generally not recommended as it is risky. Alternatively, you should have teammates with cheap towers to help deal with the early game while you farm. You can also use the Supply Drop to help you farm more efficiently if you really want to get the Golden Minigunner down early.

Trivia: The Golden Minigunner, alongside its normal counterpart, the Minigunner, currently has the most skins out of any tower in the game.
The Golden Minigunner used to be the most expensive skin in the game, until the Coin Crate 's addition in V1.59.0, which possesses skin that cost 1,346,914,794 Coins.

golden_pyromancer.name: Golden Pyromancer
golden_pyromancer.description: The Golden Pyromancer is a golden perk for the Pyromancer, obtained from the Golden Crate for 50,000 Coins, if you own the Pyromancer. Its main gimmick is its ability to burn enemies, dealing extra damage over time and later reducing the enemy Defense.

Description: The Golden Pyromancer is a golden perk for the Pyromancer, obtained from the Golden Crate for 50,000 Coins, if you own the Pyromancer. Its main gimmick is its ability to burn enemies, dealing extra damage over time and later reducing the enemy Defense.

If an enemy is set alight, the flames will be applied to the enemy until the burn time runs out. There are two types of damage the Golden Pyromancer can apply. The first is Normal Damage which is non-burn related. This can pierce through multiple enemies, not including flying enemies, which it is unable to damage without flying detection. Its flame can initially only hit four different enemies, but with upgrades it increases to ten enemies at once. The second is Burn Damage which is applied for every second an enemy is set alight. Both damage methods can damage Lead enemies. The Golden Pyromancer will attack any enemy, even if the enemy is on fire. However, if there are multiple enemies in its range, it will attack the first enemy that is not on fire. Unlike its normal counterpart, the Golden Pyromancer can detect hidden enemies from Level 0.

The Golden Pyromancer, in comparison to the Pyromancer, has increased normal damage, burn damage and burn time, at one point having it be effectively infinite. This is considered to be an all rounder tower.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Golden Pyromancer is considered an early to mid-game tower, because of its cost efficiency and moderate damage. It can be used to easily deal with weak enemy hordes like the Normal, Heavy or Quick and at higher Levels, it can even take out high health enemies like the Normal Boss and Elite Abnormal. Although it is unable to outright defeat hordes of higher-health enemies like Giant Bosses, it can still do substantial damage to them. Even though it is considered as such, it still has certain usage in the late game to reduce defense.
