The Golden Pyromancer will set every enemy in its range on fire. In what order the Golden Pyromancer will choose its target is based on its targeting. If there is only one detectable enemy in the Golden Pyromancer's range, then it will always target that enemy. This also occurs if all current enemies in the Golden Pyromancer's range is set on fire.
If there is only one detectable enemy in the Golden Pyromancer's range, then it will always target that enemy. This also occurs if all current enemies in the Golden Pyromancer's range is set on fire.
As the Golden Pyromancer can set lots of enemies on fire at once, due to its pierce and targeting of multiple enemies, it can be very effective against hordes of enemies such as Breakers.
The Golden Pyromancer has hidden detection from Level 0, allowing it to deal with Hidden enemies quite well early on.

The Golden Pyromancer can also be used to melt an enemy's Defense by half. The Golden Pyromancer can be used alongside other defense melting towers, like the Freezer, Electroshocker or Toxic Gunner to melt it further, though it cannot be used alongside the regular Pyromancer and other fire defense melting sources. As such, with these towers, an enemy's Defense can be removed entirely. This can be useful since it can harshly decrease the defense of enemies with very high defense like the Vindicator, Reaver or Slow King. Do note that this may be impractical as it requires you to bring several support towers, even though the tower slot could be used for more important DPS towers.

The Golden Pyromancer is best placed near the beginning of the path. This lets it kill weaker enemies and decrease defense of enemies before they reach your other towers.
The Golden Pyromancer will not be able to set enemies on fire when placed on high grounds, like ones on The Heights.
The Golden Pyromancer's burn damage does not stack with other regular Pyromancer, Golden Pyromancers or other towers that deal burn damage, like the Archer.
Trivia: The Golden Pyromancer and the Turret are the only towers that have hidden detection at Level 0. The Accelerator, Paintballer, Outlaw (now the Ranger), Jester, Commander, and Necromancer used to have hidden detection at Level 0, however, hidden detection was either moved to another level or removed from these towers.

The Level 5 upgrade's name comes from Kagu-tsuchi, who is the god of fire in classical Japanese mythology. The full name, Kagutsuchi's Fury, is also likely a reference to the upgraded Staff of Fire from Call of Duty: Black Ops II Zombies.

golden_crook_boss.name: Golden Crook Boss
golden_crook_boss.description: The Golden Crook Boss is an upgraded version of the Crook Boss, obtained from the Golden Crate for 50,000 Coins if the player owns the Crook Boss. It can also be bought in the Daily Store for 55,000 Coins. The normal counterpart, the Crook Boss, can be claimed by reaching Level 30 or alternatively purchasing it for 300 Robux.

Description: The Golden Crook Boss is an upgraded version of the Crook Boss, obtained from the Golden Crate for 50,000 Coins if the player owns the Crook Boss. It can also be bought in the Daily Store for 55,000 Coins. The normal counterpart, the Crook Boss, can be claimed by reaching Level 30 or alternatively purchasing it for 300 Robux.

Initially, the Golden Crook Boss has high damage, though it has rather low range. However, with later upgrades, the firerate decreases and its damage increases significantly. The range also increases and becomes comparable to towers like the Minigunner. The Golden Crook Boss has the ability to spawn Golden Pistol Goon from Level 0, which with later levels get double spawns. Additional, at Level 3, it spawns Golden Tommy Goon 1, which gets replaced by Golden Tommy Goon 2 at Level 4. Every time it summons an unit, it stops attacking for a second. All the units have flying detection but only the Tommy Goons have hidden detection.
In comparison to its normal counterpart, the Crook Boss, the Golden Crook Boss has higher damage and slightly higher range, but it is more expensive at all Levels. It also spawns stronger units.

The Golden Crook Boss can be considered a mid to late-game tower, as its expensive cost for extremely high DPS makes it a great tower later on during the game and has sufficient DPS to remain strong in the extra-late game.

There is a limit of five Golden Crook Bosses per player. Additionally, it has a limit of ten Golden Pistol Goons per tower and a limit of three Golden Tommy Goon 1s and Golden Tommy Goon 2s per tower.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: You can only place a maximum of five Golden Crook Bosses. If you have other towers without placement limits (such as the Minigunner and the Militant) then it is best to use them after you have got five Golden Crook Bosses.
If you have other towers without placement limits (such as the Minigunner and the Militant) then it is best to use them after you have got five Golden Crook Bosses.

The Golden Crook Boss is well worth its cost mid to late-game, and it does a great job at dealing damage, especially when the goons are included. In some regards, the Golden Crook Boss is superior to the Minigunner, but it does have a hefty placement limit, and it often relies on the goons that can be killed easily.
In some regards, the Golden Crook Boss is superior to the Minigunner, but it does have a hefty placement limit, and it often relies on the goons that can be killed easily.
Do not rely entirely on the goons as their low health makes them vulnerable to enemy collision and abilities that deal damage.

If you are on a map where units can consistently target enemies from further away, such as Crossroads or Honey Valley, the units that spawn from the Golden Crook Boss may prove quite useful in providing extra damage, especially against slower enemies. You may also use towers, such as the Electroshocker, Frost Blaster or Freezer, to slow down enemies, giving the units more time to shoot at enemies. Do note, however, that there is a limit on how many of them can be spawned from a single Golden Crook Boss. Additionally, they all have lifespans, making them last on the map for only a few minutes.
You may also use towers, such as the Electroshocker, Frost Blaster or Freezer, to slow down enemies, giving the units more time to shoot at enemies.
Do note, however, that there is a limit on how many of them can be spawned from a single Golden Crook Boss. Additionally, they all have lifespans, making them last on the map for only a few minutes.

It may be useful to keep skipping waves in order to keep the Golden Crook Boss's units attacking so they can stack more. Do be aware that you may be overwhelmed by the amount of enemies, so make sure you are safe before skipping.
Do be aware that you may be overwhelmed by the amount of enemies, so make sure you are safe before skipping.

The Field Medic can protect the Golden Crook Boss's units from attacks that can damage unit, such as stomps, so it can be useful to pair this tower with the Mercenary Base in modes like Hardcore mode or Polluted Wasteland II, allowing you to stack up a lot of units. Be aware that this may cause major performance issues if there are too many units present.
Be aware that this may cause major performance issues if there are too many units present.
Trivia: The current upgrade names are a reference to the text that appeared in the upgrade descriptions of the Crook Boss before the MEGA Update, which could have been considered the upgrade names for the tower. The Level 1-3 upgrade names are the same as the Crook Boss before the MEGA Update. These upgrade names were a reference to the Mafia City meme, as the Crook Boss was originally a reference to that meme.
The Level 1-3 upgrade names are the same as the Crook Boss before the MEGA Update.
These upgrade names were a reference to the Mafia City meme, as the Crook Boss was originally a reference to that meme.

The former second Level 2 upgrade name, Goldeneye, is a reference to the James Bond franchise. The name originally comes from Operation Goldeneye, a plan by Commander Ian Fleming to monitor the alliance between Francoist Spain and the Axis powers during World War II. Ian Fleming would later use the name for his estate in Jamaica, where he wrote the James Bond series. GoldenEye would be used for the title of the 17th film in the James Bond film series, starring Pierce Brosnan as James Bond in 1995. Officially, the upgrade name was based on the GoldenEye 007 Nintendo 64 video game, released in 1997.
The name originally comes from Operation Goldeneye, a plan by Commander Ian Fleming to monitor the alliance between Francoist Spain and the Axis powers during World War II.
Ian Fleming would later use the name for his estate in Jamaica, where he wrote the James Bond series.
GoldenEye would be used for the title of the 17th film in the James Bond film series, starring Pierce Brosnan as James Bond in 1995.
Officially, the upgrade name was based on the GoldenEye 007 Nintendo 64 video game, released in 1997.

The former second Level 3 upgrade name, M1927, is the name of a Thompson gun. However, at Level 3 both the Default and Golden skins wielded an M1A1 Thompson. They did not wield any weapons similar to the M1927 Thompson until Level 4.
The former second Level 4 upgrade name, Level 100 BOSS, is most likely a reference to the Mafia City meme. This is because originally, the Crook Boss was a reference to the this meme.

golden_scout.name: Golden Scout
golden_scout.description: The Golden Scout is a upgraded version of the Scout, obtained in the Golden Crate for 50,000 Coins. It can also appear in the Daily Skin Store for 55,000 Coins. You automatically unlock the Golden Scout's normal counterpart, the Scout, when you first join in the game.

Description: The Golden Scout is a upgraded version of the Scout, obtained in the Golden Crate for 50,000 Coins. It can also appear in the Daily Skin Store for 55,000 Coins. You automatically unlock the Golden Scout's normal counterpart, the Scout, when you first join in the game.

The Golden Scout is very cheap in comparison to other towers, meaning that it can be placed right from the start of the game. However, the Golden Scout has mediocre DPS, meaning that in harder modes it is not that effective later on during the game.

In comparison to its normal counterpart, the Scout, it is considerably more expensive to upgrade. Despite this, the Golden Scout is significantly better than its normal counterpart because it has much higher DPS and efficiency. The Golden Scout is considered an early-game to mid-game tower, although it can handle the late-game with some support.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Golden Scout is mainly used as an early-game to mid-game tower and does not perform as well later on during the game. Placing multiple Level 0 Golden Scouts can be a good way to defend earlier waves.
Placing multiple Level 0 Golden Scouts can be a good way to defend earlier waves.

The Golden Scout has cheap hidden detection. This means that the Golden Scout can be used to defend against weaker Hidden enemies, like the Hidden and Shadow, while you can work on getting more expensive towers and upgrades. It can also defend well against Hidden enemies with higher health such as the Hidden Boss or Shadow Boss at later levels, when multiple of them are placed down. It also has cheap lead penetration, making it useful for enemies like Lead and Elite Lead. However, it does not have flying detection, so it cannot target the Lead Balloon while its balloons are not popped.

The Golden Scout can be used as a cheap way to distract enemies like the Molten Boss from using their abilities on more useful towers, like the Accelerator. This could be risky however, due to the tower slot limit of 5, you may not be able to choose better towers. You can use the Golden Scout to deal with the early waves to give it some use other than distracting bosses' abilities.

golden_cowboy.name: Golden Cowboy
golden_cowboy.description: The Golden Cowboy is a golden perk for the Cowboy, unlocked from the Golden Crate for 50,000 Coins, if you have the Cowboy. It can also appear in the daily skin store for 70,000 Coins.

Description: The Golden Cowboy is a golden perk for the Cowboy, unlocked from the Golden Crate for 50,000 Coins, if you have the Cowboy. It can also appear in the daily skin store for 70,000 Coins.

While initially it has a slow firerate, it deals moderate damage with a fairly low range. On later levels, the Golden Cowboy gains much higher damage, higher range and a faster firerate. The Golden Cowboy can also generate cash every sixth shot. The amount of shots needed for the Golden Cowboy to generate cash can be seen above its tower icon in the upgrade box or when you hover your cursor over it. After firing the last shot, it will spin its gun for a short while. The Spin Time is decreased at higher Levels. This ability can act as a primary or secondary source of economy.
The Golden Cowboy is considered an all round tower. Its DPS makes it decent to defend early and mid-game, while its ability to generate cash can make it useful for the entire match.

In comparison to its normal counterpart, the Cowboy, the Golden Cowboy has higher damage, slightly higher range at Level 0 and it generates more money. It is, however, more expensive to place down and upgrade.
The Golden Cowboy has a placement limit of twelve per player.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Golden Cowboy is a great all-round tower, being able to handle earlier waves and later waves on most gamemodes. Early on during the game, you may want to place down multiple Level 0 Golden Cowboys because of their low price. Due to its low placement limit of 12, it is unable to deal with the later waves on its own in terms of DPS, though its money generation can still be effective in the later waves.

The Golden Cowboy generates a specified amount of money every sixth shot from Levels 0-3 and every twelfth shot at Levels 4-5. Later on during the game, higher level Golden Cowboys will be able to earn lots of money from enemies, being on par with the Farm, and even outperforming it. If you want to use this tower for farming early on, multiple Level 2 Golden Cowboys can be quite effective at generating money. The amount of cash earned can be increased even further with the Commander and Cooldown Flag Firerate Buff. Enemies summoned by other enemies or sent by players do not count for cash shot. Any enemy that the game does not consider a summoned enemy can still be generated cash from. This includes actually summoned enemies that the game does not consider summoned, like the Slime from the Slime, or enemies converted in a way that makes them look like a summoned enemy, such as Corpses. Additionally, you can increase the money earned by the Golden Cowboy by placing it near the start of the path, ensuring that no other towers can damage enemies before the Golden Cowboy. While the Golden Cowboy cannot damage lead enemies, like the Lead, shots towards these enemies will contribute to the Golden Cowboy's cash shot.

golden_soldier.name: Golden Soldier
golden_soldier.description: The Golden Soldier is a ground tower that fires in bursts. It is an upgraded version of the Soldier, obtained from the Golden Crate for 50,000 Coins, if you own the Soldier. It can also appear in the Daily Skin Store for 50,000 Coins.

Description: The Golden Soldier is a ground tower that fires in bursts. It is an upgraded version of the Soldier, obtained from the Golden Crate for 50,000 Coins, if you own the Soldier. It can also appear in the Daily Skin Store for 50,000 Coins.

The Golden Soldier fires in bursts, with a short delay between each burst, though in Level 3 and 4, it will no longer fire in bursts and will instead auto fire like the Militant. It is a fairly cheap tower, so it can be used effectively in earlier waves. It gains flying detection at Level 0 and hidden detection at Level 2, so it is an effective counter against hidden and flying enemies.

In comparison to its normal counterpart, the Soldier, the Golden Soldier has flying detection immediately, more range, more damage, a higher burst, and a faster firerate on most Levels, but it is more expensive to place down and upgrade. Due to its cheap cost and efficient stats, it is considered an early to mid-game and late-game tower.

Later on during the game, the Golden Soldier's effectiveness dwindles against high health enemies and is outclassed by other, stronger, towers. Despite this, it still acts as an effective anti-air option, as well as dealing with hordes of weaker enemies relatively quickly.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Golden Soldier is an effective early game tower at Level 2, having high DPS and hidden detection for a cheap price. In the mid game, you can get multiple Level 3-4 Golden Soldiers, as they can effectively kill most enemies that appear there, such as the Possessed Armor and Slow Boss. It should not be relied on in the late game if you have better towers like the Turret or Ranger. It can, however, be used as a secondary DPS source to support your main DPS tower, depending on your loadout.

The Golden Soldier is a ground tower that fires in bursts. It is an upgraded version of the Soldier, obtained from the Golden Crate for 50,000 Coins, if you own the Soldier. It can also appear in the Daily Skin Store for 50,000 Coins.

Description: The Golden Demoman is a splash damage tower that is an upgraded version of the Demoman, obtained from the Golden Crate for 50,000 Coins, if you own the Demoman. It can also appear in the Daily Skin Store for 55,000 Coins.

The Golden Demoman throws explosive golden grenades at enemies which deal medium damage within an explosion radius. To compensate, it has a rather fast firerate compared to other Splash Damage towers. It has no damage drop-off, so it deals full damage to all enemies within explosion radius. At Levels 0-2, the Golden Demoman takes one second to aim at an enemy before throwing its grenade. This only affects the damage for the first throw, as it means the Golden Demoman has to wait 0.8 seconds before throwing it. While it is aiming, it will lock onto one enemy until it throws the grenade, after which it can target a different one. Even after the targeted enemy dies, the Golden Demoman will continue targeting it, though its grenade will land slightly ahead of where the enemy dies, in order to hit the enemy should it be still alive and moving forward. The Golden Demoman will also continue to aim at a target enemy even if it leaves its range, allowing it to attack outside of its range.

The Golden Demoman is excellent for clearing huge crowds, except for those immune to splash damage. It is relatively weak against major bosses, though it can be useful for clearing the enemies that spawn from some major bosses. The Golden Demoman is considered an early game to mid-game tower, though in late game it can be quite useful for AOE damage when multiple are placed down.
The Golden Demoman can damage Lead and Hidden enemies, and has no placement limit.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Golden Demoman is considered an early to mid-game tower, allowing it to clear early waves quickly with its splash damage that is able to hit an unlimited number of enemies. Golden Demoman can completely bypass Defense through its explosives, allowing it to quickly clear larger hordes of high-defense enemies like Heavy or Armored. This also makes it very useful against enemies that received the Blessed attribute from Trickster Elf or Fallen Jester as it can completely bypass the extremely high defense of these types of enemies.

The Golden Demoman is excellent as starting defense in solo Hardcore mode, similarly to Golden Pyromancer. Its optimal usage is to place one down at the front of the map and upgrade it to Level 3 before getting something else. Keep in mind that the earlier levels of Golden Demoman, like Level 0 and Level 1, can leak faster enemies like Swift, though this is not a huge issue since the earlier enemies have relatively low hp, and past Level 2 it can handle these enemy types much better. Afterwards it is advantageous to invest in a few more Golden Demoman s as they can clear larger hordes much better this way.

The Golden Demoman is best used when set to target Random, especially due to its faster firerate which allows for maximum area coverage. Alternatively the Golden Demoman can be set to target first as summoner enemies like Necromancer and Frost Necromancer, or major bosses like Frost Spirit and Molten Warlord summon enemies in front of themselves, allowing Golden Demoman to quickly eliminate these weaker enemies and let the other towers focus on the target enemy.

The Golden Demoman is a good cost-effective option for early-mid game as it can easily clear earlier waves, though it struggles in late game by itself. Pairing Golden Demoman with high single-target damage towers like Golden Minigunner and Crook Boss, or stall towers like Slime Trooper and Tesla allows for maximum efficiency as a crowd clearer. Placing multiple Golden Demoman s also allow it to take down stronger swarms much more easily, although this can cause some lag if particles are turned on.

In some cases, Golden Demoman can be used as enemy bait to protect other more vulnerable towers like Accelerator or Juggernaut by taking hits for them, and since it is stun immune, it is not affected, though do note certain enemies will not target towers with the Stun Immunity.

gladiator.description: The Gladiator is an exclusive melee ground tower that could have been obtained by triumphing The Heights during the SFOTH Event, or through limited time gamepases.

Description: The Gladiator is an exclusive melee ground tower that could have been obtained by triumphing The Heights during the SFOTH Event, or through limited time gamepases.

The Gladiator swings its sword in an arc, piercing through multiple enemies at once. At Level 2, it unlocks the War Cry ability; upon activation, it makes it attack much faster by giving it a Firerate Buff, allowing it to deal significantly more damage and deal with stronger threats. Additionally, it removes the Fatigue Debuff or Scared Debuff from the Gladiator. When activating the ability, the Gladiator will stop attacking enemies for 1.5 seconds. From Level 3, it also unlocks the passive ability Fire Aspect. Once the cooldown bar reaches 0, the next attack will inflict burn on an enemy, dealing damage over time for a short duration.

The Gladiator also has a unique passive ability where it can block stuns, such as attacks from the Frost Hero or the Fallen King. During the parry, it stops attacking enemies for 0.75 seconds. It cannot parry other types of attacks, like debuffs or freezes.
The Gladiator has hidden detection from Level 0 and lead detection from Level 3. It has no placement limit.
Ability: Decreases swingrate by 65% through the Firerate Buff while also removing any Fatigue Debuff or Scared Debuff on the tower. When activated, the Gladiator cannot attack enemies for a few seconds. Lasts for 15 seconds.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: Due to the Gladiator's attack hitting up to ten enemies it can deal high amounts of damage to crowded groups of enemies.

Since the Gladiator has a very short range, it should be placed at bends or turns on paths to maximize how much of the path it covers in its range. It should also be placed at the front to kill early-game enemies quickly. On maps with multiple lanes, it is recommended to place the Gladiator near intersecting paths, where enemies enter its range from multiple paths, allowing it to take out enemies from multiple paths at once.

The Gladiator's swingrate can be decreased with the Commander, helping the Gladiator attack faster. The Gladiator's Warrior's Call, paired with the Commander 's Call to Arms, can further decrease swingrate, causing the Gladiator to be able to attack very quickly. This can effectively handle fast and tough enemies. Do note that the Warrior's Call ability stops the Gladiator from attacking for a 1.5 seconds when activated. The ability should be used a few seconds before enemies enter the Gladiator's range.

The Gladiator's capability to hit more than one enemy makes it very efficient against groups of enemies, especially slow ones. Do note that it can only hit a limited number of enemies in one swing.

The Gladiator struggles against fast enemies, such as the Bolt and Fallen Rusher, as most often will escape Gladiator's range very quickly. Additionally, singular high-health enemy like the Speedy Boss can easily pass through its range. On the other hand, groups of slow, tough enemies like the Slow Boss are optimal for the Gladiator as it can hit a decent number of enemies within its range. It may become feasible by setting up multiple Gladiators placed along the path to handle further, more of them.

The Gladiator could have been seen in the second and third versions of Medieval Times farming in front of a house, supposedly on vacation. This was due to the fact that the Gladiator was unusable between the 13th of October 2019 and the 29th of November 2019. Attempting to place the Gladiator resulted in the following message being displayed: " Hey! I'm on vacation, don't bother me! ". This Easter egg was still in the game, despite the Gladiator being usable again, though it would be removed on the 4th of February 2023 when Medieval Times was remade.

commando.name: Commando
commando.description: The Commando is a tower that could have been obtained through triumphing the Area 51 map in Normal+ mode as part of the Area 51 Event. It cannot be bought in the store. It could most recently be bought for 799 Robux for a limited time.

Description: The Commando is a tower that could have been obtained through triumphing the Area 51 map in Normal+ mode as part of the Area 51 Event. It cannot be bought in the store. It could most recently be bought for 799 Robux for a limited time.

The Commando fires lasers from its laser pistols. These lasers can pierce through enemies, dealing damage to at most two enemies. Additionally, the Commando has a limited amount of ammunition. After it runs out of ammo, it will throw away its guns, which puts it into a reload animation. This takes more time than regular burst cooldown.

At Level 3, it gains a Missile ability. This ability allows it to fire out missiles on a spot selected by the player. The range missiles can be fired in is twice as large as the Commando's range. At Level 3, it fires out two missiles, though at Level 4 its increased to four. The ability has a cooldown, though unlike other abilities, each missile counts as a separate ability use. This means each ability cooldown only gives back one missiles, not all of them. If a missile hits an enemy, it will deal damage to them and stun them. As it deals Splash Damage, they will create an explosion that deals damage to enemies caught in it, also bypassing their defense. If a missile does not hit anything, it will stay on the ground and act as a landmine, remaining on the ground for eighty seconds. These missiles can damage Lead, Flying and Hidden enemies.
The Commando has a placement limit of eight per player.
Ability: Fires out two and at Level 4 four missiles at selected area. Missile range is double of regular range. Reloads one missile per cooldown.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Commando should mostly be used as a mid to late game DPS and area of effect tower, as both regular gun and missiles have decent area of effect capabilities and it is quite expensive to upgrade. The DJ Booth can be useful at reducing its upgrade cost, making it more affordable.
The DJ Booth can be useful at reducing its upgrade cost, making it more affordable.

At earlier Levels, its only source of damage is through its guns. As these pierce through enemies, having them placed in corners or near straight lines can allow it to maximize the number of enemies hit. Additionally, changing its targeting can also help, making it hit as many of them possible. Before Level 2, these guns can indirectly hit Hidden enemies if another detectable enemy is nearby, though this should not be relied on.

At Level 3, it gains its Missile ability, allowing it to send out missiles at a selected area. As they can be targeted anywhere in its range, they can be quite useful at clearing out hordes of weaker enemies like the Fallen Hazmat, Breaker4 or Reaver, or to weaken stronger enemies like the Fallen Giant or Failed Experiment. These missiles can bypass defense. The area they can land in is not infinite, instead the missile range is double of the Commando's range. Because of this, it can be used to kill any enemy that goes past its main range. The missiles do not explode if they hit nothing, they instead stay on the ground until an enemy steps on them, possibly making them hit something later or allowing you to set them up for enemies in advance. However, do note that after their lifespan ends, they will instantly explode, even if nothing stepped over them.

Do note that its missiles do not instantly get sent out to the selected spot, they take a few seconds to actually travel there. Because of this, if targeting a singular enemy, it may be better to place them slightly in front of the enemy instead of directly at it.

The Commando gets hidden detection from Level 2, and not only that, its missiles can also hit Hidden enemies. This makes the Commando quite effective against hordes of Hidden enemies. However, it is relatively costly compared to other towers, so it should not be used for early game hidden enemies. The missiles can also damage Flying enemies as well, making it more versatile.

However, it is relatively costly compared to other towers, so it should not be used for early game hidden enemies.
The missiles can also damage Flying enemies as well, making it more versatile.

The missiles fired out by the Commando stun enemies on hit, making it quite effective at stalling enemies. As the missiles damage multiple enemies at once, its quite effective at stalling hordes of enemies.
As the missiles damage multiple enemies at once, its quite effective at stalling hordes of enemies.

The DJ Booth can be useful when combined with the Commando, as it has quite low range. As its missile range is double of its regular range, this means its missile range is actually affected by Range Buffs.
As its missile range is double of its regular range, this means its missile range is actually affected by Range Buffs.
As both its regular and missile damage are affected by Damage Buffs, towers like the DJ Booth or Mercenary Base can be useful with it.
Trivia: This was the second event tower added, after the Gladiator.
This tower is based on the Commando from Risk of Rain 2.
The Commando used to appear alongside the Commander on the "Triumph" screen before the Overhaul Update.

Before the 20th of November 2024, the Commando was the only event tower that was not available through a gamepass. When it did receive a gamepass, it was put on sale with a cost of 999,999,999 Robux prior to the release of v1.42.0, which got later reduced to 32,323,232 Robux and then quickly taken offsale, making it the most expensive gamepass in the entire game.

The Level 4 upgrade description mentions that the Commando gains " Really Cool Armor ", despite not being a statistical change. This armor is stated to likely being stolen from Area 51. The original default appearance actually reused some assets from enemies that appeared in that map, such as the old missile launcher being the same as the one used by the Raider Boss. Before the Overhaul Update, it was called " Cool gold armor ". This was removed during the Hardcore Testing BETA; however, it was later re-added in the Overhaul Update.

slasher.description: The Slasher, formerly known as the Shredder, is a short-range ground tower that could have been unlocked by triumphing Nightmare Carnival as part of the Halloween 2019 Event. It was most recently obtainable via a gamepass costing 499 Robux until the 19th of November 2025.

Description: The Slasher, formerly known as the Shredder, is a short-range ground tower that could have been unlocked by triumphing Nightmare Carnival as part of the Halloween 2019 Event. It was most recently obtainable via a gamepass costing 499 Robux until the 19th of November 2025.

The Slasher attacks by slashing and stabbing enemies with its knife. Unlike the Gladiator, which is a multi-hit tower, the Slasher is a single target tower. However, the Slasher can deal critical damage for 2x damage every three swings at Level 0, with the multiplier increasing with upgrades.

At Level 2, it gains the ability to apply bleed to enemies. Each bleed applied will only deal damage to an enemy once before disappearing, with there also being a 1 second delay between each bleed damage. Additionally, it can only deal damage while bleed is not being applied. This bleed can stack up to 450 times, which will cause a bleed collapse, dealing increased damage to the enemy instantly. Once the bleed collapses, there is a five second cooldown before bleed can be applied again. The damage dealt varies based on an enemy's max health and the Slasher's base bleed damage, EV (exponential value) and how many bleed stacks are removed at once. Because of this, when the enemy receives bleed damage from the enemy over time, it is calculated as: (Base Bleed Damage × (1 0.9)) × (Enemy Max Health EV) While bleed is collapsing on an enemy, it is calculated as: (Base Bleed Damage × (45 0 0.9)) × (Enemy Max Health EV)

Damage from bleed is always rounded up, for both damage over time and from bleed collapse. Additionally, damage from bleed damage will not be displayed as the full damage dealt for the Slasher unless only one Slasher was applying bleed. Damage displayed will be based on the number of bleed stacks applied by the selected Slasher. This damage is not affected by Damage Buffs.

The Slasher can be considered a mid to late-game tower as its fairly effective during the mid and late game due to its high DPS, and its bleed effect that can affect every enemy, including major bosses.
The Slasher has a placement limit of eight per player.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Slasher can be very effective at taking down single high health enemies and chipping bosses, due to its high bleed collapse damage.

The Slasher can apply bleed to enemies, allowing it to deal even more damage to the enemy. However, these do not deal any damage while the Slasher is attacking the enemy unless max stack is reached, where it will explode. The amount of damage dealt is based on the enemy's max health, meaning that its effectiveness scales with the enemy's health. Placing down multiple Slashers can help by making them apply bleed faster, also making it explode faster. However, at level 4, the Slasher can apply maximum bleed very quickly, and due to the long cooldown before being able to apply bleed again, it's more recommended to spread out Slashers to maximize its high collapse damage.

The Commander can be quite useful, as it allows it to deal more DPS and makes it apply bleed faster.
Stalling towers, such as the Cryomancer or Electroshocker, can be useful, as it makes enemies stay in the Slasher's range for longer, allowing for it to deal more DPS and apply more bleed.
Be aware of the Slasher's short range. Placing this tower at corners of the path is crucial to get the most out of this tower.
The Slasher has a small placement footprint meaning that it can squeeze in beside other towers quite easily, if space is a problem.
Trivia: This is the second melee tower to be added to the game, with the first being the Gladiator.
The former Level 3 upgrade name " Swords Dance " is a reference to the Pokémon move of the same name.
The Slasher was loosely inspired by the Knifer from Tower Battles.
The Slasher was the first tower to gain Stun Immunity with upgrades instead of having it from Level 0, the second being the Accelerator.

The Slasher (when it was called the Shredder) used to have a Knife Throw ability before the Overhaul Update, which would make the Slasher throw a piercing knife. This ability was later given to the Assassin tower, which coincidentally is also a melee tower. With the ability, the Slasher gained a 200% Range Buff, its swingrate was set to 0.7 and the ability cooldown was 25 seconds. It was meant to receive 500% more damage, but this was glitched and never occurred. The Knife Throw became a passive ability that the Slasher then gained at Level 2, though that was later removed in the Hexscape Update.

frost_blaster.name: Frost Blaster
frost_blaster.description: The Frost Blaster is a tower that pierces through and freezes any enemy hit by its projectile. It could have been unlocked by triumphing Village of Despair during the Christmas 2019 Event. It could have also been through a limited time gamepass for 350 Robux. It was most recently available again for 525 Robux.

Description: The Frost Blaster is a tower that pierces through and freezes any enemy hit by its projectile. It could have been unlocked by triumphing Village of Despair during the Christmas 2019 Event. It could have also been through a limited time gamepass for 350 Robux. It was most recently available again for 525 Robux.

The Frost Blaster starts out with decent damage, gaining more damage at higher levels and it also has a somewhat high firerate. However, it fires piercing projectiles that freezes enemies when hit. Any enemy with the Freeze Immunity cannot be slowed down, frozen or have its Defense dropped by the Frost Blaster. This makes Frost Blaster an offensive support hybrid since it has a higher DPS than the Freezer.
Starting at Level 2, the Frost Blaster will melt 15% defense every tick, though it can only decrease an enemy's defense by 33%. For example, if an enemy has 50% defense, it will be decreased by 16%.

The Frost Blaster is mostly considered as an early to midgame tower, though it can sometimes be considered as an all-around tower. Its relatively low-medium placement cost and decent DPS can be useful in the early game, while its later upgrades and relatively higher DPS can be sufficient in the mid to late game. Though, this tower should mainly be used as a staller and crowd control tower due to its freezing and piercing capabilities. The Frost Blaster has a placement limit of 12 per player.
Strategy: The Frost Blaster's piercing projectile makes it a great tower for early and mid-game. For earlier waves, a Level 0-2 Frost Blaster can be effective at killing enemies that spawn, though by the time high health singular enemies spawn, like the Elite Abnormal, it should be upgraded to Level 3 because of its higher DPS and better chilling Later on in the game the Frost Blaster does not have enough DPS to deal with enemies like the Fallen Giant or Hidden Boss on its own, meaning that you need other towers alongside it. It can, however, be useful at chilling enemies and decreasing their Defense.

Later on in the game the Frost Blaster does not have enough DPS to deal with enemies like the Fallen Giant or Hidden Boss on its own, meaning that you need other towers alongside it. It can, however, be useful at chilling enemies and decreasing their Defense.
It can, however, be useful at chilling enemies and decreasing their Defense.

Unlike other freezing towers, the Frost Blaster only chills an enemy. Larger enemies, like the Fallen Giant will get slowed down for a shorter amount of time. Additionally, it cannot slow down any enemy that has the Freeze Immunity. It can still apply the chillness slowdown effect to Boss enemies, as long as it does not have Freeze Immunity. However, the slowdown effect will be much weaker. The Level 3 is especially good at slowing down, as its freeze time and firerate are nearly identical, allowing to close to permanently slow down smaller enemies.

The Frost Blaster's Defense melting ability can be useful for decreasing an enemy's Defense, allowing your towers to deal more damage to it. However, do note that as the defense melting happens when an enemy is slowed down. Because of this, freeze immune enemies cannot have their defense melted. The defense melt can stack with other towers, such as the Pyromancer, Electroshocker or Toxic Gunner, allowing you to remove an enemy's defense entirely. However, the Frost Blaster's defense melt does not stack with other freezing towers.

The Frost Blaster's range is quite high at Level 4, making it harder for enemies to get out of its range. This also means it is able to chills enemies from far ranges, surpassing many other stalling towers in this regard. You can use the DJ Booth to increase this already high range even more.

Because of the Frost Blaster's freezing and cheap hidden detection, it can be used against early hidden enemies like the Fallen Soul or Hidden. However, it may be best to upgrade a single one to Level 2-3 or place multiple Level 1 Frost Blasters as a single Level 1 Frost Blaster is unlikely to deal with them on their own, especially against Fallen Souls. Later on, Level 4 Frost Blasters are effective at freezing high health hidden enemies like the Hidden Boss, Elite Phantom and Elite Soul.

The Frost Blaster is effective against Leads and Elite Leads as it has lead detection from Level 0 and can freeze them. The Frost Blaster should be upgraded to Level 2-3 or have multiple lower levels placed down because of their high health.

Trivia: The Frost Blaster is the oldest tower in the game that has yet to receive a skin. The Soldier Beach skin was originally made as a Frost Blaster skin, however, it ended up getting converted into a Soldier skin instead. Certain parts of the design like the Frost Blaster weapon look did get carried over to the Soldier version of the skin.

archer.name: Archer
archer.description: The Archer, formerly known as the Holiday Archer, is a tower that attacks enemies with a bow. It could have been unlocked from the Gift of Sharpness, which costed 2,500 Tickets, as part of the Christmas 2019 Event. The gift could have also been bought via a limited time gamepass for 250 Robux. It could later be bought through a different limited time gamepass, which was sold multiple times.

Description: The Archer, formerly known as the Holiday Archer, is a tower that attacks enemies with a bow. It could have been unlocked from the Gift of Sharpness, which costed 2,500 Tickets, as part of the Christmas 2019 Event. The gift could have also been bought via a limited time gamepass for 250 Robux. It could later be bought through a different limited time gamepass, which was sold multiple times.

The Archer shoots arrows that damage and pierce through enemies, making the Archer a multi-target tower. The firerate of the Archer is separated into two halves. The first half is the Archer loading the bow with an arrow. This can happen even if there are no enemies in the Archer's range. If it starts attacking with its bow loaded, its firerate will be effectively halved for that shot. The second half is the Archer aiming the bow, and then firing it. This can only happen if there are enemies in its range, unlike the first half. It also boasts a very high range, despite its very low cost.

The arrows it fires will be shot in a straight line. However, if the arrow hits an enemy, it can bounce to another enemy if it is in an ~10 stud radius from the hit enemy. This allows the arrow to change its trajectory and extend how far it goes, making it far more effective at clearing out enemies. If there is no enemy in that range, the arrow will not change directions. The direction of the bounce depends on the enemies. If there are only enemies at the front, it will bounce to the front, if there are only enemies at the back, it will bounce to the back. Meanwhile, if enemies are on both the front and the back, it will be capable of going either way.

At Level 3, the Archer gains the ability to equip different arrows, with the default arrows being replaced by fire arrows at Level 3. These set an enemy on fire, as long as it does not have the Burn Immunity. At Level 4, it can now swap to explosive arrow, which create an explosion upon hitting a single enemy, meaning its piercing is replaced by an explosion which deals damage on top of the arrow. The final arrow is an shock arrow, which stuns enemies for a brief period of time. There is a 10 second cooldown before arrows can be switched again.

The main drawback of this tower is that arrows are projectile-based and will take a short time to reach their intended location. The Archer can detect Hidden enemies at Level 2+. It can also damage Lead enemies at Level 3+ with its flame arrows, though only burn damage can damage them, or through its explosions.
The Archer has a placement limit of 15 per player.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: Due to its cheap cost, Archers can be useful early on during the game.
The Archer's arrow is quite accurate, as it will hit the intended target every single time.

Due to the Archer's arrows bouncing from enemies, the exact placement of the tower is not nearly as important as for other projectile towers like the Harvester or Frost Blaster. It can however still help, as the bouncing benefits from compact path layouts. Such maps include Simplicity and Harbor, as the paths on there are relatively close to each other.
It can however still help, as the bouncing benefits from compact path layouts. Such maps include Simplicity and Harbor, as the paths on there are relatively close to each other.
Natural obstacles, such as hills, do not interfere with the Archer's arrow; it passes right through them.

At Level 3+, the arrows fired by the Archer will gain the ability to set enemies on fire, if set to flame arrows. This can allow it to deal more DPS to each enemy hit. It also has the highest max hits, allowing it to hit more enemies than the other arrows in most cases. Do note that the burn damage cannot be applied to enemies with Burn Immunity, making the Archer weaker against them. The Archer's burn damage does not stack with other Archers or with towers that deal burn damage, like the Pyromancer. This may hinder some towers' performance, such as the Golden Pyromancer, in which the burning damage dealt is superior compared to that of the Archer. Because flame arrows do not stack with other Archers, it is recommended to only have one or a few Archers with flame arrows, with the rest using different arrows.

At Level 5, it gains the shock arrows, which can stun enemies. While the shock is quite short, it can still be useful at stunning if the arrows do not hit the enemy at the same time, but instead hit them separately, applying the stun multiple times and keeping the enemy stunned for a long time, though this can be tricky to pull off. If an enemy has the Stun Immunity, it will not be stunned but instead only slowed down. For Bosses, they do get slowed down, but the slowdown is weaker on them.

At Level 4+, it gains the explosive arrows, which explode upon hitting the first enemy. The explosion does not replace the arrow damage, meaning the explosive arrow are actually quite effective against single target enemies. It also bypasses defense with its explosion, making it useful against high health defense enemies like the Fallen Hero.

Trivia: This tower could have been a reference to Robin Hood. This may also have been based on the exclusive Archer tower from Tower Battles.
When Hardcore Testing BETA was initially released, the Archer was available for 1 Coins if you did not have it.

When initially released, the Archer could pierce through infinite enemies so long as they were within its range. This was changed on the 4th of March 2020. Now, it can only pierce through a limited number of enemies.

After the Overhaul Update, the Archer supposedly had "special arrows" between Level 4-5. This supposedly gave arrows the ability to inflict an effect on enemies (such as stuns and explosions). However, this was only available for special skins that were not yet made. It was then promptly removed in the next update. One of the special arrow effects would later return on the 7th of April 2023, with flame arrows that inflict burn damage, and another two more on the 15th of January 2025, with arrows that explode and stun enemies on impact.

The Archer's Level 5 upgrade name, Shot of the Century, is named after an ability name given to The Umbra on the Tower Defense Simulator Wiki. This, in turn, is named after the phrase " shot heard round the world " by Ralph Waldo Emerson, in the context of the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand leading to World War I and indirectly leading to most 20th century conflicts.

swarmer.name: Swarmer
swarmer.description: The Swarmer is an event damage over time tower that could have been obtained by triumphing Eggy Island 's Hard difficulty as part of the Spring 2020 Event. It could have also been bought via a gamepass for 350 Robux during Spring 2020, and can most recently be bought again for 799 Robux.

Description: The Swarmer is an event damage over time tower that could have been obtained by triumphing Eggy Island 's Hard difficulty as part of the Spring 2020 Event. It could have also been bought via a gamepass for 350 Robux during Spring 2020, and can most recently be bought again for 799 Robux.

The Swarmer deals damage by throwing beehives and later by firing bees, additionally applying a single stack of bees on an enemy. The struck enemy is then inflicted with the Bee Debuff effect, taking damage over time without requiring the Swarmer to directly attack it. The bee stack has a set duration for each level, in which it will then decay with the individual Bee Debuff effect expiring along with it. The enemy will be damaged each Tick, the interval between each sting for a given amount of time, known as Sting Time. This functions similarly to other forms of tick damage, such as the Pyromancer 's burn damage.

The Swarmer can apply multiple bee stacks at a single enemy, with each Swarmer having a cap that increases every level. Other Swarmers can contribute to the stack, exceeding the initial maximum stack in an instance where there is only one Swarmer, and multiple bee stacks will inflict all of their collective DPS on a single target. When there are multiple stacks applied, Sting Time does not apply to each one. Instead, after the first stack's Sting Time ends, a single stack will be removed and the timer will restart. The Bee Debuff effect will persist so long as there is at least one extant stack. There is a limit of 10,000 stacks per enemy. This can damage Lead enemies and bypasses Defense.

The Swarmer additionally has the Bee Swarm Grenade (internally just Swarm) ability, where it throws a grenade that deals AOE damage and applies a single stack of bees to all enemies caught in the explosion radius. The Bee Debuff's stats from Bee Swarm Grenade is directly proportional to the current level of the Swarmer that it was thrown from. The bee swarm grenade's explosion deals explosion damage, bypassing defense, dealing damage to Lead while also having no damage drop off.

Due to its stacking capabilities, the Swarmer is generally considered to be a boss killer, being able to do quite high DPS when a lot of Bee Debuff effects are stacked. Additionally, it also has decent early game potential. It, however, is heavily hindered by its lack of detections and generally not being that strong with a low amount of extant bee stacks.
Ability: Throws a bee swarm grenade that deals area damage and inflicts the stinging effect on enemies that were hit by it, dealing damage over time. The explosion deals damage to Lead, bypasses defense and has no damage drop off.
Strategy: The Swarmer is generally not the most effective option for earlier parts of the game due to its slow firerate, rather low range and low sting damage. If used, it should be set to Strongest so that it can hit as many enemies as possible or prioritize stronger enemies to apply more bee debuff effects to. First Enemy targeting would make it always target the first enemy, which can be ineffective as some damage will be wasted if you have more than enough stacks. Later on, as Swarmer excels in single target damage, it is best to keep all Swarmers placed on Strongest. It can, however, become a very strong tower once higher health enemies such as the Fallen Squire and Slow Boss start to appear.

The Swarmer will reapply the bee debuff effect to an enemy if it attacks the same enemy, allowing it to be stacked. Only the sting time for one effect can be active on an enemy. If there are 100 stacks, the earliest one will be active. This effectively means that constantly applying the effect can extend it. This allows it to reach extremely high DPS values, even being able to take down the bosses like the Fallen King and Molten Warlord somewhat quickly. For example, ten Level 5 Swarmers, after firing at a boss for just 12 seconds, will have applied roughly 100 stacks of bees, dealing a total of 400 DPS from just the incomplete stack alone.

The Commander can be extremely useful with the Swarmer, as it allows it to apply its effects at a faster rate, making its rampup much faster. The DJ Booth can be used to boost it, however its effects are far less effective on it due to the Damage Buff only buffing its main attack (which has its damage revoked at Level 3) and Bee Swarm Grenade, so it is recommended to use Purple track instead if the Swarmer is your only or primary DPS source. The Green track can additionally help with affording the extreme amount of Swarmers required to reach the tower's full potential.

The Bee Swarm Grenade ability can be used to quickly apply the stinging effect to multiple enemies, allowing the Swarmer to start dealing more damage faster. If multiple Swarmers are placed down, using abilities from multiple of them can allow you to mass apply the effect to multiple enemies at once. Additionally, as only one effect can expire at once, it will last for quite a while before it ends.

The Swarmer is unaffected by some debuffs applied by enemies, but not all. For example, Wox the Fox will be unable to apply the Scared Debuff to it, but the Boomer can apply all its debuffs without any issues.
Trivia: The original design of Swarmer is based on R2DA's Swarmer in name and appearance. Additionally, the Swarmer's Level 5 outfit was very similar to R2DA's Beekeeper Suit.

The store description is taken from a scene involving Nicholas Cage in the film The Wicker Man.
Immediately after the Swarmer's addition, it could have been bought for 2,500 Coins. However, this was soon removed, and anyone who acquired the Swarmer this way was refunded.

The Swarmer's stinging mechanic was originally a bug that allowed the Swarmer to stack the effect multiple times. This would be removed in v1.9.0 with the tower debuff reworks, though later brought back in v1.52.0.
The Swarmer has the highest cost efficiency in the entire game, at $3,808.63 on Level 5.
The Swarmer is currently the only tower to have one of its upgrades remove its direct damage.

↑ DPS assumes that only one enemy is currently being stung and only one stack is applied. It is calculated as (Damage ÷ Firerate) + (Bee Damage ÷ Tick)
↑ How much DPS is added every second through it applying bee stacks. It is calculated as (Bee Damage ÷ Tick) ÷ Firerate
↑ DPS when every single stack is applied for one Swarmer. It is calculated as (Damage ÷ Firerate) + [(Bee Damage ÷ Tick) × Stack Limit]

tooltips: A cheap single target DPS tower that shoots bees that apply a damage over time debuff on enemies.
Swarmers can stack multiple bees on a target increasing the strength of the damage over time.
Later levels also gain a bee grenade that applies the debuff to multiple enemies.

Swarmer has been made unobtainable from the game as of the 26th of May 2020 as it was part of the Spring 2020 Event. Players with the item in question can continue using it, but you cannot obtain this item anymore, outside of limited-time promotional sales.

upgrades.name: Bee Swarm Grenade
description: Throws a bee swarm grenade that deals area damage and inflicts the stinging effect on enemies that were hit by it, dealing damage over time. The explosion deals damage to Lead, bypasses defense and has no damage drop off.

toxic_gunner.description: The Toxic Gunner is a ground tower that fires toxic bullets in bursts, applying poison on enemies. It was unlocked by triumphing Trick or Threat Town as part of the Halloween 2020 Event. It was also obtainable through a gamepass for 500 Robux during the Solar Eclipse Event. Most recently, it was brought back for 699 Robux during the Backyard Legends Event.

Description: The Toxic Gunner is a ground tower that fires toxic bullets in bursts, applying poison on enemies. It was unlocked by triumphing Trick or Threat Town as part of the Halloween 2020 Event. It was also obtainable through a gamepass for 500 Robux during the Solar Eclipse Event. Most recently, it was brought back for 699 Robux during the Backyard Legends Event.

The Toxic Gunner fires in bursts with a short delay between each burst. These shots apply poison to enemies, which slows them down by 10% at Level 0, getting higher with levels, reaching 30% at Level 4. Only major bosses like the Patient Zero and the Fallen King are immune to this, however they are not immune to its attacks. This poison also deals damage over time to the enemy which deals 1 damage every second for 6 seconds at Level 0, reaching 10 damage every second for 10 seconds at Level 4. It can also decrease an enemy's defense at Level 3, decreasing it by 3% each poison tick. It can only decrease up to 50% of an enemy's defense. This tower does not have hidden detection, requiring the use of other towers to attack hidden enemies, like the Minigunner.

This is considered an all-rounder support tower. Because of its cheap cost and decent DPS, it can be used as an early-game tower and even in mid-game. Later on, it can be used to deal additional DPS to enemies. However, the slowing effect and defense melting allows the Toxic Gunner to have some use, even during the late-game, as a support tower, paired with high damage towers like Ranger and Accelerator.
The Toxic Gunner has lead detection from Level 0 and flying detection from Level 3. It has no placement limit.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: Because of its cheap cost and high DPS for its cost, the Toxic Gunner is a viable early to mid-game tower. The Toxic Gunner's ability to slow down most enemies and decrease their defense allows it to be an all-round tower. However, the Toxic Gunner does not gain hidden detection at any level. For suitable hidden detection, other towers must be used, such as the Minigunner. A Firework Technician or Level 4+ Ace Pilot can help the Toxic Gunner by giving it hidden detection if the Toxic Gunner is in its secondary range. The UAV can do the same temporarily, while also providing flying detection and giving 30% more range. However, it can only be used 4 times, so you cannot solely rely on the UAV.

The Toxic Gunner's firerate can be boosted by the Commander, allowing more enemies to be affected by slowness. The Toxic Gunner's cooldown cannot be boosted by the Commander. However, this is not an issue at Level 4, as the Toxic Gunner has no burst cooldown at that Level.

The Toxic Gunner's defense melting can be useful against enemies with defense, such as the Fallen Rusher, as it can decrease it quite quickly while slowing the enemy down. When combined with other defense melting towers, like the Pyromancer, it can remove all of the enemy's defense. The defense melting does not stack with the Jester 's defense melting.

It is recommended to have one Toxic Gunner with targeting set to Random to slow down as many enemies as possible.

Combined with the Freezer, Jester, Slime Trooper and Electroshocker, this tower can cause some enemies to be essentially immobilized. The slowing effect from the Toxic Gunner gives these towers more time to attack the enemies, increasing the duration of time that enemies are immobilized. This works quite well when paired with Hacker 's slowdown, further slowing affected enemies and aiding Hacker in the conversion of enemies.

The Toxic Gunner can be used to defeat Lead and Flying enemies, as both its normal damage and poison damage can damage them. This can make Toxic Gunner viable in Hardcore Mode, for late-game support and early game lead defense.

Trivia: The Toxic Gunner was supposed to be released during the Halloween 2020 Event, but it was postponed to the Frost Invasion Event due to it being unfinished. The Toxic Gunner is the only event tower to be released after its event has concluded, also being unobtainable immediately after it had released. As a result, if you had beaten the Halloween 2020 Event before the 8th of May 2021 (when the Frost Invasion event released), you would have had to wait until then to obtain this tower.

The Level 3 upgrade name, Sinister Gear may be a reference to Lord Sinister, the boss of the Halloween 2020 Event where Toxic Gunner was obtained.
The Level 4 upgrade name, Going Nuclear! is a reference to the Going Nuclear! soundtrack that plays in Polluted Wasteland II.
The Toxic Gunner has had a defense melting statistic since it was added; however, it was unused until the 24th of November 2023.

The Toxic Gunner is the only tower that cannot detect nor indirectly hit Hidden enemies at all. There is one rare situation where the Toxic Gunner can damage Hidden enemies, where it applies its poison debuff to an enemy which initially is not a Hidden enemy, but turns into one later.

sledger.name: Sledger
sledger.description: The Sledger is a melee ground tower that attacks enemies with a sledgehammer which has a freeze effect on later levels. It was originally unlocked by triumphing Outpost 32 as part of the Frost Invasion Event. During the Frost Invasion Event, the Sledger was purchasable via a limited time gamepass for 500 Robux. It is could most recently be bought through a limited time gamepass for 749 Robux.

Description: The Sledger is a melee ground tower that attacks enemies with a sledgehammer which has a freeze effect on later levels. It was originally unlocked by triumphing Outpost 32 as part of the Frost Invasion Event. During the Frost Invasion Event, the Sledger was purchasable via a limited time gamepass for 500 Robux. It is could most recently be bought through a limited time gamepass for 749 Robux.

The Sledger attacks enemies by simply bashing them with its sledgehammer. It hits enemies in a cone with an angle of 60°. This applies a chillness slowness effect, which stacks up to 35% at Level 0. At Level 3+, when the slowness is higher than max slowness, it will freeze the enemy instead. Enemies immune to freeze cannot be frozen or slowed down, while larger enemies get frozen for a shorter amount of time than average sized enemies.

At Level 4+, it deals double normal damage to frozen and chilled enemies through its Ice Breaker passive ability, whether they are frozen/chilled from the Sledger or any other tower that inflicts these effects (like the Freezer). At Level 5, it now has an Aftershock passive ability, which, every single time the Sledger attacks, a large frost shard pattern will trail in the direction the Sledger hit, dealing 40% of the Sledgers damage. This damage always rounds up, no matter the decimal. Though, it has a 0.4 second delay before it deals damage. Aftershock damage is not affected by Ice Breaker. It also applies chillness, which has identical stats to the base attack.

Starting from Level 0, it has the ability to hit three enemies in a single swing (but due to a bug, it is higher than intended by one at all levels), which increases with upgrades. It also gains lead detection on Level 0, but never hidden or flying detections.

The Sledger is considered a viable mid-late game tower due to its average cost and good DPS. In later waves, its DPS is overshadowed by many other towers, but it makes up for this by having the ability to freeze enemies at Level 3+, being able to deal double damage to frozen enemies at Level 4+, and having amazing AOE range at Level 5. The Sledger pairs well with other Sledgers and the Commander.
The Sledger has a placement limit of six per player.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Sledger does not gain hidden detection at any level, meaning it cannot detect Hidden enemies, such as the Phantom. However, if another detectable enemy is in range, then a Hidden enemy may be indirectly hit by the Sledger. The Hidden enemy can also be frozen, so long as the Sledger is Level 3+. A Level 4+ Ace Pilot near the Sledger will grant permanent hidden detection but it requires the Sledger to be in its secondary orange range.
However, if another detectable enemy is in range, then a Hidden enemy may be indirectly hit by the Sledger. The Hidden enemy can also be frozen, so long as the Sledger is Level 3+.

A Level 4+ Ace Pilot near the Sledger will grant permanent hidden detection but it requires the Sledger to be in its secondary orange range.

The Sledger can slowdown enemies from Level 0 and freeze enemies at Level 3. This makes it useful as a support tower, letting your towers deal more damage to enemies. This is especially effective against hordes of slow enemies, like the Slow Boss. It instantly freezes enemies when hit, making it even better at freezing. The Sledger can be useful against fast high-health enemies like the Fallen Tank or the Amalgamation due to their fast speed getting negated by the Sledger's freeze and slowdown. Be aware that enemies with Freeze Immunity cannot be frozen or slowed down, such as the Void Trickster. While Boss enemies are immune to freeze by default, they are not immune to the chillness effect entirely unless they also have the Freeze Immunity. They can be slowed down, however, the effect will be much weaker than other enemies. You can also use stunning towers like the Electroshocker and Warden to slow them down even further, though this is generally not necessary. Be aware that enemies that are already frozen do not have their freeze times increased when hit by the Sledger.

At Level 4, the Sledger can deal double damage to frozen and chilled enemies, allowing it to deal high amounts of damage. Due to this, the Sledger works very well with other freezing towers, along with other Sledgers nearby. Combining the Sledger with the Commander will also allow it to hit frozen enemies several times in a short period of time, which can result in high amounts of damage being dealt in a short period of time. While Damage Buffs can increase this damage, their effectiveness is halved on it. For example, a Level 5 Sledger will only deal 330 damage to frozen and chilled enemies instead of 360 when its damage is increased by 20%. However, enemies that have Freeze Immunity cannot be frozen or chilled, meaning they are not able to take the extra damage from Sledger.

The Sledger creates a trail of ice when it attacks at Level 5 with its Aftershock. In most cases, this just acts as additional damage, though it has its own additional uses. This makes it quite effective against breaker enemies, as its main attack can damage the breaker while its Aftershock attack can damage the other breaks it summons. The Aftershock can hit enemies that come into its attack range later, allowing them to be receive some damage even if they were not hit by the initial attack. The Aftershock damage is increased by the same amount as the main attack. This means that it gets massively higher Damage Buffs than regular, making Damage Buffs a great way to boost the damage of the Sledger.

The Sledger has a small placement footprint, meaning that it can squeeze in beside other towers quite easily, if space is a problem.

It is best when the Sledger is placed near by corners because it maximizes its range. Clumping Sledgers close together is a good method for maximizing damage output. It is best to clump Sledgers near towers that deal high DPS, like the Accelerator (which also gives it time to charge up) and Ranger. To slow the most enemies down for the longest period of time, it is best to spread out Sledgers.

Trivia: The Sledger old Level 2 icon used to be the same as the Archer 's Level 3 icon.
The Sledger used to share most of its upgrade icons with the Gladiator.
The Sledger is the third melee tower to be added to the game, with the first being Gladiator, the second being Slasher, then Warden and Brawler were added after.
The sound of the Sledger that hits an enemy was the same sound as the Vindicator when towers caught hit when using ability.

The Sledger old Level 4 and 5 upgrade names are references to the Frost Invasion Event. The old Level 4 upgrade name, Outpost 32 Research, is a reference to the Outpost 32, a research facility used as a map for the Frost Invasion Event and the Operation I.C.E Event. The old Level 5 upgrade name, Into The Frost Dimension, is a reference to the dimension enemies from the Frost Invasion Event came from.

executioner.name: Executioner
executioner.description: The Executioner is a ranged ground tower that was unlocked by triumphing Totality Tower. It could have also been obtained through a gamepass for 750 Robux during the Solar Eclipse Event. The Executioner's most recent sale has it require 799 Robux to purchase.

Description: The Executioner is a ranged ground tower that was unlocked by triumphing Totality Tower. It could have also been obtained through a gamepass for 750 Robux during the Solar Eclipse Event. The Executioner's most recent sale has it require 799 Robux to purchase.

The Executioner attacks by throwing its axe at an enemy, hitting the enemy and bouncing to other enemies. If there is only one enemy in its range, the axe will simply deal damage once. For cases of there being two or more enemies, it will bounce between a specific number of max targets for a specific number of times. For instance, with a max bounce statistic of 15, it will bounce 15 times, however, due to its max targets statistic being 5 in this scenario, it will only bounce 15 times between 5 enemies. With each hit, the axe will boost its damage by a specific number.

The Executioner will with each throw start a small windup before throwing, which is followed by the axe flying between enemies. This has a max flight time of 0.4 for each target. Once it has hit the last enemy, it will take a max of 0.55 seconds to return to the tower, making the Executioner catch it for 0.1 seconds. Once the axe has been caught, the proper firerate will begin.

The Executioner's high damage and ability to damage multiple enemies makes it a great tower for area of effect. However, it is very weak against singular enemies, with its DPS being significantly reduced if there is just one enemy in its range. The Executioner has hidden detection at Level 3 and flying detection at Level 0.
The Executioner has a placement limit of 9 per player.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: Because of how the Executioner works, it is strictly an AOE tower, requiring at least two enemies to properly reach its full potential. Using it on a single enemy will result in extremely low DPS due to the axe not being able to bounce on one enemy. This makes the Executioner a horrible choice for any single target enemies.
Using it on a single enemy will result in extremely low DPS due to the axe not being able to bounce on one enemy. This makes the Executioner a horrible choice for any single target enemies.

Each hit of the Executioner's axe can trigger a firework from the Firework Technician. Since usually the axe will be hitting multiple times, it will drastically increase the odds of getting a firework by sheer quantity, which will also greatly increase the Executioner's damage output.
Since usually the axe will be hitting multiple times, it will drastically increase the odds of getting a firework by sheer quantity, which will also greatly increase the Executioner's damage output.
Due to the Executioner's ability to damage multiple enemies, this can be used as a great tower to clear out hordes of weaker enemies and even minor bosses at Level 5.

The Executioner gains hidden detection at Level 3, however because of how expensive it is to upgrade it to that level, it is recommended to bring other towers with cheap hidden detection. Later on in the game, the Executioner can deal with hordes of high health hidden enemies, like the Soul and Elite Phantom. Although the axe itself may travel through them, the axe will only end up damaging the enemy it bounced to, meaning it cannot be used to indirectly kill such enemies.
Later on in the game, the Executioner can deal with hordes of high health hidden enemies, like the Soul and Elite Phantom.
Although the axe itself may travel through them, the axe will only end up damaging the enemy it bounced to, meaning it cannot be used to indirectly kill such enemies.
The Executioner can do well against enemies that summon other enemies on death, like the Mystery, as it can both damage the Mystery and the enemy it spawned if you are lucky enough.

The Executioner can detect flying enemies, making it useful in Hardcore mode against enemies like the Void Floater and in Pizza Party against Balloon Kids. However, the Executioner cannot damage Lead enemies.
However, the Executioner cannot damage Lead enemies.

Towers that can slow down enemies, like the Electroshocker, Toxic Gunner or Sledger are very useful with the Executioner, as they let enemies stay in its range for longer and helping to make sure there are more than one enemy in its range at once. Range boosting towers like the DJ Booth can also be useful for this.
Range boosting towers like the DJ Booth can also be useful for this.

Due to the Executioner only having its firerate start once it has caught its axe, which will only start once the windup ends, then the axe stops travelling and is caught. This results in the Executioner being very ineffective with Firerate Buffs. Damage Buff however are very effective with it, as not only will they boost the damage itself but also how much damage is increased per hit. For instance, a 20% Damage Buff will boost the damage itself from 50 to 60 and the added damage from 15 to 18 at Level 5.

Damage Buff however are very effective with it, as not only will they boost the damage itself but also how much damage is increased per hit. For instance, a 20% Damage Buff will boost the damage itself from 50 to 60 and the added damage from 15 to 18 at Level 5.
Trivia: The Executioner is the second ground tower that can detect flying enemies, with the first being the Hunter.

The Executioner may originally have based been on the Executioner card from Clash Royale and the Boomerang Thrower from the Bloons Tower Defense game series. The former store description of the Executioner is a reference to the Avatar: The Last Airbender franchise. The Executioner's flying detection may have also been based on the Executioner card's ability to attack air troops.

The Executioner has a love for rodents, specifically guinea pigs, rats, and hamsters, as revealed by his concept artist, @tyronedag0at on X.
