elf_camp.name: Elf Camp
elf_camp.description: The Elf Camp is a unit spawning tower that could have been unlocked by triumphing Cold Ambush during the Violent Night Event. After a player had returned to the lobby, it was claimed through the Gift Box menu. It could also have been obtained through a limited time gamepass for 500 Robux during the Violent Night Event and Krampus' Revenge Event, and for 799 Robux during the The Final Act Event.

Description: The Elf Camp is a unit spawning tower that could have been unlocked by triumphing Cold Ambush during the Violent Night Event. After a player had returned to the lobby, it was claimed through the Gift Box menu. It could also have been obtained through a limited time gamepass for 500 Robux during the Violent Night Event and Krampus' Revenge Event, and for 799 Robux during the The Final Act Event.

The Elf Camp is a spawner tower that summons elves. These elves are modernized versions of the enemies that appeared in the Violent Night Event. At Level 0, it only summons the Elf. However, with later Levels, it can spawn multiple units at once instead of just one. The functionality of these units varies, making each unit unique. With Levels, some units will be replaced by their stronger variants.

For the first upgrade, the Elf Camp only summons Elves, which can only collide with enemies. This unit is later replaced with the Guardian Elf, which can also damage enemies with its sword. At Level 1, it can spawn an additional unit, the Snowball Elf, that throws snowballs at enemies from a distance, dealing damage. It is replaced by the Cannoneer Elf at Level 2, which deals more DPS, and by the Gunner Elf at Level 3, which fires in bursts and at Level 4 spawns twice, dealing even more DPS. At Level 2, it can also spawn the Bomber Elf, which explodes upon death, dealing damage to enemies in its explosion radius. It is replaced by the Gift Bomber at Level 4, which instead throws present bombs and flies in a sleigh, allowing it to avoid colliding with non- Boss enemies. It does not explode upon death. At Level 4, it can also spawn its final unit, the Ripped Elf, which throws a large snow boulder at enemies, dealing a large amount of damage to any caught in the explosion radius.

The Elf Camp is considerably an early to mid-game tower as its cheap cost and units such as the Snowball Elf or Bomber Elf can be quite useful in the early-game, while its later units like the Ripped Elf or Gunner Elf can be quite useful in the mid-game.
There is a limit of four Elf Camps per player.
Strategy: The Elf Camp can be an effective counter against defense enemies, as its units deal full damage when colliding with enemies. Splash Damage from the Bomber Elf or Ripped Elf is also not affected by Defense. Damage from the Guardian Elf and ranged elves like the Snowball Elf or Gunner Elf is still affected.
Splash Damage from the Bomber Elf or Ripped Elf is also not affected by Defense.
Damage from the Guardian Elf and ranged elves like the Snowball Elf or Gunner Elf is still affected.
It is best advised to place the Elf Camp away from the main path, as it has no use close to it.
The Elf Camp can be very useful against Hidden enemies due to most of its units having hidden detection. The Gift Bomber can also detect Flying enemies while the Elf Camp is at Level 4.
The Gift Bomber can also detect Flying enemies while the Elf Camp is at Level 4.
Do note that some enemies can damage units. As most of the Elf Camp units have low health, they will often be killed instantly.
Despite being a flying unit, the Gift Bomber is affected by enemy abilities that damage units, even if it does not look like was not hit by it.

The Bomber Elf 's splash damage can be quite useful at clearing out hordes of enemies that appear early on. Later on, the Ripped Elf and Gift Bomber can also prove useful for the stronger hordes of Slow Bosses, although it takes a while for the projectiles to hit, meaning they could miss faster enemies. The Ripped Elf 's snowballs may not hit the path most of the time.

Later on, the Ripped Elf and Gift Bomber can also prove useful for the stronger hordes of Slow Bosses, although it takes a while for the projectiles to hit, meaning they could miss faster enemies. The Ripped Elf 's snowballs may not hit the path most of the time.
The Ripped Elf 's snowballs may not hit the path most of the time.
The Electroshocker, Frost Blaster, Freezer and Toxic Gunner pair well with the Elf Camp as they slow down enemies before colliding with units, allowing the units to survive longer.
Units spawned by the Elf Camp are not affected by any buffs or debuffs.

Units spawned by the Elf Camp are far less effective against Ghost enemies as they cannot collide with them and only some of the units can detect them. The Gift Bomber, despite being a flying unit, cannot collide with Flying enemies. However, they are effective against Lead enemies, as collision and splash damage deals damage to them.
The Gift Bomber, despite being a flying unit, cannot collide with Flying enemies.
However, they are effective against Lead enemies, as collision and splash damage deals damage to them.
As the Gift Bomber is a flying unit, it cannot collide with most enemies. It can only collide with Boss enemies, like the Molten Warlord or Fallen King.
The two Gunner Elves that spawn are not one unit but two. This means the DPS of both units is effectively doubled at Level 4.
This means the DPS of both units is effectively doubled at Level 4.
Trivia: The elves spawned by this tower are based on multiple enemies that appear in the Violent Night Event. The Elf is based on the Basic Elf. The Bomber Elf is based on the enemy of the same name. The Guardian Elf is based on the Cookie Guard The Gift Bomber is based on the Sleigh. The Ripped Elf is based on the enemy of the same name. The Ripped Elf is the first humanoid unit to use a body similar to R15. The Snowball Elf, Cannoneer Elf and Gunner Elf do not appear to be based on any enemies from the event. Though the Gunner Elf does use the same accessories as the Builder Elf.

jester.name: Jester
jester.description: The Jester is an exclusive splash damage tower previously obtainable by triumphing the third act of the Lunar Overture Event. It could also have been obtained through a limited-time gamepass for 750 Robux during Lunar Overture Event. Most recently it could be bought for 749 Robux as part of the 2025 Halloween event countdown.

Description: The Jester is an exclusive splash damage tower previously obtainable by triumphing the third act of the Lunar Overture Event. It could also have been obtained through a limited-time gamepass for 750 Robux during Lunar Overture Event. Most recently it could be bought for 749 Robux as part of the 2025 Halloween event countdown.

The Jester is a tower mostly based around debuffs. It throws a bomb at enemies, two at Level 4, which can be configured to apply one of the four debuffs it can apply to enemies. Most of these bombs also deal splash damage, which makes them able to deal damage to lead enemies. However, unlike most other splash towers, the Jester's splash damage is always the same, regardless of how far away the enemy is from the center. Additionally, the Jester's bombs do not ignore defense and can only hit five enemies.
The first is the fire bomb, which sets enemies on fire.

The second bomb is the ice bomb, which is unlocked at Level 2. It slows down enemies by 25% for 2 seconds, which stacks up to 25% and deals 20% of the fire bomb damage. From Level 3, it starts to reduce enemy Defense, reducing up to 33% of it.
The third bomb is the poison bomb, unlocked at Level 3. It creates a puddle of acid, which damages enemies. The puddle lasts for 30 seconds. Additionally, it does not deal splash damage.

The fourth and final bomb is the confusion bomb, unlocked at Level 4. This bomb causes the enemies to walk towards the entrance for 2 seconds, with an 6-second cooldown before it can be reapplied on an enemy; however, Boss enemies will not be affected by the confusion. It deals no damage.
The Jester has hidden detection at Level 3.

The Jester is considered an all-round tower, as its cheap cost means it can be used early on to defend, while in mid and late-game multiple of its bombs can be used to effectively clear out hordes or to weaken enemies, by slowing them down or reducing their defense.
The Jester has a placement limit of eight per player.
Ability: Swaps out the current bomb type to the selected bomb type.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Jester has four bombs that have unique effects on enemies. The fire bomb deals burn damage, which is half of the Jester's damage. The ice bomb slows down enemies, though its damage is 20% of the Jester's damage. The poison bomb, instead of exploding, creates a poisonous puddle that damages enemies and reduces defense. Damage is 30% of the Jester's damage. The confusion bomb causes non-boss enemies to go towards the entrance instead of the exit, though it deals no damage.

If the bomb for a slot is changed, the Jester will not change the bomb or bombs it is currently holding until it throws them. The Equip Bombs ability can be used to make the Jester change its bombs instantly.
While the Jester can indirectly hit flying enemies with its explosions, this should not be completely relied on, and you should use other flying detecting towers instead.
The Jester, for most bombs, is a splash damage tower, allowing it to deal damage to lead enemies. It also bypasses Defense, though its poison damage does not.
It also bypasses Defense, though its poison damage does not.
Poison bombs can be quite good against crowds, as their poisonous puddles can deal a lot of damage when stacked.

The ice bomb can decrease up to 33% of an enemy's defense through its chill, making it very useful against enemies with high defense. If you use another defense melting tower, like the Pyromancer, you can remove most of the enemy's defense or remove it entirely. However, do note that the Jester's defense melting does not stack with other chilling towers.

The Jester can be very useful at slowing down enemies because of its ice and confusion bombs, especially when used together. Do note that the ice bomb will make confused enemies walk slower, making them walk a shorter distance to the entrance, reducing the confusion bomb's effectiveness. However, as the confusion bomb has a cooldown before it can be applied again, the ice bomb can still be useful at slowing while confusion bomb is on cooldown. The ice bomb cannot slow down enemies that are immune to freeze, as the regular Freeze Immunity also prevents enemies from being slowed down by the chillness slowdown. However, bosses can still be slowed down by it, as long as they do not have the regular Freeze Immunity, as boss enemies are only affected less by the chillness slowdown. The confusion bomb will make enemies walk towards the entrance instead of the exit, with the distance depending on the enemy's speed. Because of this, faster enemies will be more affected by it than slower ones. If a confused enemy reaches the entrance, it will change directions and move towards the exit, even if currently confused. Therefore, Jesters with confusion bombs should not be placed next to the entrance, so that the confusion effect does not get wasted by this. Having multiple Jesters with ice or confusion bombs can be quite useful at slowing down hordes, due to the bomb's max hits of five.

The Jester has somewhat low range even at Level 4, so proper placement is important to effectively utilize its range. The DJ Booth can alleviate this low range while also lowering upgrade costs. The Level 2 Ranger 's buff can be used, but it is far less effective since it does not give as much range and is temporary for each wave.

The Commander can help alleviate the Jester's somewhat slow firerate.
When using multiple Level 4 Jesters, it is recommended that each Jester has varied combinations of bombs, like poison and ice bombs, to ensure they can be at their most efficient.

The Jester may struggle against fast enemies like the Quick, Enraged or Bolt because of its low range, slow firerate and ability to throw projectiles, allowing them to get out of their range quickly, at times without any damage dealt to them. However, multiple Jesters can be quite effective against them. Towers like the Tesla, Warden or Sledger can be useful at giving Jesters more time to hit enemies.

When an enemy is confused, it could walk back towards the acid puddle, regenerating its health, meaning confusion bombs are not recommended against them. Ice bombs can be used as an alternative against such enemies, though as it makes enemies walk slower, they will walk on it for a longer amount of time, allowing them to heal more. cryomancer.name: Cryomancer
cryomancer.description: The Cryomancer is an exclusive support tower which attacks enemies with a frost beam. It could have been obtained by triumphing Krampus Frosthold. It could have also been obtained via a gamepass for 500 Robux during the Krampus' Revenge Event. Most recently, the Cryomancer was put on sale in December of 2024, costing 699 Robux to purchase.

Description: The Cryomancer is an exclusive support tower which attacks enemies with a frost beam. It could have been obtained by triumphing Krampus Frosthold. It could have also been obtained via a gamepass for 500 Robux during the Krampus' Revenge Event. Most recently, the Cryomancer was put on sale in December of 2024, costing 699 Robux to purchase.

The Cryomancer fires a frost beam which applies the chillness slowness effect to enemies every hit, which stacks up to its maximum slowdown. This beam can only hit three enemies every tick at Level 0–3, increasing to six at Level 4. At Level 4, when the enemy's slowdown is higher than max slowdown, the enemy will freeze. Larger enemies will be frozen for a shorter amount of time than average sized enemies. Enemies with Freeze Immunity also cannot be frozen or slowed down. It also has a limited amount of ammo, which means that when it runs out of its ammo, it will have to reload. It only reloads when it runs out of ammo. At Level 2+, its freezing effects will deal tick damage every second. It can also damage Lead enemies from Level 0, though due to it not having any damage at Level 0, in reality it cannot damage them until Level 2. It cannot detect Hidden or Flying enemies. The Cryomancer will melt 5% defense every tick, increasing the value it decrease it by with upgrades. It can only melt an enemy's defense by 33%. For example, if an enemy has 50% defense, it will be decreased by 16%.
As this tower's damage is quite weak meaning it can only be used to clear out earlier waves, this tower is mostly considered a support tower.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: This tower should not be used as early-game defense, as it deals no damage until Level 2. At Level 2, the Cryomancer can fend off against weaker enemies like the Normal or Abnormal, though while it can deal some damage to stronger ones like the Normal Boss, its low DPS will make killing it very long. Because of this, the Cryomancer should be used mostly as a support tower alongside other towers.

Multiple Cryomancers can be quite effective at slowing down hordes of enemies. Do note that enemies with the Freeze Immunity cannot be slowed down or frozen by the Cryomancer. Larger enemies are also frozen for a shorter amount of time than average-sized enemies. Bosses are immune to being frozen by default. However, they are only partially immune to being slowed down by its chillness effect, as it is only weaker on them. Due to this, the Cryomancer can be very useful for slowing down major bosses such as the Fallen King.

The Cryomancer can be useful for decreasing an enemy's defense, allowing your towers to deal more damage to it. It is especially useful as it can melt defense from Level 0, being the cheapest form of defense melting in the game. However, do note that as the defense melting happens when an enemy is frozen or slowed down, freeze immune enemies cannot have their defense reduced. The defense melt can stack with other towers, such as the Pyromancer, Electroshocker or Toxic Gunner, allowing you to remove an enemy's defense entirely. However, the Cryomancer's defense melt does not stack with Frost Blaster 's and Freezer 's defense melt.

The Cryomancer can be quite useful at clumping up enemies, allowing towers like the Mortar or Rocketeer to hit more enemies with their explosions.

The Cryomancer has lead detection from Level 0, allowing it to deal damage to lead enemies when it is upgraded to at least Level 2. However, it does not have hidden detection, only being able to hit these enemies when they are caught in its frost beam. You can use outside means, such as the Firework Technician or the UAV, to remedy this. The Cryomancer cannot damage Flying enemies without flying detection, even if they are caught in the hitbox of the Cryomancer.

hallow_punk.name: Hallow Punk
hallow_punk.description: The Hallow Punk is an exclusive ground tower that deals Splash Damage, which knocks back all enemies hit. It is unlocked by triumphing all the Hexscape Event nights on the Easy difficulty. Most recently, it was obtainable through a limited-time gamepass for 299 Robux.

Description: The Hallow Punk is an exclusive ground tower that deals Splash Damage, which knocks back all enemies hit. It is unlocked by triumphing all the Hexscape Event nights on the Easy difficulty. Most recently, it was obtainable through a limited-time gamepass for 299 Robux.

The Hallow Punk is an early-game Splash Damage tower that deals medium damage to enemies within an explosion radius. However, the Hallow Punk has a slow firerate. All enemies hit by it will be knocked back, with the distance depending on its size, while at Level 2 and above, will have burn applied to them. Additionally, it does not have damage drop off when enemies are away from the center. It does not bypass defense. This tower has lead detection at Level 0+, hidden detection at Level 2+ and flying detection at Level 3, making it effective against all types of enemies.

The Hallow Punk can be effective against low-mid health crowds of enemies, but struggles against high health hordes of enemies. It can however be useful at knocking them back. The Hallow Punk is considered an early-mid-game tower.
The Hallow Punk has a placement limit of ten per player.
Strategy: Due to the Hallow Punk's cheap cost, a few of them placed down can be effective in the early-game, being quite effective against hordes and even high health enemies that appear during early-game.

If the Hallow Punk fires and the enemy is out of range, the missile will still track it down and hit it. Paired with its high range, this makes it near impossible for an enemy to avoid at least one rocket from the Hallow Punk.
Paired with its high range, this makes it near impossible for an enemy to avoid at least one rocket from the Hallow Punk.

The Hallow Punk has lead detection at Level 0, hidden detection at Level 2 and flying detection at Level 3, making it an option against such enemies. It also means it can be used to take down Lead Balloons, though because of its low DPS it will likely be unable to take care of them on its own.
It also means it can be used to take down Lead Balloons, though because of its low DPS it will likely be unable to take care of them on its own.
Changing Hallow Punk's targeting to Strongest, making it deal highest damage possible. Random targeting can also be useful, especially at Level 2+ where it gains burn.
Random targeting can also be useful, especially at Level 2+ where it gains burn.
Trivia: The Hallow Punk is the first tower to have only 3 levels.
During Containment, if Easy difficulty is selected, the Hallow Punk is included in all loadouts as a sixth tower, even if the player had not obtained the Hallow Punk.
Update History: For previous cosmetic variations, see the gallery page.

harvester.description: The Harvester is a tower which fires projectiles at enemies. It could have been obtained by triumphing all Hexscape Event maps on the Hard difficulty. Most recently, it was brought back through a limited time gamepass priced at 799 Robux.

Description: The Harvester is a tower which fires projectiles at enemies. It could have been obtained by triumphing all Hexscape Event maps on the Hard difficulty. Most recently, it was brought back through a limited time gamepass priced at 799 Robux.

The Harvester deals DPS with its projectile. It has an ability to create thorns along with the path of two segments, which slow and deal damage to enemies periodically. These thorns only last for a few seconds on the path. During later levels, the Harvester gains high damage and firerate, and the thorns are enhanced to deal more damage, receive an extended lifespan, cover a larger area, and have more slowdown.

The Harvester's Thorns ability also has an effect on another tower, the Farm. All Farms in its range will create additional thorns on the path. These thorns use the same statistics as the Harvester, except that the damage, duration and range statistics are halved at Level 0, with each Level increasing their power (except the range) by 10%, up to 100%.
The Harvester is considerably a mid-late game tower as its main DPS can be effective during the mid-game while its Thorns ability can be great against weaker and higher health hoards later on.
The Harvester has a placement limit of five per player.
Ability: On use, the selected area will produce thorns that deal damage and slow enemies. All Farms that are both in the range of the Harvester and the track also generate thorns with halved statistics through its Nature's Bond.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Harvester's high DPS allows for it to be an effective DPS for the mid to late-game. Do note however, that it is a projectile tower with the potential of missing enemies. This can make it less reliable than towers like the Accelerator or Ranger, which will not miss the intended target. While not particularly great against hordes, its Thorns ability can be used to compensate for this.

The Harvester is a decent pick against mid to late-game Flying enemies, as it has flying detection from Level 0. It does not, however, have any other detections until Level 3, where it gains the hidden detection, though its Thorns ability can be used to damage Hidden enemies. Do note that the Thorns cannot damage either Flying or Lead enemies.

Its Thorns ability can be an effective counter against Aggro enemies. While it may not be enough to kill stronger ones, such as the Fallen Shield with Aggro, it can be used to damage the crowds of enemies that appear alongside it on any part of the map.

The Harvester's Thorns ability also affects the Farm through Nature's Bond. It will make all Farms in the range of the Harvester create thorns, with their statistics being half of the Harvester's thorns statistics at Level 0, becoming stronger with Levels. Placing down Farms where their range covers the path while also being in the Harvester's range can significantly increase how much damage its Thorns ability deals. The Farm can also be used to generate cash to help afford the Harvester's high upgrade costs. Range Buffs from towers like the DJ Booth can be useful at allowing the Harvester to have more Farms in its range and to boost their damage.

Towers that apply the Damage Buff, such as the DJ Booth or Mercenary Base can be quite useful with the Harvester, as they can not only boost its main attack but also the damage of its Thorns. However, do note that the Farms are only affected if the Farm itself is in the range of the Damage Buff giver.

Description: The Snowballer is an exclusive offensive support tower that could have been obtained by triumphing Outpost 32 on the Easy difficulty. It could be obtained via a gamepass for 249 Robux.

The Snowballer throws snowballs at enemies, dealing splash damage to them. These snowballs also apply chillness, which slows them down. At Level 3, it can also freeze enemies for a few seconds after reaching max chillness. These snowballs are explosive, dealing damage to multiple enemies in the explosion. These enemies receive damage based on their distance from the center of the explosion. The further away they are, the less damage they receive. Additionally, this also grants it the ability to bypass enemy defense. The Snowballer can damage Lead enemies from Level 0 and detect Flying enemies on Level 3.
The Snowballer is mainly considered to be an early-game tower due to its low cost and low DPS, however it can provide decent stalling later on during the game.
Strategy: The Snowballer's DPS makes it only reliable as an offensive tower in the early game, though even there it can struggle in harder modes like Hardcore mode and special modes. This means that it is mostly a support tower used to slow down enemies in harder modes, though it can be used as an early-game tower in easier modes quite well. If you want to use the Snowballer for early game, it is best to try get it to Level 3 as fast as possible, since it will be able to damage more enemies per attack as well as freeze enemies.

Do note, however, that the Snowballer can only hit up to 2 enemies at Level 0-2, making it worse against crowds in comparison to other freezing towers like the Cryomancer or Frost Blaster. However, it is very cheap to fully upgrade the Snowballer, where it can hit up to four enemies, which makes it a good option for handling weaker crowds that are not immune to freeze.

elementalist.name: Elementalist
elementalist.description: The Elementalist is an exclusive tower that could have been obtained by triumphing Outpost 32 from the Operation I.C.E Event on the Hard difficulty. It is mainly an offensive tower with some support capabilities, mainly in the form of freezing enemies. It could be bought through a limited time gamepass for 799 Robux.

Description: The Elementalist is an exclusive tower that could have been obtained by triumphing Outpost 32 from the Operation I.C.E Event on the Hard difficulty. It is mainly an offensive tower with some support capabilities, mainly in the form of freezing enemies. It could be bought through a limited time gamepass for 799 Robux.

The Elementalist fires in bursts. The displayed firerate in-game is the time between a burst ending and another burst starting, while the actual time between shots during a burst is a separate statistic. It has two modes which it can switch between, fire and frost. Fire makes it set enemies on fire with each hit, making them receive additional burn damage, while frost applies chillness to enemies, slowing them down. At Level 2, it also gains two abilities, both of which can only be used with their respective modes active and have separate cooldowns, allowing players to quickly switch modes and utilize both abilities. The first is Heatwave, which creates a heatwave in its range, dealing damage to enemies, applying burn to them and knocking them back. The second is Ice Turret, which allows it to create an Ice Turret in its range. It is a stationary unit with limited lifespan that deals damage to enemies, applying chillness to them while also being able to freeze them. There is a 5 second cooldown before modes can be changed.
The Elementalist has a placement limit of 5 per player.
Abilities: Creates a shockwave, which deals damage to enemies, knocks them back and sets them on fire.
Creates an Ice Turret in the selected spot, which chills and freezes enemies.
Strategy: The Elementalist can be quite effective at taking down single, high health enemies, due to its high DPS and its frost mode slowing them down, giving it more time to damage them. Its Ice Turrets can also help, as they provide additional DPS and allow it to deal even more damage to these enemies.
Its Ice Turrets can also help, as they provide additional DPS and allow it to deal even more damage to these enemies.

The Elementalist can clear out hordes of weaker enemies with ease, as its Heatwave ability allows it to deal a lot of damage to hordes. The Elementalist itself can also be used by having it apply its burn to multiple enemies, most easily by setting it to Random, though its burn effect is weaker than the one from Heatwave.
The Elementalist itself can also be used by having it apply its burn to multiple enemies, most easily by setting it to Random, though its burn effect is weaker than the one from Heatwave.

As each enemy can only have burn applied once, it may be more beneficial to have only one Elementalist set to fire and the others set to frost, with others only being set to fire to use its Heatwave ability.

While the Ice Turrets created by the Elementalist may appear to have infinite health due to their lack of a health bar, this is not the case. It does have health, meaning it can be killed by abilities, though its health is quite large. While the Boomer cannot kill it with its 400 damage explosion, the Brute can with its 1,000 damage Smash.
While the Boomer cannot kill it with its 400 damage explosion, the Brute can with its 1,000 damage Smash.
Unlike most other stalling towers, the Elementalist has hidden detection, making it great against enemies like Shadow Bosses or other high health enemies.

The Elementalist lacks any lead or flying detection, but it does have other ways to damage these enemies. Elementalist set to Fire can directly hurt any Lead enemies through burn damage. Elementalist can damage and set fire to Flying enemies through Heatwave, however they do not take knockback. This should not be relied on as the Heatwave's 40 second cooldown makes it inconsistent.
Elementalist set to Fire can directly hurt any Lead enemies through burn damage.
Elementalist can damage and set fire to Flying enemies through Heatwave, however they do not take knockback. This should not be relied on as the Heatwave's 40 second cooldown makes it inconsistent.
This should not be relied on as the Heatwave's 40 second cooldown makes it inconsistent.
When using frost mode, selecting Strongest can help stall high health enemies. This is greater when using Ice Turret as it can freeze the enemy if it doesn't have Freeze Immunity.
This is greater when using Ice Turret as it can freeze the enemy if it doesn't have Freeze Immunity.
The Elementalist is incapable of dropping Defense with its frost or fire mode and other towers like Freezer and Pyromancer should be used to drop them instead.
The Elementalist can only inflict slowdown onto enemies and cannot freeze enemies on its own, only the Ice Turrets are capable of freezing.

Unlike the Engineer 's sentries, Ice Turrets have to be built somewhere within the Elementalist's range manually using the Ice Turret ability and only one Ice Turret per Elementalist can be active at a time. The Ice Turret requires to be built in empty spaces with no towers, but towers and other Ice Turrets can be placed on top of them once they are built. As Ice Turrets have to be replaced regularly, it is best to communicate with your team to leave an empty space in Elementalist's range for optimal Ice Turret placements.

firework_technician.name: Firework Technician
firework_technician.description: The Firework Technician is a support based tower that can only be obtained from completing a specific Mission Quest. Either the 🇺🇸 Rise for the Pledge! or Happy New Years! quests must be completed to get the Firework Technician, either of which costs 650 Coins to start. Currently, the 🇺🇸 Rise for the Pledge! quest can be started.

Description: The Firework Technician is a support based tower that can only be obtained from completing a specific Mission Quest. Either the 🇺🇸 Rise for the Pledge! or Happy New Years! quests must be completed to get the Firework Technician, either of which costs 650 Coins to start. Currently, the 🇺🇸 Rise for the Pledge! quest can be started.

At the beginning of each wave, Firework Technician grants all 3 detections; hidden, lead and flying, for a few seconds to all towers within its range, with the duration depending on the level. Additionally, all towers in its range at all times will have a chance to fire out a firework. The chance depends on the tower's firerate and the Firework Technician's firework shot percentage cap. At base, it is set to 0.5 which is a maximum chance of 50% and at Level 4 it is set to 1, a maximum chance of 100%. The maximum chances however, are quite unlikely to actually ever be reached outside of Sandbox mode, where the tower's firerate can be set to high numbers. Fireworks are fired out on impact, which is when enemy receives damage from the tower's main attack. If a tower can hit multiple enemies, in most cases this means each enemy damaged will have a chance to make the tower generate a firework. For example, the Rocketeer will generate one for each missile, the Necromancer will generate one for each enemy hit by its projectile or each one of its beams, and the Hallow Punk has a chance to generate an infinite number of fireworks as each enemy damaged by its explosion has a chance to generate one. Not all towers can generate fireworks and units are completely unable to generate them. These fireworks will be fired out at the hit enemy which generated the firework and deal their own firework damage. While stated to be additional damage, the damage from them is not added to the tower's damage, it is instead just its base damage. Fireworks will create explosions which deal damage to enemies hit, bypassing defense, dealing damage to Lead enemies and being boostable by Damage Buffs, these explosions have no damage drop off, and will also set the enemies on fire, dealing additional burn damage. The chance of a firework being fired is calculated as:
Firework Shot Chance Cap 1 + 2.71 8 (− 0.5 × (F i r e r a t e − 6))

Where Firework Shot Chance Cap is taken from the Firework Technician, and Firerate is taken from the tower that fires out the firework. Firerate in this case is the statistic displayed with the hourglass to the right of the tower. In most cases, this is the firerate statistic (the time between each shot), though in some cases it may be the burst cooldown (time between bursts), like the Elementalist, the spawnrate, like the Military Base or just unrelated to any statistic it has, such as the Trapper. This means towers with a slower firerate have a greater chance to fire a firework. The firerate is not calculated with the Firerate Bug.
The Firework Technician has a placement limit of one per player.
Strategy: The Firework Technician's range is quite small, so it is recommended to use Range Buffs from the DJ Booth or alternatively, using the Range Flag consumable with it. The DJ Booth can also be useful to boost its damage, as its fireworks are affected by Damage Buffs. Furthermore, DJ Booth may also be used to reduce its upgrade costs as they are quite expensive. Do note that the Firework Technician itself needs to be within the range of the Damage Buff giver, not the tower that the firework is being fired from.

The DJ Booth can also be useful to boost its damage, as its fireworks are affected by Damage Buffs. Furthermore, DJ Booth may also be used to reduce its upgrade costs as they are quite expensive. As the Firework Technician has a placement limit of only one, its placement should be strategized for optimal effect on nearby towers. Multiple Firework Technicians can be brought into a match, though do note that their effects will not stack. For example, a tower with the firerate of 100, which is in range of 100 Firework Technicians, will only fire one firework instead of 100, despite having a guaranteed chance to do so. You can also use the Hacker 's Hologram Tower ability to clone more Firework Technicians, but this can be costly.

It is recommended to pair it with low firerate towers such as the Minigunner or area of effect towers such as the Rocketeer in order to fully optimize and maximize the firework shots. While towers with higher firerate do have better chances than towers with lower firerate, they are still not nearly as optimal. For example, a tower with a firerate of 0.1 in range of a Level 4 Firework Technician will have a chance of around ~4.98% to fire a firework, while a tower with a firerate of 1 will have a chance of around ~7.59%. A tower with a firerate of 0.1 will be more likely to fire out a single firework in the time it takes the tower with firerate of 1 to fire a single shot. It should still be noted that towers with an exceptionally high firerate, such as the Level 4 Ranger, have a significantly higher chance of generating a firework per shot. However, unless a tower's firerate exceeds around 12 with a Level 4 Firework Technician (where there is over a 95% chance of generating a firework), this is not guaranteed.

Multiple towers which hit many enemies at a time will have a chance to generate a firework for each enemy hit. Because of this, towers like the Hallow Punk, Cryomancer, Electroshocker or Rocketeer can generate multiple fireworks at once, and in general have a higher chance of generating at least one firework. This increases their DPS exponentially, so it is recommended to place a Firework Technician near these towers or vice versa. Do note that not all towers are capable generating it. A full list of towers that can generate fireworks is shown at the end of this section.

The Firework Technician's ability to provide towers with all detections is very useful. While it is only temporary and its effects only take hold at the start of each wave, it can still prove great for towers like the Swarmer and Ranger, with the provided detections greatly increasing its effectiveness against enemies of specific Attributes. This makes it especially useful in modes which feature all three detections, though due to its rather low duration it is not the best option.

biologist.name: Biologist
biologist.description: The Biologist is an exclusive tower that creates plants around itself. It could have been obtained from beating Bathroom Approach in the Hard difficulty. It can be obtained via a limited-time gamepass for 849 Robux.

Description: The Biologist is an exclusive tower that creates plants around itself. It could have been obtained from beating Bathroom Approach in the Hard difficulty. It can be obtained via a limited-time gamepass for 849 Robux.

The tower itself does not attack, as it only has three statistics: range, deadzone range and firerate. All of these statistics are only used by its ability to place down various plants, which is how it deals damage. The plants will only be placed down in its range, but not its deadzone range. As it has a firerate of 1, it means it can only place down one plant every second. It can deploy three types of plants, these being the Sunflower, Ivy (Level 1+) and Nightshade (Level 3+).
Sunflower is the most basic plant, as it targets a single enemy and deals damage to it. At Level 2+, it can additionally detect Hidden enemies.

Ivy deals energy damage with an AOE effect, applying poison to enemies. The poison deals damage over time and slightly slows down enemies. It can also damage Lead enemies with its explosion and poison.

Nightshade is similar to the Sunflower, as it also deals damage to a single target. However, it fires far slower, deals more damage and applies confusion to enemies. It can also detect Flying enemies.
The Biologist has a placement limit of eight per player.
Skins: To see all the upgrades of a skin, see the gallery page.
Strategy: The Biologist is extremely versatile, having a good damage output and a cheap price, making it an excellent choice for early game while also being a solid sub-DPS/support in the mid to late game. It is also a good option for Hardcore since its units has all forms of detection. Do note that enemies with two or more enemy types that require detections, such as the Lead Balloon, will be immune to the damage from its units.

It is also a good option for Hardcore since its units has all forms of detection. Do note that enemies with two or more enemy types that require detections, such as the Lead Balloon, will be immune to the damage from its units.

The Sunflower has the highest DPS out of all the plants, making it great against single enemies. It is also the only plant with hidden detection, meaning that this plant should be used when they spawn. It offers the best cost efficiency out of all the plants, making it highly effective to place multiple Sunflowers.

The Ivy can be great against hordes of enemies, due to its attack dealing damage in an area. Unlike most other explosions, this one does not bypass defense. Any enemy hit by it also has poison applied to it, which deals damage over time and slightly slows it down. This makes it useful at stalling enemies, though the slowdown is quite low. This effect is the same as the one applied by the Toxic Gunner, though it has different statistics. In case of both towers applying poison, Toxic Gunner 's effect will take priority. Both the explosion and its poison can damage Lead enemies, making the Ivy useful against such enemies.

The Nightshade, similarly to the Sunflower, targets a single enemy and deals damage to them, though unlike it, the Nightshade also confuses them, allowing them to stall the enemies while damaging them. Because of this, the Nightshade will deal less DPS than the Sunflower, but it will gain more time to damage enemies because of its confusion, alongside its massive range. Confusion can only be applied by Nightshade every four seconds. Additionally, it will not apply it if any confusion cooldown is active, even one from other towers such as the Jester. This also applies to other towers. If the Nightshade 's confusion effect ends, a Jester will be unable to apply confusion to that enemy.

Most buffs work on the Biologist. However, most of them are insignificant as none of them are applied to units which are its method of attacking enemies. Because of this, towers which debuff the enemies such as the Electroshocker, Freezer or Warden are recommended to use alongside the Biologist, as they can make its plants deal more damage or give them more time to kill them. The DJ Booth 's discount buff is quite helpful since the tower itself has expensive upgrades. Damage Buffs given by DJ Booth and Mercenary Base are completely useless as the effects does not apply to the units. The Firerate Buff and debuff can alter the minimal time between each plant being created. This, however, only has an impact in cases where plants have very similar timers.

warlock.description: The Warlock is a melee and ranged hybrid ground tower that could have been unlocked by triumphing Outpost 16, Banlands and Blind Faith on the Hard difficulty of the Null & Void Event. It can be obtained via a limited-time gamepass for 849 Robux.

Description: The Warlock is a melee and ranged hybrid ground tower that could have been unlocked by triumphing Outpost 16, Banlands and Blind Faith on the Hard difficulty of the Null & Void Event. It can be obtained via a limited-time gamepass for 849 Robux.

The Warlock has two range rings, each allows it to attack in a specific mode, each with its own statistics. The bigger range ring is the ranged attack range. With it, the Warlock fires energy beams at enemies. This deals damage to a single enemy, while also knocking it back at later levels. There is a 3 second cooldown before an enemy can be knocked back again.

The second red range ring is the melee range. In it, the Warlock will attack enemies with its sword. This will deal AOE damage, with the intended target receiving both the melee and ranged damage, while anything hit alongside it only receives the ranged damage. This also applies bleed to enemies. If there are enemies in both its ranged and melee ranges, it will prioritize attacking enemies in its melee range.

At Level 4, it gains the ability to apply bleed to enemies. Each bleed applied will only deal damage to an enemy once before disappearing, with there also being a 1.8 second delay between each bleed damage. Additionally, it can only deal damage while bleed is not being applied. This bleed can stack up to 40 times, which will cause a bleed collapse, dealing increased damage to the enemy instantly. The damage dealt varies based on an enemy's max health and the Warlock's base bleed damage, EV (exponential value) and how many bleed stacks are removed at once. Because of this, when the enemy receives bleed damage from the enemy over time, it is calculated as: (Base Bleed Damage × (1 0.9)) × (Enemy Max Health EV) While bleed is collapsing on an enemy, it is calculated as: (Base Bleed Damage × (4 0 0.9)) × (Enemy Max Health EV)

Damage from bleed is always rounded up, for both damage over time and from bleed collapse. Additionally, damage from bleed damage will not be displayed as the full damage dealt for the Warlock unless only one Warlock was applying bleed. Damage displayed will be based on the number of bleed stacks applied by the selected Warlock. This damage is not affected by Damage Buffs.

The Warlock can be considered a mid to late-game tower as its fairly effective during the mid and late game due to its high DPS, and its bleed effect that can affect every enemy, including major bosses.
The Warlock has a placement limit of four per player.
Strategy: The Warlock is an excellent option against high health enemies, due to its high DPS and bleed. Generally, it is preferred that the Warlock deals damage to such enemies in its melee range, as it has far higher DPS and AOE. It is entirely possible to use it while not taking advantage of its melee range as it does have quite high DPS without it, though this is not generally recommended. The knockback from the ranged attack can be helpful for keeping enemies within melee range. However, this is not always reliable as the Warlock prioritizes melee range and, due to various immunities related to knockback, prevents it from occurring consistently.

The Warlock will prioritize attacking enemies in the melee range, regardless of its targeting. For example, if set to Last Enemy and there are enemies in both its melee and ranged range, it will only target the last enemy in its melee range, ignoring all enemies in the ranged range. This can be beneficial in certain situations, such as allowing it to ignore Aggro or target specific enemies that you want it to target. However, it can also lead to scenarios where a Warlock's target escapes its melee range while other enemies remain in range, leaving a potentially strong enemy with nothing to defeat it. Because of this, other towers should be taken to help with anything that gets past the Warlock's range as it will quite often be unable to actually deal with it itself

The names of most of the tower upgrades likely reference different features from the tabletop game Dungeons and Dragons: While not a direct reference, Level 1 may be related to the Acolyte background, a feature that grants the Magic Initiate (Cleric) origin feat to any Dungeons and Dragons character. Level 3 references Pact of the Blade, a subfeature of a class feature from the original Dungeons and Dragons Warlock called Eldritch Invocations. The feature evolves around the use of a Pact Weapon, further reinforcing the reference to the large sword the tower is carrying. Level 4 references the Eldritch Knight, a subclass of the original Dungeons and Dragons Fighter that grants spellcasting to the purely martial class.

spotlight_tech.name: Spotlight Tech
spotlight_tech.description: The Spotlight Tech is a cliff tower which uses a spotlight beam to burn and confuse enemies, while also revealing Hidden enemies.

Description: The Spotlight Tech is a cliff tower which uses a spotlight beam to burn and confuse enemies, while also revealing Hidden enemies.

It attacks enemies using a spotlight, which damages enemies with its bright light ray. This light ray takes some time to move from one target to another. This light ray has a specific radius in which it damage enemies. It will damage an infinite number of enemies, though enemies will receive less damage the further they are from the center. Depending on the distance, they will either receive 100% of the stated, 60% or 35%. This spotlight can also apply one of the following effects based on the level:
Starting from Level 1, it will apply burn to enemies. This will deal additional damage over time, even if they are not currently in the spotlight's light ray.

Starting from Level 2, it will start to reveal Hidden enemies by applying Exposed to them. This lets towers without hidden detection to target them. If the enemy gets out of the spotlight, it will lose Exposed, meaning towers need hidden detection for it again.
At Level 4, it can confuse enemies. This happens once it deals 1,800 damage to enemies, after which it will confuse all enemies currently in its spotlight.
The Spotlight Tech has a placement limit of one. It can detect Flying enemies from Level 0, Lead enemies from Level 1 and Hidden enemies from Level 2.
Strategy: The Spotlight Tech can be an effective AOE tower, due to it dealing damage to an infinite number of enemies and applying burn. Setting the Spotlight Tech to Random allows it to apply burn to nearly every enemy on the map, potentially increasing the maximum damage output to a far larger extent. Stalling towers like the Toxic Gunner, Freezer or Electroshocker can be used to clump up enemies in one spot, allowing the Spotlight Tech to hit more enemies with its spotlight.

Stalling towers like the Toxic Gunner, Freezer or Electroshocker can be used to clump up enemies in one spot, allowing the Spotlight Tech to hit more enemies with its spotlight.

Starting from Level 2, the Spotlight Tech has the ability to reveal Hidden enemy in its spotlight diameter. This makes it useful alongside towers that do not have hidden detection, like the Ranger, top path Pursuit or Swarmer.

At Level 4, the Spotlight Tech will begin to confuse enemies once it reaches 1,800 total damage. Only damage from the spotlight boosts it. Any damage from burn will not contribute to the threshold, meaning the best method of activating it is having as many enemies in its spotlight as possible.

Trivia: The Spotlight Tech is based on the Spotlights that appeared during the Lunar Overture Event and The Final Act Event. Additionally Spotlight Tech is inspired by theatrical technicians called spotlight operators, hence the name.

The Spotlight Tech is the first exclusive cliff tower.
The Spotlight Tech is regarded as the Spotlight Technician in the game's description, and the update log in both the Discord server and in-game.
The Spotlight Tech is currently the only tower in the game to have two upgrades with the same name (Levels 1 and 3 both share the name Backstage Crew).

war_machine.name: War Machine
war_machine.description: The War Machine is currently a tower exclusive to anyone who is a moderator or a higher special role in the Tower Defense Simulator Discord server. It is also rewarded to people who contribute to the game, with the primary way of achieving that being reaching 15 contributions in the game, followed by a review by a lead developer.

Description: The War Machine is currently a tower exclusive to anyone who is a moderator or a higher special role in the Tower Defense Simulator Discord server. It is also rewarded to people who contribute to the game, with the primary way of achieving that being reaching 15 contributions in the game, followed by a review by a lead developer.

The War Machine uses an exoskeleton with two miniguns. At Level 2, the exoskeleton also has a missile launcher, allowing it to fire Stark Missiles. At Level 2, it also gains the ability to apply various buffs to towers in its range through its Command Aura.
The War Machine has a placement limit of 5 per player.
Ability: Deploys a convoy of Railgun Tanks at the exit. The number of units spawned depends on the Level.
Strategy: The War Machine can be a powerful DPS tower mid to late game, dealing close to 1,000 DPS.

At Level 2, the War Machine gains a missile launcher, which gains more missiles and stronger stats with upgrades, which is quite decent against hordes of enemies, such as the Fallen Hazmat. Because the missile launcher deals splash damage, the War Machine can also damage Lead enemies with it, making it very useful against the Lead and Elite Leads early on.
Because the missile launcher deals splash damage, the War Machine can also damage Lead enemies with it, making it very useful against the Lead and Elite Leads early on.

At Level 4, the War Machine gets hidden detection and at Level 5, it gets flying detection, making it a very versatile tower by the mid to late game combined with its high DPS and splash capabilities. Although it cannot damage them with its main attack, its missiles and the Railgun Tank collision and explosion damage can also damage Lead enemies. However, because of how expensive it is to upgrade to Level 4 and 5, it should not be solely relied upon to attack enemies with these attributes.
Although it cannot damage them with its main attack, its missiles and the Railgun Tank collision and explosion damage can also damage Lead enemies.
However, because of how expensive it is to upgrade to Level 4 and 5, it should not be solely relied upon to attack enemies with these attributes.
At Level 5, it gains the Freeze Immunity, making it useful against enemies that mainly freeze towers.
Trivia: The War Machine's appearance and some of its mechanics appear to have been based on an Exoskeleton tower suggestion from the Tower Defense Simulator Discord server. However, the name of the War Machine and its Stark Missile are references to the War Machine from Marvel.
However, the name of the War Machine and its Stark Missile are references to the War Machine from Marvel.
The War Machine's Level 5 Command Aura description is a reference to its first description, which in turn was a reference to Risk of Rain 2, specifically the Commando 's old ending phrase.
The War Machine had the most expensive upgrade cost in the game, until Gatling Gun was added.
After the Overhaul Update, the War Machine gained 12 damage on Level 2, giving it 13 damage, thus giving it an absurd 104 DPS for just $2,900. This was later fixed in May 2021.

Description: The Mecha Base is currently a tower exclusive to anyone who is an administrator or higher in the Tower Defense Simulator Discord server, though on rare occasions it has been given to other people. It is planned to become an evolved version of the Military Base in the fourth quarter of 2026. It spawns futuristic units which can attack enemies as it moves. Each vehicle spawns at the end of the path, with regular intervals between each spawn. It heads towards the start of the path until it is destroyed. If it reaches the start of the map, it will naturally be destroyed.

The Mecha Base spawns several mechanized walkers called Marks that upgrade in stats depending on the level of the Mecha Base. The units can shoot bullets from afar, and upgraded variations can also shoot missiles which deal splash damage.
The Mecha Base has a placement limit of 3 per player.
Strategy: The Mecha Base is extremely useful for large maps, like Tropical Isles and Polluted Wasteland II, due to its units having long range. It is not as effective on shorter maps like Dead Ahead, but still remains highly impactful due to its high ram damage and relatively low spawnrate. In maps with multiple paths, only one unit spawns as opposed to two. This unit will go down a random path.

mine.description: The Mine was an unreleased tower that was only shown in a poll.

Description: The Mine was an unreleased tower that was only shown in a poll.

As it was never added to the game, its statistics are not known and likely were never made. However, its mechanics are known. Similarly to the Farm, it would be an income generating tower and the second tower to be primarily focused on money generation. To differentiate itself from the Farm, rather than generating income at the beginning of the wave, it would generate it over time.

The Mine although polled, was never added. It lost to the Medic, who had the highest number of votes and also the Shredder who had the second highest vote count. While the other two ended up getting added, the Mine was not.

tooltips: Mine was only shown off in a poll. Because of this, not all information on the item in question is known and certain information may not be entirely accurate. Additionally, whenever it will be added in the future is not always clear.

Description: The Sentry was a tower with a unique spool-up mechanic. It could have been purchased for 3,650 Coins from the store prior to the 24th of December 2019. Those who bought the Sentry can no longer use it, as it has been removed after the Overhaul Update.

When the Sentry locked onto a target, it would start to spool-up until its firerate was half its original firerate without the Firerate Bug, though due to the Firerate Bug, this would not be the case. For example: At Level 5 the firerate was meant to be 0.2 minimum and capped at 0.1 maximum, however due to the Firerate Bug, they were effectively increased to about 0.25 minimum and 0.15 maximum firerate. The spool-up would last about 5 seconds.

The Sentry also had a noticeable delay when switching between targets, making it a very situational tower. And while it could still shred through single targets, this delay rendered it terrible against hordes, making it most effective against bosses.
Strategy: To make better use of the Sentry's spool-up, consider changing its target to Strongest. However, be aware if two enemies have similar health to each other, the Sentry will continuously swap between attacking these two enemies. This will reduce the damage output of the Sentry due to the delay between switching targets. The same issue occurs with if targeting is set to First. The Sentry will swap targets if the initial target is overtaken. For this reason, the Sentry is fairly weak against the Necromancer. Consider using the Rocketeer or Demoman alongside the Sentry to reduce the amount of enemies that the Sentry can target.

If the Sentry gets stunned by enemies, the spool-up will reset. You can place the Sentry further away from the path to reduce the chances of this happening.

The Sentry fires faster as long as its target is within range. You can extend the time an enemy is in range with a Pyromancer, Freezer and Electroshocker, so long the specific enemy is not immune to their effects.

The Sentry will have difficulty attacking fast enemies, such as the Error, without a supporting tower. This is due to the delay when switching between targets.
This is due to the delay when switching between targets.

The Sentry is most effective against the major bosses due to their high health and slow speed. Be aware that most major bosses will be able to stun the Sentry, resetting the spool-up. The boss may also spawn enemies, which will distract the Sentry away from the boss. You can set the Sentry's targeting to Strongest to prevent this.

The Commander is recommended with the Sentry as it reduces spool-up time as well as minimum firerate.
Trivia: The Sentry made a small beep when its target moved out of range or was killed. The Sentry also made the same sound when stunned.
The Sentry also made the same sound when stunned.
The Sentry was loosely based on a multitude of games including Risk of Rain 2 and Team Fortress 2. The Sentry design was based on Team Fortress 2's Sentry Gun.
The Sentry design was based on Team Fortress 2's Sentry Gun.

The Sentry was the first tower to rely on RNG for an upgrade. The Sentry used to have a 30% chance to receive a teddy bear at Level 5, which gave it hidden detection. After 5 August 2019, however, this did not affect anything statistics-wise as the Sentry could now always detect hidden enemies at Level 5. The Teddy Bear on top of the Sentry was the Teddy Bloxpin from the Roblox catalog.

This was the only tower to make use of the spool-up mechanic. This was the first tower to have the lock-on mechanic, in which it would target the enemy it first attacked until it was dead or moved out of range, even if other enemies overtook it or had more health than it. This was removed in the MEGA Update.

The Sentry was likely made unobtainable, and later removed, most likely due to the multitude of bugs the Sentry encountered. There was a firerate issue with the Sentry where its minimum firerate was not half of the maximum firerate. This issue was resolved with a Commander as the minimum firerate is as expected, with Firerate Buff applied. The lock-on mechanic does not work. For this reason, the Sentry constantly changes targets whenever another suitable enemy enters its range. The displayed firerate for this tower was a leading decimal when spooling-up. Even at minimum firerate, the number displayed was a leading decimal and was not a terminating decimal.

Description: The Twitgunner was an unreleased tower added in the Overhaul Update.

It also has a tweet animation where it pulls out a phone and makes a tweet, though the exact purpose of this is not known.
Strategy: Due to its cheap cost and DPS, this tower would mostly end up being a better Scout for early-game.

Some of the tower textures, like the phone used while it would tweet were made in August of 2019, meaning they are most likely reused textued from the Clout God.

void_miner.name: Void Miner
void_miner.description: The Void Miner was an exclusive tower mostly gotten by developers of the game and, at the time, testers of the game.

Description: The Void Miner was an exclusive tower mostly gotten by developers of the game and, at the time, testers of the game.

The Void Miner worked similarly to the Farm. At the end of each wave, it would generate a specific number of corruption. This was added to a corruption counter that appeared on the tower itself. Upon reaching 2,000 corruption generated, the Hidden Wave would be guaranteed to happen, even if the requirements were not met, allowing for it to be triggered outside of Fallen mode. If 2,000 corruption were not generated, nothing would happen, as corruption had no other purpose.
Strategy: It is recommended to place Void Miner early on in a match so it can acquire as much Corruption as possible.
Trivia: The Void Miner that got into the game is very different from its initial concept. The corruption generated by it originally was not meant for activating Hidden Wave. Instead, it would be used as a currency to unlock additional upgrades for towers. It would have been obtained by beating the Hidden Wave. At some point, the Void Miner was redesigned to be used for activating the Hidden Wave, added to the game as an exclusive tower, and then scrapped, leading to its removal in the Overhaul Update.

combatant.name: Combatant
combatant.description: The Combatant or Brawler was an unused tower from 2021 that was originally meant to be a starter tower and the replacement for the Paintballer. It is effectively an early version of the Brawler. This tower appears to have two names, Combatant and Brawler, both with slightly different statistics and appearance. The Brawler was used in the Main Lobby while the Combatant was used in matches. To differentiate it from the current Brawler, the tower will be referred to as the Combatant, and anything specific to the Brawler will be referred to as such.

Description: The Combatant or Brawler was an unused tower from 2021 that was originally meant to be a starter tower and the replacement for the Paintballer. It is effectively an early version of the Brawler. This tower appears to have two names, Combatant and Brawler, both with slightly different statistics and appearance. The Brawler was used in the Main Lobby while the Combatant was used in matches. To differentiate it from the current Brawler, the tower will be referred to as the Combatant, and anything specific to the Brawler will be referred to as such.

The Combatant would punch enemies with its fists, dealing damage to them. Its statistics were mostly copied from the Gladiator, with even the ability being carried over, though that most likely did nothing. The Combatant version specifically also has a sound and particles for crits, suggesting it could or was planned to make crits, though it is unclear if these ever worked. The crit effects are not present on the Brawler.
Ability: Ability carried over from the Gladiator as its statistics were copied for the Combatant. If this did anything is unknown, though it likely had no function.
Strategy: As the Combatant reuses the Gladiator 's statistics, it ends up mostly being an early-game tower.

crystallizer.name: Crystallizer
crystallizer.description: The Crystallizer was an unreleased tower that was developed in 2022 that would be the Polluted Wasteland II reward tower. It was originally meant to be added as part of a second part to the update that added Polluted Wasteland II. Alongside it, a Polluted Wasteland II equivalent of the Hidden Wave would be added to it. It was never properly finished.

Description: The Crystallizer was an unreleased tower that was developed in 2022 that would be the Polluted Wasteland II reward tower. It was originally meant to be added as part of a second part to the update that added Polluted Wasteland II. Alongside it, a Polluted Wasteland II equivalent of the Hidden Wave would be added to it. It was never properly finished.

The Crystallizer was a structure that could be placed on the ground. Once placed, it would spit out balls of acid onto the path, which would leave acidic crystals on the path which would be used to damage enemies. This means it was effectively a toxic based Trapper. With upgrades, the crystals would gain the ability to make enemies vulnerable for a few seconds, presumably making them receive more damage.
Despite its similarities to the Trapper, the Crystallizer was a late-game oriented tower.
Trivia: Initial pitches for the tower supposedly also used different names for it like Nuclear Silo.
